## Session 61 — DISCIPLINE, Effect A: the make-% shave SHIPPED (v1) — a disciplined defender now shaves a flat, small, absolute slice off his man's make%, everywhere on the floor. The audit corrected the premise the session was designed on: Discipline was never "near-dead" — it was quiet on the WRONG meter. And the "fouls committed" half of the spec turned out to be a foundation piece, deferred to its own session. (2026-07-16)

**Register:** a build session, wiring-first (Emmett's S60.2 ruling — "mess with the missing wiring a bit first, then calibration"). Scope walled to Discipline. **Effect A (make shave) SHIPPED; Effect B (fouls) deferred as a foundation build — see the ruling below.**

**THE MEASUREMENT GATE CORRECTED THE PREMISE (Discipline is quiet, not dead — but only half the spec was ever unbuilt).** The design conversation was held believing Discipline is near-dead/disconnected. The audit against live source + a real run found that half true:
- **The foul wire is LIVE, not dead.** `Matchup.FoulRate` reads `defender.Discipline` at one site (`Core/Matchup.cs:423`), called from exactly one caller (`RollHGenerator.cs:601`, the shooting-foul door). A 0→99 Discipline walk (oracle, live config) moves the shooting-foul RATE **~5% relative against an average foul-drawer, up to ~37% against a foul-magnet** — the door is a two-sided drawing-vs-restraint contest, so the swing depends on where the shooter's FoulDrawing already sits on the tanh curve. The S53/S54 "FTA 3.7→3.6, near-inert" read was measuring the wrong meter twice over: FTA is *shooting fouls only*, and against a flat-50 shooter the swing is small on an already-small base. **Quiet by tuning (`DefenseFoulWeight` 0.2), not absent.**
- **Discipline touches make% NOWHERE (confirmed clean).** Grep of `Matchup.cs`, `RollHGenerator.cs`, `EffectiveRating`, and the Roll G defensive blend — the only gameplay read of Discipline is the FoulRate contest. `DefenseRating` blends PerimeterDefense/PostDefense/RimProtection only. **So the make shave is genuinely unbuilt, and 50 is a clean neutral point (the make-curve bakes in an average defender, not Discipline).**

**THE §2 FORK — THE NUMBER THAT DROVE THE RULING (real 5,205-game season).** Emmett's spec is "fouls committed." Defensive fouls split:

| category | share of def fouls | per team-game |
|---|---|---|
| **shooting** (where Discipline is wired) | **35%** | 6.5 |
| **non-shooting** — reach-ins, off-ball grabs (Discipline reads nothing) | **65%** | 12.1 |

65% of the fouls a disciplined player actually avoids live in the door Discipline can't touch. **Fork (a) — tune the shooting door only — can technically reach a 10-15% total-fouls swing, but only by raising `DefenseFoulWeight` from 0.2 to ~0.6-0.8 (up to EQUAL with the offense's 0.8 foul-drawing weight)**, which abandons the deliberate offense-dominant contest, leaves the effect lopsided by matchup, and inflates how much a 0-Discipline defender fouls on shots (playability risk from the other side). So the honest read forces fork (b): reach the non-shooting door.

**EMMETT'S RULING — non-shooting fouls must EVENTUALLY be attributed to an individual, so build toward that (2026-07-16).** This ruled OUT the quick fork-(b) team-blend. The structural finding: non-shooting fouls are authored as a **team** rate in Roll B's Foul slice (reads Hustle + physicality + pressure, no Discipline) and charged anonymously in Roll D, which explicitly does **not** attribute the foul to a man. A team-Discipline blend on Roll B would move the team total but put **no name on the foul** — torn out the moment per-man attribution lands. Not worth building. **So Effect B becomes its own session: a per-man non-shooting foul model where each defender generates his own reach-ins, his own Discipline gates the rate, and the foul carries his name — which delivers the per-man swing, the ~5× stacking, AND the attribution at once.** That is a foundation change to how non-shooting fouls are born (the "slow down and get it right" class), not a knob. **This session ships Effect A only** — clean, per-man, no architectural friction — and leaves the shooting-foul wire untouched at 0.2 (no point tuning the shooting door in isolation now and re-tuning the whole foul picture next session).

**EFFECT A — THE MAKE-% SHAVE (shipped).** A defender's own Discipline shaves his man's make% by a small, ABSOLUTE, FLAT-across-zones amount. `RollHGenerator.ApplyDisciplineShave` (a named static, mirroring `ApplyUsageRelief` — golden binds to the engine's own code, not a copy), ported constant-for-constant from `tools/discipline_shave_oracle.py`:

    progress = clamp((defenderDiscipline − 50) / 49, −1, +1)   // symmetric about the midpoint
    shave    = DisciplineMakeShaveScale × progress
    makePct  = clamp01(makePct × (1 − shave))

Seated beside the multiplicative usage siblings (volume tax, relief) after the C3 block. **SYMMETRIC about 50 (Emmett's ruling, off the archetype table):** a lockdown defender (99) shaves, an average defender (50) is neutral, a LIABILITY (0) gives up a cleaner look — because the make-curve already bakes in an average defender, 50 is the true neutral point, and it gives a 0-Discipline defender real teeth. **ABSOLUTE** — reads the defender's own Discipline, no shooter term (unlike the foul contest, which is and stays a two-sided contest). **FLAT across zones** — multiplicative, so the proportional reduction is constant everywhere (the signed invariant). At `DisciplineMakeShaveScale` = 0.015 a max-Discipline defender moves one shot ~1.5% relative (60% rim finisher → 59.1%, 34% shooter → 33.5%) — barely a game from one man; five of them shave ~1.5% off the whole other team, where a close one turns. Null defender (empty slot, DEC-6) → no shave (guarded). Kill switch at scale 0 → true identity branch, no arithmetic. Magnitude is a **PLACEHOLDER**, page-tuned later, never suite-asserted; Load-guarded to [0.0, 0.05] (a design ceiling on how much one defender's restraint may ever move a shot).

**ONE ENGINEERING CALL, FLAGGED — the knob went in RollHConfig, not MatchupConfig.** The prompt named `MatchupConfig`, but the shave's three make-chain siblings — `PressureVolumeTaxScale`, `UsageReliefBonusScale`, `IqMakeSensitivity` — all live in `RollHConfig` and are read via `_cfg` right where the shave seats. Matching them (so the shave reads the same way as the terms beside it) put `DisciplineMakeShaveScale` in RollHConfig / the config.json `RollH` block. The prompt's "read the nearest sibling" instruction won over its literal section name. Reversible if Emmett prefers Discipline's knobs centralized.

**ONE HONEST CATCH (caught in-sandbox, never reached Emmett's machine).** The first Phase 67 run FAILED three real-path sub-checks — all at **Mid**, all reading a ratio slightly off the pure 0.985 multiplier (Rim/Short/Long/Three read exactly 0.985000). Not an engine bug: C5.5 (screening +), C6 (HelpDefense −) and C7 (OffBallDefense −) are ADDITIVE terms *downstream* of the shave seat, and at Mid they fire via the 0.30 Mid multipliers while netting to zero at the other zones for all-50 players — an additive term downstream does not preserve a multiplicative ratio. A test-design flaw, fixed the way the usage-relief gravity test handles it: neutralize the downstream additive terms (Screening/HelpDefense/OffBallDefense → 0) so the live/kill ratio isolates the shave. Golden parity was exact from the first run; the shave itself was never wrong.

**Proven by the new Phase 67 check (all OK): golden parity 8 cases at 1e-12 (worst |Δ| = 0.0e0, constants cross-checked vs loaded RollHConfig first, identity rows bit-exact, boost-arm clamp row saturates); formula invariants (symmetric about 50, average defender neutral bit-identical on a live scale, monotone in Discipline, bounded by the scale ceiling, absolute); and through the REAL Roll H path — FLAT ACROSS ZONES (live/kill make ratio == (1−shave) = 0.985000 at every zone, worst dev 1.1e-16), exactly ONE shave (ratio is 1−shave, not (1−shave)²), ABSOLUTE (identical 0.985000 for weak/avg/elite shooters), null-defender bit-identical, COMPOSE (with relief + IQ both live the shave still lands its exact multiplier, non-clamping precondition held), kill switch bit-identical; config guards (negative and > 0.05 throw, 0 loads).** Middle-rung sandbox pre-check taken (SDK from the Ubuntu feed; oracle ALL OK before porting; compiled + full suite green in-sandbox). **Green on Emmett's machine: `ALL CHECKS PASSED`** — every Phase 67 line matched the sandbox (0.985000 flat, absolute identical, compose 0.985000). Season sanity: league FG% 45.7 → 45.4 (a small directional drop — disciplined defenses shave a hair off the league; magnitude is the placeholder, page-tuned later). Observation + stress runs green with the shave live.

**Full record:** design.md (the make-door make chain — new Session 61 Discipline-shave subsection, labelled the MAN-TO-MAN wire per the scheme ruling below; foul-door cross-reference), status.md (Effect A → Built; the scheme-toggle architecture ruling; the §2 fork ruling recorded), attribute-meaning.md (the Discipline finding rewritten — "near-dead" replaced with "was quiet on the wrong meter; now wired on two channels"), `tools/discipline_shave_oracle.py` + `tools/discipline_shave_golden.json`.

**SCHEME-TOGGLE ARCHITECTURE RULING (Emmett, 2026-07-16 — logged, not built).** The make-% shave routes through the man-to-man matchup like every defensive rating. When the zone/scheme layer lands, defensive scheme will **toggle distinct wiring sets** (man reads the matchup; zone reads areas/rotations) rather than one scheme-agnostic wire — so Discipline (and every defensive rating) gets a *per-scheme* implementation, and this wire is explicitly the **man-to-man** one. Labelled as such in design.md so a future session does not mistake it for the universal version. A real reshaping of what the parked scheme layer is.

**Next: Effect B — the per-man non-shooting foul model.** Each defender generates his own reach-in/off-ball fouls, his own Discipline gates the rate (absolute, per-man, non-compounding — five disciplined defenders drop the team total ~5× one, because each owns his own ~fifth of the opportunities, never five terms on one event), and the foul carries his name. That delivers the full "fouls committed" spec (the 10-15% per-defender swing, the ~5× stacking) *and* the individual attribution Emmett ruled toward — all against a real per-defender model, tuned then, not now. Its own design + oracle pass.

## Session 60.2 — MEASUREMENT: the first read off a REAL POPULATION. Volume is FREE — the ball-hog is MORE efficient than his even-share teammate. The tax prices him but can never stop him. And the 347-team world we were about to build already exists (2026-07-16)

**Register:** a measurement/design conversation. **NOTHING SHIPPED — no engine change, no config change, no commit.** All code written this session was scratch, lived in the sandbox, and is gone. This entry exists because the findings are not.

**THE CORRECTION THAT OPENED IT (Claude wrong twice; Emmett's instinct right).** Emmett: *"I'm beginning to think we need to start making some realistic teams for these guys to play against, 5 50's across the board is a very unrealistic team."* Claude first pushed back (authoring a "realistic" team is a guess wearing a nicer suit — flat-50's sin with better manners) and then recommended building the divvy. **Both the pushback and the recommendation were wrong on the facts.** The truth, found by looking:

- **`worlds/stock-d1.world.json` has 347 schools**, 32 conferences, 4 tiers. The divvy exists. The season page exists (`season <world.json> <seed>`, Phase 55, in the suite since S29). **Emmett's "eventually we will need 360 unique teams" described something already built.**
- **His prestige instinct was already the ruling**, in the divvy's own header: *"Prestige stops generating quality and becomes what it is: ACCESS."* One national pool, prestige-weighted access, the Gonzaga mechanism. He was arguing for a decision he made at S29.
- **S59 already used it** — the drive gate's league read (rim 36.3%→33.8%) came off the real divvy'd population, not a bench.
- **What IS true:** the pool still runs the Pass-1 position-based generator, and **not one of the 47 committed sweep configs uses `opponentDials`.** S59.2 built the dial, committed the parser, and the four-level divisional-ladder rosters that proved the body gate were never committed — run in-sandbox, thrown away. **The instrument got fixed and nothing was ever pointed through it.** That is the S36.1 stale-plan pattern inverted: the board reads "instrument upgrade shipped," which is true, and misses that it is unused.

**THE INSTRUMENT (scratch, sandbox-only, not committed).** 100 teams × 30 games = 3,000 games. Players drawn from the **live Pass-2 cohort** (`BuildCohort(seed, 46000)`), top 500 by the generator's **own** `Rscore` — the recruiting line, *"value of the player's best viable pathway to minutes"* — so the quality sort was **not** a scalar Claude invented; the generator already computes it and it is oracle-locked. Tendencies came from the committed, golden-proven `DeriveTendencies` (skill-derived, not authored). Random 5-man teams, no prestige, no depth chart (**all HierarchyRank 5**, so skill alone authored usage). Cut at Rscore 57.3 vs a cohort median of 19.2 — roughly the top 1%.

### FINDING 1 — Volume is FREE, and hoarding is a FREE LUNCH (league scale, real population)

Archetype table, tax at today's `PressureVolumeTaxScale` = **0.12**:

| | USG% | FG% | PPP | PPG |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **chucker** (top usage decile) | 39.2% | 39.6% | **0.853** | 26.4 |
| **even-share** (median decile) | 17.7% | 37.1% | **0.775** | 10.8 |

**The man taking 39% of his team's shots is MORE efficient than the man taking 18%, at 2.2× the load.** Gap **+0.078 PPP**. The engine's current advice is: always feed one guy. There is no cost anywhere.

**And reshaping usage across the entire range costs the league 0.4 points a game.** Walking `UsageExponent` 2.0 → 1.0 moves max usage 47.9% → 35.6% and median 17.4% → 19.8%, while league FG% moves **38.3% → 37.9%**, team PPG **62.7 → 62.3**, TO% **17.8 → 17.7**. Going from "one man takes 48%" to "everybody takes 20%" is worth four tenths of a point.

**The arithmetic confirms the dial does exactly what 0.12 predicts, which is nothing.** At 48% usage, pressure = 0.28; × 0.12 = a 3.4% haircut on make odds ≈ 1.4pp of FG% on a 40% shooter; spread over half a team's shots ≈ 0.4pp league-wide. **Observed: 0.4pp.**

**This closes attribute-meaning Finding 4's open question with a number instead of a flat-50 inference**, and confirms the S60 docs correction: the mechanism was never missing, it is *mis-tuned to a whisper*.

### FINDING 2 — The tax PRICES the chucker; no setting of it ever STOPS him

Walking `PressureVolumeTaxScale`, usage dials held fixed:

| taxScale | chucker USG% | chucker FG% | chucker PPP | even-share PPP | **gap** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.12 (today) | 39.2% | 39.6% | 0.853 | 0.775 | **+0.078** |
| 0.40 | 39.0% | 38.2% | 0.825 | 0.778 | +0.046 |
| 0.60 | 39.0% | 37.3% | 0.807 | 0.773 | +0.034 |
| **1.00** | 38.9% | 35.0% | 0.771 | 0.770 | **+0.001** |

**Look at the USG% column: 39.2 → 38.9 across an 8× crank. Frozen.** The tax lives in Roll H on make%; usage is decided upstream in Roll E and never hears the result. **Nothing self-corrects.** No dial in the engine takes the ball away from a man shooting 25.4%.

At **1.00** the star's efficiency edge closes to exactly zero — 2.2× the load for identical PPP, close to what a real alpha looks like. **Claude's recommendation: ~0.7** (a real star probably should keep a small edge). At 0.7 the 48%-usage man pays ~6pp of FG% (Memphis2 1: 41.7 → 35.8; Kentucky4 1: 32.0 → 25.4, a genuine drag) while Auburn 1 still shoots 42.3% on 43% usage because he is good enough to carry it. **That distinction does not exist at 0.12.** Emmett ruled: fix it, but **in a separate calibration session** — wiring first.

### FINDING 3 — Usage LEVELS are historical outliers, and it is the exponent, not the rail

`USG% max 48.1 | p90 32.9 | median 17.6 | min 7.8` — **twenty players above 39% in a 500-player league.** Westbrook's all-time record season is 41.7%.

| exponent | rail | maxUSG | p90 | median | n>35% | n>40% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | 0.52 | 47.9% | 32.4% | 17.4% | 40 | 20 |
| 1.5 | 0.52 | 45.5% | 30.4% | 18.8% | 24 | 5 |
| 1.0 | 0.52 | 35.6% | 27.9% | 19.8% | 2 | 0 |
| 2.0 | 0.35 | 37.5% | 30.9% | 18.6% | 4 | 0 |

**The exponent shapes the whole curve; the rail only clips the tip** (0.52 → 0.35 moves p90 just 32.4 → 30.9 — it never binds below the very top). **DO NOT fix this with the exponent** — dropping it to 1.0 makes every number look right by making the 45%-usage alpha *impossible to generate*, contradicting Emmett's own ruling (*"I'm not against, in extreme situations, it being higher than that, but it should come with a pretty hefty efficiency hit"*). **He wants that player to exist and to pay. The exponent deletes him; the tax charges him.**

**Note the median: 17.6%, BELOW the 20% even share.** The stars eat so much that the median player is starved — which is why S60's relief fired on three-of-five starters. Same root.

He chucks because his SelfCreation is high. Nobody chose him; no coach can bench him; a 3-for-19 night changes nothing. The dial *meant* to express a coach's plan is `HierarchyRank` — **and S59.2 already found it broken** (only 4 of 10 settings do anything; one step is worth 11 usage points). It is Parked. **This finding is the reason to un-park it.** Emmett's framing, the clearest statement of the problem all session: ***"Nobody chose him. He chose himself."***

### FINDING 5 — The S60 relief is roughly 10× too quiet, and the intent-vs-touches Open is why

Walking `UsageReliefBonusScale`; FG% by usage decile (lowest usage → highest):

| scale | d1 | d2 | d3 | d4 | d5 | d6 | d7 | d8 | d9 | d10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.0 | 35.8 | 39.5 | 37.8 | 36.4 | 37.3 | 36.8 | 36.9 | 38.2 | 37.5 | 39.9 |
| **1.0 (today)** | **37.0** | 40.6 | 39.9 | 37.8 | 39.0 | 35.8 | 36.1 | 38.4 | 38.0 | 39.6 |
| 4.0 | **45.3** | 44.7 | 42.0 | 42.8 | 40.9 | 36.6 | 37.1 | 38.0 | 37.4 | 40.4 |

At **0** the curve is flat. At **4** it is the shape Emmett asked for: 45.3% for low-usage men sliding to 40.4% for ball-hogs. **At 1.0 the bottom decile gains 1.2pp — invisible.** Emmett noticed unprompted (*"I am also concerned as to why the players with lower usage aren't shooting a little bit higher to simulate them getting more open shots"*): the wire is live and firing, at a tenth of the volume the basketball wants.

**It is also quieter than DESIGNED.** Decile 1 averages 9.1% usage → relief should be 0.109 → +10.9% relative → ~+3.9pp. **Observed: +1.2pp.** The likely cause is S60's own Open item: **the relief pays on the share the offense INTENDS, not the touches a man gets.** These are exactly the players the defense sags off, so the tilt strips them further below what the books say they carry, and they are paid for the smaller gap — the mechanism that left Okafor at 52.2 → 52.2. **Rule intent-vs-touches BEFORE tuning this scale**, or the scale gets tuned to compensate for a bonus computed off the wrong number and a later fix makes it twice too strong.

### FINDING 6 — TO% is NORMAL. Claude's turnover flag was noise; Emmett killed it.

Claude flagged "6–7 turnovers a game" off the first run. **Emmett:** *"6 turnovers isn't crazy if it comes with 50% usage. TO% is much more indicative of any issues."* Correct — the counting stat was the wrong lens.

**League TO% = 17.8** (real D1: 17–19). The **twenty highest-usage players average 15.8%** — *better* than league average, exactly how it should look. Alabama 1's "6.4 turnovers" is a **17.6% rate at 45.7% usage.** There is no turnover problem on a real population. (The S49 attribution inversion concerns *blame*, not rate, and stays open on its own terms.)

### FINDING 7 — Efficiency reads LOW across the board, and it is NOT a distribution problem

Top-1% field: **FG% 38.4 | 3P% 28.8 | FT% 63.1 | team PPG 62.9**, against real D1 of roughly 44 / 34 / 71 / 72. Every number 5–8 points light, all the same direction — a field of blue-chips shooting worse than an average real team.

**Claude's hypothesis — that concentration on bad shooters dragged FG% down — is DEAD:**
- attempt-weighted league FG% **38.4** vs per-player mean **38.5** → concentration costs **0.1pp**
- **r(USG%, FG%) = −0.004** (top 500) and **+0.082** (full cohort, variance intact)

**The zero was checked for the artifact it looks like.** A "no effect" headline is exactly what a restricted range manufactures (S59.2's standing rule), and the top-500 pool was selected on Rscore, which correlates with both usage and shooting — so the correlation was re-run on the **unrestricted 46,000-player cohort**. It survives. Not a selection artifact.

**A caveat on Claude's own metric, recorded so nobody over-reads the flat correlation:** FG% is confounded by shot location. The diet is skill-derived, so the best shooter takes *threes* and posts a low FG% **by design**, while a rim-runner posts a high one for dunking. **PPP is the right lens**, and on PPP the top usage decile *is* modestly better (0.74 → 0.85 top-1%; 0.62 → 0.69 full cohort). **Flat-ish PPP-vs-usage is arguably CORRECT basketball** — the usage-efficiency tradeoff is real and the skill-curve debate lands near flat. Emmett's call, not a bug.

So the low levels are a **curve** read, not a distribution read — the first ever taken against a real population, and what S47's FT note (*"flat-50 FT% ~49.8, a calibration note for later"*) has been waiting for.

**A spread worth a real check, not a shrug:** the random-world field (all 46,000, median Rscore 19.2) ran **FG% 27.8 / team PPG 50.8**; the top-1% field ran **38.4 / 62.9** — a 12-point PPG spread. S59.2's divisional ladder found scores nearly flat across levels (53–53 at D3, 57–57 at high-major). Not necessarily a contradiction — these endpoints are far wider than D3-to-D1, since "everyone in the pool" includes thousands who would never play anywhere — but it is unexplained and should not be assumed benign.

## Session 60 — The USAGE-RELIEF bonus SHIPPED (v1): the low-usage half of the usage↔efficiency curve. Emmett's underathletic sniper can now exist. And the wire pays on what your offense INTENDS to give a man, not what the defense lets him have — measured, not assumed (2026-07-14)

**Register:** a build session. Full CONVENTIONS ritual — fresh pull, required reads, check-in gate, oracle-first, sandbox pre-check, green on Emmett's machine, then docs. **One engine behavior added; the tax side did not move.**

**What shipped.** The engine has taxed a player for carrying MORE than his equal share since Phase 17/27 — `pressure = max(0, share − equalShare)` — but paid **nothing** for carrying less: every below-share player read exactly 0, so a 13%-usage specialist shot identically to a 20%-usage one. S60 adds the mirror, stamped in the same pass off the same array:

    relief   = max(0, equalShare − finalShare)          → Roll E stamps it (RollEGenerator.ReliefAt)
    makePct  = clamp01(makePct × (1 + relief × Scale))   → Roll H pays it (RollHGenerator.ApplyUsageRelief)

Applied in Roll H **after the C3 penalty block, before the C4 passing converter** — the input stage is named in the golden so parity can never be achieved against the wrong stage. **Multiplicative**, so it scales the probability the player already earned from his matchup: a bad shooter on a light load is still a bad shooter, just a somewhat more efficient one. **Emmett's design ruling (2026-07-14):** *a light load lets anyone shoot "open shots" and be somewhat efficient regardless of ratings; fed usage, the ratings show.* **Emmett's anchor ruling holds:** the ~31.7% at 43% usage is plausibly correct — **anchor the top, lift the bottom**. `UsageReliefBonusScale` = 1.0, a CALIBRATION PLACEHOLDER; the SHAPE is what was signed off (S59.2 archetype table: sniper at 13.5% usage, 3P 37.1 → ~39.5). **0 is the legal kill switch** and runs a true identity branch — bit-identical for the right reason, not via a harmless ×1.0.

**Three design properties, each deliberate.** (1) **Its own branch, NOT folded into C3.** The Phase 17 block is gated `if (usagePressure > 0.0 || usageResidual > 0.0)` — precisely the branch a below-share shooter never enters. Folding the relief in would have meant it silently never fires on the players it exists for; a green suite would not have caught it. (2) **Attention does NOT amplify it.** `C3AttentionAmplifier` scales the *penalties* for an above-share, above-attention shooter; relief is shot-selection and is independent by the locked shape. (3) **Gravity and relief COMPOUND, intentionally.** They read different inputs — C1/C4 read team openness/gravity/spacing (who is around you), relief reads the shooter's own share (how little load he carries) — so a player with both gets both, multiplicatively. That is Emmett's *"stats are contextual to teammates"* composed with his *"open shots"* ruling, not double attribution. Phase 66 proves the **input** independence (C4 neutralized, nothing clamping, live/kill ratio == the multiplier in both gravity states), and separately proves the compounding is real: gravity off +2.59pp, gravity on +4.35pp.

**THE FINDING — the wire pays on INTENT, not on touches.** Emmett's box score showed an asymmetry Claude went and measured through the live generator rather than explain away: slot 5 moved hard (Baptiste 42.2→44.0, Thornton 43.7→46.1) while slot 4 barely moved at all (Okafor 52.2→52.2, Eze 52.9→53.1) — **and both take ~13% of the shots.** The corpus's actual reliefs:

| player | share the offense INTENDS | relief | bonus |
|---|---|---|---|
| Marcus Webb | 20.06% | 0.0000 | none |
| DeShawn Pryor | 23.89% | 0.0000 | none |
| Trey Holloway | 22.76% | 0.0000 | none |
| Javon Okafor | 18.45% | 0.0155 | +1.6% |
| Cory Baptiste | 14.84% | 0.0516 | +5.2% |

**Okafor takes 13.5% of the shots in the actual games, but his own offense intends 18.45% for him** — a hair under even. The defense strips the other five points off him via the Phase 27 tilt and the Phase 46 denial, both of which run **after** Roll E stamps. So the engine pays him for being 1.5 points below even, not the 6.5 he actually plays; his +1.6% bonus is small enough to vanish into sampling noise on ~7,900 attempts, which is exactly what the box score shows. Baptiste is the opposite: his team genuinely does not feature him, so he gets the real bonus. **Three of five get nothing at all.**

This is **not a bug and not an asymmetry the relief introduced** — the tax reads the same pre-tilt basis (`RollEGenerator.cs` ~249: *"the tilt changes WHICH slot is rolled, not the pressure each slot carries"*), so the two stay perfectly mirrored. It was flagged at the check-in gate before a line was written, Emmett said go, and the S59.2/S60 scope wall closes the wants-vs-gets thread. But it **changes what is true to write down**: *"low-usage players shoot better"* is the wrong sentence; *"players their own offense does not feature shoot better"* is the right one. They come apart precisely for the man the defense takes away. Logged as a new Open for the calibration page, not chased.

**It also answers the S59.2 loose thread** (*"the usage-pressure penalty may read what a player wants rather than what he gets"*) with a precise verdict: the pivot reads **post-floor/rail** shares — so the rail's clamping IS reflected, and a railed star is NOT paying for shots the rail took away — but **pre-tilt and pre-denial**, so the defense's denial is not reflected on either side of the curve. Half of the thread is closed; the other half is the new Open above.

**The prompt's "complete inventory" was incomplete — caught at the check-in gate.** `RollE.Execute` does not take the `RollEGeneration` record; it takes `double[] pressures` as a loose positional parameter. Stamping relief therefore widened the signature to carry `double[] reliefs`, which broke **six files the prompt never listed**: `Resolver.cs` (both Roll E call sites — `genE.Reliefs` / `breakGenE.Reliefs`) and 13 harness call sites across `Program.Observation.cs`, `Program.Checks.Rebounding.cs`, `Program.Checks.Shooting.cs`, `Program.Checks.Selection.cs`. All compile-loud, all mechanical, no scope change — but twelve files, not six.

**Three extractions (an engineering call, flagged as a call).** The relief math now lives in **one named place each** — `RollEGenerator.ReliefAt`, `RollEGenerator.PressureAt`, `RollHGenerator.ApplyUsageRelief` — and the live game and the Phase 66 check call **the same statics**. Without this the golden would have bound to a *second copy* of the formula and could have been green while the engine did something else; it also gave the pivot check exact probe points (`equalShare ± ε`) instead of a numeric search. The tax's old inline expression now routes through `PressureAt`: same arithmetic, byte-identical output (every pre-existing golden parity line unchanged), but the pivot physically lives in one place instead of two lines that happen to agree.

**Assumptions 1–7 verified at the gate, all held.** Pivot `1.0/populated` on post-rail shares (`RollEGenerator.cs` ~194, after `ApplyFloorAndRail`); the C3 gate skips the relief case (`RollHGenerator.cs` ~259); five `RollEGeneration` ctor sites confirmed by repo-wide grep (86/121/206, stub 66, spy 1836 — no deconstruction anywhere); `RollK.cs` ~123 reset + Roll E's unconditional stamp + Roll H's putback short-circuit at ~81 bound the leak; `RimCeiling` 0.9527 live, so `0.9527 × 1.11 = 1.0575` — **the clamp zone is genuinely reachable at the rim**, making the clamp production code rather than a defensive no-op.

**Proven by the new Phase 66 check (30 assertions OK).** Golden parity 8 cases at 1e-12 (**worst |Δ| = 0.0e0**, `UsageReliefBonusScale` cross-checked against the loaded config first, identity rows held to a **harder** bar than the tolerance — bit-exact return of the input, not merely within 1e-12 of it; the fixture is required to exercise ≥3 identity rows and ≥1 clamped row). Formula invariants: relief exactly 0 at and above equal share; all three monotonicities as share rises (relief, multiplier, makePctAfterRelief), **including through the clamp** where a flat saturated region is permitted but a rise is not; equal-share player bit-identical on a LIVE scale; kill switch bit-identical at every relief × every input including the clamping-capable one; bonus-only; the clamp saturating at exactly 1.0. **Pivot consistency, exact semantics, both lineup sizes** (populated 5 and 4): `equalShare−ε` → relief only, exactly `equalShare` → both exactly 0, `equalShare+ε` → tax only — no numeric transition search — plus the algebraic identity that makes the shared pivot **structural** rather than a coincidence of two similar-looking formulas: `pressure − relief == share − equalShare` **exactly**, and `pressure × relief == 0`, at every probed share and on every slot of a live Roll E run. Wiring proofs through the real Roll E→H path: the star taxed (share 52.00%, pressure 0.3200) and the role big relieved (share 12.00%, relief 0.0800); **the below-share big's make% rises 27.87% → 29.98% (+2.11pp)**; **the above-share star bit-identical live vs kill (0.4266045746128752) — the anchor ruling as an assertion**; null-stamped state → 0 → existing probes bit-unchanged; explicit 0.0 bit-identical to null; FastBreak bit-identical; the putback probe bit-identical **even with a deliberately hostile stale relief of 0.11** (the short-circuit holds above the C-block); RollK's ResetOffense clearing relief to null. Config guards: negative throws, 0 loads cleanly.

**Middle-rung sandbox pre-check taken** (SDK from the Ubuntu feed; oracle ALL OK before porting; compiled + full suite green in-sandbox). **Green on Emmett's machine: `ALL CHECKS PASSED`** — and **Phase 66 matched the sandbox byte-for-byte**, `0.4266045746128752` to the last digit, the same `+2.11pp`, the same `1.110000000` ratio. S56's sandbox==Windows finding repeating, and unlike S58/S59 there was no Linux-vs-Windows `tanh`/`pow` gap to report because this formula is one multiply and a compare.

**§0.7 drift audit — baselined the pristine tree and diffed the full suite.** 867 lines moved, **every one sanctioned**: the observation corpus, all eight stress buckets, the season page, turnover-clock counts, the config hash. **Unmoved as asserted:** every Phase 61–65 golden verdict byte-identical, Phase 56's parity byte-identical, every direct-stamp Roll H probe. **No unexplained mover.** League FG% **43.73% → 44.03% (+0.30pp)** — the bottom edge of the predicted 0.3–0.6pp band, and predicted to the digit before Emmett ran it. PPP 0.9755 → 0.9814.

## Session 59.2 — The DIVISIONAL GATE is real and already built (measured, not shipped): same skill + a small slow body = a D3 star and a below-average high-major player. The sweep bench can dial the opponent now — and the flat-50 opponent it used for eight families was hiding the mechanism. Claude was wrong FOUR times — the fourth by a rule it had written into these docs twenty minutes earlier; all four are recorded (2026-07-14)

**Register:** a design conversation that turned into a measurement session. **No engine change. No config constant changed.** Harness-only instrument upgrade (`opponentDials`) + ~110,000 games of measurement, all run in-sandbox. Findings live in `attribute-meaning.md`; nothing here is a tune.

**Where it started.** Closing S59, Emmett questioned the drive gate's absolute 28→48 handle-unlock anchor: *"I think that bar needs not exist. If I'm a quick, athletic 6'6" guy against a slow, plodding 7-footer, even a 10 handle will get me around some. But if the defender is just as athletic, that 10 handle won't do him much."* Pushed further, he named the general principle: **"this is how virtually every attribute that counts stats should work. When athleticism and/or size are major advantages, skill advantages get muted hard; when the bodies equalize, skill is felt hardest. It's the size and athleticism which dictate where you can play, more than anything else."** And then the question that reframed the session: *"Is this not how we've been building things this entire time?"*

**The answer was yes, and Claude said no. WRONG CALL #1.** Claude read `EffectiveRating` (`baseline + skillShift + physicalShift + heightShift`), `DeriveDisplacement` (`skillLevel + physLevel`), and `BlockWeight` (fixed per-zone weights × skill + × length), saw addition everywhere, and asserted flatly that the engine "has never worked that way — not in one place." **The muting lives one stage later, in the bounded logistic that converts rating → make%, not in the arithmetic.** A big body gap shoves a player toward the curve's floor, where the same rating difference buys a much smaller make% difference. `design.md`'s own Phase-4 additive-vs-multiplicative ruling says so explicitly — *"a monster physical edge crushes a player toward the floor, where the make%-distance between him and a scrub compresses — athleticism 'wipes out the skill gap' in the box score"* — and that ruling was the **stated reason additive beat multiplicative**. Claude read the rating math, stopped, and contradicted a design decision recorded in the doc it had already pulled. Emmett's memory of his own architecture was correct; Claude's source-read was half a stage short.

**WRONG CALL #2 — the flat-50 bench, and the finding it manufactured.** Corrected, Claude then measured properly: 28,000 games walking a player's body 20→80 at two skill levels. Result: what elite skill is worth was **dead flat** (+11.2pp FG% at body 20, +11.6 at body 50, +11.1 at body 80) and *rose* slightly in points. Claude reported this as emphatic — "there is no muting; not weak muting, **none**" — and told Emmett the divisional mechanism "doesn't exist yet." Rebounding agreed and looked worse for the thesis (rating worth +2.7 at body 20 climbing monotonically to +3.7 at body 80; the 6'4" 190 weak-athlete elite rebounder grabbed **8.1 boards**, more than an average-bodied average-handed player's 7.7). **Emmett rejected the premise, not the numbers:** *"50s across the board is not very good talent."* He was right. **The sweep bench hardcoded Team B at flat all-50** — no way to dial it — which caps the body gap at ~±30, and the logistic compression does not bite until well past that. The bench could not see the thing it was pointed at.

**The instrument upgrade (the only code this session).** Optional top-level **`opponentDials`** on the sweep config: same `"1"–"5"` → dial-object shape as a case's `slotDials`, run through the **same** `ParseDialObject` — hoisted from a local function inside the cases parser to a shared static specifically so the opponent could not drift onto a second, laxer copy. Absent = flat all-50, so **every pre-S59.2 config reproduces byte-for-byte** (proven by diff on a full rerun of the rebound walk). **Deliberately fixed across rungs, not per-rung:** the opponent is the *neighborhood*, held still while the swept player walks; per-rung opponent dialing would move two things at once. To walk the competition itself, run one config per level and assemble. The console header now prints the opponent's actual dials so no run can silently misreport what it measured.

**What the corrected instrument says — the gate is real, and it was already built.** Same walk, two opponents. What an elite scoring edge is worth (FG%):

| swept body | vs flat-50 | vs a real high-major roster |
|---|---|---|
| 20 | +11.2 | **+6.0** |
| 50 | +11.6 | +10.6 |
| 80 | +11.1 | +9.9 |

Nearly **halved** for the small slow player against real talent. Rebounding the same: against a genuine 6'10"-hyper-athlete front line, hands are worth +1.6 at body 20 vs +2.7 at body 80, **perfect hands + tiny body = 5.3 boards while average hands + freak body = 7.8** — the freak wins by 47% with worse hands, which is Emmett's ruling exactly. Against flat-50 the same comparison had *inverted*.

**The divisional ladder — the headline.** Real level-appropriate rosters on both sides, four levels. **The relative-engine control held perfectly:** a typical player scores **11.6 / 12.1 / 12.2 / 12.3** points at D3 / D2 / mid-major / high-major and every game is even (53–53, 55–55, 56–56, 57–57). *"The same mathematical drama at D3 as at D1"* is now measured, not asserted. Then one player, **identical elite scoring skill, two bodies:**

| level | typical | 6'1" & slow | big & athletic |
|---|---|---|---|
| D3 | 11.6 / 35.3% | **19.6 / 44.5%** star | **27.6 / 57.6%** monster |
| D2 | 12.1 / 36.9% | 17.8 / 42.8% very good | 24.1 / 53.8% |
| Mid-major | 12.2 / 38.8% | 14.0 / 38.0% ordinary | 19.8 / 48.9% |
| High-major | 12.3 / 38.9% | **10.7 / 32.0% BELOW average** | **16.6 / 44.0% still a star** |

**Identical skill. The body alone sets the ceiling.** The small player tops out around D2; the big one is a star anywhere. His shooting decays 44.5 → 42.8 → 38.0 → 32.0 as he climbs — that decay *is* the muting. **Every part of Emmett's divisional thesis checks out.** The S59 unlock-anchor worry is largely defused: the relative machinery already sorts by body.

**WRONG CALL #3 — and the usage hole it exposed.** The D3 star scored 19.6, not the ~25 Emmett wants. Emmett: *"no coaching strategy as well as 50s across the board tilting usage."* Half right — the teammates were level-appropriate, **but `HierarchyRank` was pinned at its baseline 5 for every player the bench has ever built**, so no sweep in `attribute-meaning.md` has ever had a go-to guy. Walking it exposed four findings: **(1)** ranks 7/8/9/10 are the *same player* (45.1/45.1/45.2/45.2% usage) — proven to be `UsageRail` 0.52 by lifting it to 0.95, whereupon they separate and hit a *second* wall at 54% (`UsageFloor` 0.09 × 4 teammates = 36%, capping anyone at 64% of selections); **(2)** one rank step is worth **eleven usage points** (rank 5 → 29.1%, rank 6 → 40.4%) so there is no setting producing the ~33% a 25-point scorer needs, and rank 6 is already past real basketball (~32–36%); a normal chart 10/7/5/3/1 on identical players gives **45.7 / 22.0 / 12.4 / 10.1 / 9.9** — one star and four ghosts, the middle of the roster mashed against the floor; **(3) the structural one** — Claude proposed `HierarchyExponentNeutral` 1.0 → 0.5 off the identical-player bench (#1: 45.7 → 38.9, apparently fixing it) and **it does nothing on a realistic roster** (44.8 → 44.8), because a genuinely more-skilled star is pinned against the rail before the depth chart speaks. **So `UsageRail` — designed as an emergency brake — is what actually authors every real star's usage.** Nobody decided 45%; that is just where the fence is, which is also why the top of the dial is dead. Emmett's 40% ceiling is therefore **not a tuning job**; dropping the rail to ~0.46 hits 40% while leaving the dial equally dead one notch lower. **(4)** volume is **free**: usage climbs 29.1 → 45.2% and FG% *rises* 44.5 → 45.8. The Phase 17 usage diet shift is meant to be the price and is not biting — which blocks Emmett's ruling directly (*"I'm not against, in extreme situations, it being higher than that, but it should come with a pretty hefty efficiency hit"*). That player cannot exist today.

**Emmett's spec, recorded for the Roll E session:** usage above ~40% unrealistic; below ~8–10% unrealistic; extreme usage permitted **if** it carries a hefty efficiency cost. `UsageFloor` 0.09 already matches the lower bound.

**Emmett's stop ruling (2026-07-14):** *"until we get an actual variety of real players, I'm not sure we get much from this."* Correct, and consistent with the page-only calibration principle — the synthetic bench had produced three wrong readings in one session and a fourth would have taught nothing. **No constant was changed.** All rail/exponent numbers came from temporary edits to the *build-output* config, reverted after each run, with the committed `config.json` verified byte-identical afterward (one restore line reported success before it had actually restored; caught, source and delivered files confirmed untouched by diff).

**Loose thread logged, not chased:** with the rail artificially lifted, rank 10 posted 39.0 FG% while rank 9 at *identical* usage (54.3 vs 54.4) posted 45.1. Not live behavior. The shape suggests the usage-pressure penalty may be computed from what a player *wants* rather than what he *gets* — so a clamped star could be paying a diet penalty for shots he never takes. Ten minutes in the Roll E session.

**The role-player probe — and WRONG CALL #4, the same trap inside the same hour.** Emmett, closing: *"we were doing it as what if this guy was a star player? But what if this 6'1" guy who could score 27 in D3 got to be the fourth option on a D1 team? He could be really impactful in the right role."* This exposed a blind spot in every measurement above: **every player was run as the star.** Probed, the D3 scorer on a high-major roster shot 34.5% at 13% usage vs 31.7% at 43% — **a thirty-point usage drop buying 2.8 points of shooting**. Claude then reported that "good teammates don't help him — the attention channel deserves its own look," having held the teammates fixed at skill 68 and varied only his rank. **Wrong, and by the exact rule Claude had written into these docs twenty minutes earlier.** Varying the teammates: his 3P% climbs **27.7 → 32.1 → 34.1 → 37.1 → 37.7** as teammate skill goes 55 → 97. **The S48 gravity→attention→relief channel is live and worth +10pp**; it delivers Emmett's player exactly (the underathletic sniper hits 37.1% from three in a Big 12 environment as a low-usage option beside real talent). The clean decomposition — elite teammates fixed, only his rank moving — gives 37.1% at rank 1 and 37.1% at rank 5 and 36.1% at rank 10: **he shoots the same whether he is the first option or the fifth.** So **teammate gravity does everything and role does nothing**: context changes a player's value, role does not. Two further findings fell out: the dial is dead at the **bottom** too (ranks 1/2/3 identical, all floored — so 4/5/6/7 are the only live settings, four of ten, not the three previously reported), and **next to elite teammates the dial collapses entirely** (ranks 1–7 all give 13.5% usage; even rank 10 reaches only 20.3%, the skill channel drowning the hierarchy weight — a coach cannot make a specialist high-usage on a good roster). **This is Finding 4 from the other side: volume has no price AND scarcity has no reward — one flat curve, two impossible players.** Emmett's anchor ruling: **the ~31.7% at 43% usage is plausibly correct; the low-usage end is the wrong number** — so the fix anchors the top and lifts the bottom, and is not a re-tune of the star.

**Emmett's scope ruling for the next session (2026-07-14): the CURVE only, not the dial.** The usage↔efficiency link is what four separate threads need (Pass B's whole payoff is "the denied drive becomes someone else's better shot" — the exact wire proven dead here); the hierarchy dial's coarseness and the rail-authors-usage finding stay parked, because they cannot be fixed honestly without the real population Emmett's stop ruling already called for. Per CONVENTIONS §6 the prompt is **not** drafted from this session's momentum — its own audited pass, fresh pull, reflection gate.

**The methodological finding, which outlives every number above.** The bench's flat baselines are a **convenience, not a neutral control**. Each one is an assumption that the measured thing does not interact with what was flattened — and that assumption failed **three times in one session**: flat-50 *opponents* hid the body-gap muting; flat-50 *teammates* invalidated the first divisional ladder; *identical players* hid the usage rail. **Whenever a finding's headline is "X has no effect," suspect the baseline before believing it** — that is the conclusion a flattened control manufactures. Every finding in `attribute-meaning.md` from S45–S55.1 was measured against a flat-50 opponent and now carries a document-wide caveat: each is the *even-bodied, average-competition* answer, not the general one. Re-measuring the eight families against dialed opponents is Open. Emmett caught this from the outside, twice, with no access to the code — both times by refusing a premise rather than disputing a number.

**Next:** Roll E usage architecture — the two channels (skill + depth chart) must land inside 8–40% *by design*, with the rail returning to an emergency brake that never fires in a normal game, and volume carrying a real efficiency price. Downstream of a real generated population per Emmett's stop ruling, so the divvy/generation work likely comes first.

## Session 59 — Pass A: the perimeter-defense DRIVE GATE SHIPPED (v1): a walled perimeter driver now loses part of his rim access and re-routes it to a contested three — a per-man location transform in Roll G, post-displacement, shot DIET only; the S54 "perimeter defense is point-neutral" finding is ANSWERED (2026-07-14)

**Scope:** The fifth engine change of the wiring arc, and the first of the three-pass answer to the **S54 perimeter-defense point-neutrality** finding (a perimeter stack pushed the opponent off the three but into higher-% twos, so B.PTS barely moved — perimeter defense paid only alongside rim protection). Pass A gives the on-ball defender a **rim-access wall**. Three pure statics on `Matchup` (`DriveTools`, `DriveOrientation`, `ApplyDriveGate`) + the `DriveGateTrace` record, ONE insertion in `RollGGenerator.GenerateWithResidual`, 11 knobs on `MatchupConfig` (+ `config.json`), a new **Phase 65** suite check, and the csproj golden copy. The oracle + golden were **already committed** before the build (locked spec, signed off 2026-07-14) and were NOT regenerated — verified byte-identical after a re-run. Roll E / selection / usage (Pass B), the off-ball three lever (Pass C), make% anywhere, `DeriveDisplacement` and its constants, `TiltInteriorDiet`, `ApplyDietShift`, the coaching layer, and the foul paths were **not** touched. Full CONVENTIONS ritual: fresh pull, every §1 sibling read against live source, all seven adversarial assumptions checked at the check-in gate, Emmett's explicit go before the first file. Middle-rung pre-check taken: SDK from the Ubuntu feed, tree compiled clean, full suite ran green in-sandbox before delivery.

**What shipped (the locked spec, ported constant-for-constant).** A per-man location transform applied to the **displaced** pie and **before** the usage diet shift:
- **`DriveTools` — first step BEATS him, the handle only UNLOCKS it.** `beat = 0.62·FirstStep + 0.38·Quickness`, times `unlock = clamp01((BallHandling − 28)/(48 − 28))`. The weights are asymmetric on purpose (burst primary, lateral quickness support). The handle is a **multiplicative gate, not an additive term**: an elite handle with no burst is walled like an average driver (it scales a mediocre beat), a quick first step with NO handle scores **exactly 0** and is walled hardest, and BallHandling above 48 changes the composite by **exactly 0** — a permission slip, never a scoring edge.
- **`DriveOrientation` — perimeter-oriented only.** `clamp01(1 − (offPostness − 46)/26)` over `offPostness = (Height + Strength + PostMoves)/3`. Guard → 1, post scorer → 0 (immune — a perimeter wall does not reach the post route), point-forward → partial. **Deliberately NOT `Matchup.Postness`** (which reads Height/**PostDefense**/Strength — a defense-side "is he a big"). This asks an offense-side question — "is HE a post player" — so it must read **PostMoves**. Reusing the existing helper compiles, looks right, and silently breaks the golden's POST-scorer case; the divergence was caught at draft time and re-confirmed at the gate.
- **`ApplyDriveGate` — suppression-PRIMARY, diet only.** `gap = DriveTools − matched.PerimeterDefense`; only the wall side fires: `supp = GapFn(max(0, −gap), 1.0, 1.4, ReferenceScale 25)` (the shared normalizer — no twin knob), `mult = 1 − 0.55·tanh(supp/1.5)`. Remove `orient·(1−mult)` of Rim and `0.45·orient·(1−mult)` of Short (Short is only partly drive-derived — floaters yes, post-ups and cuts no), redistribute to **contested Long/Three only**, proportional to the shooter's own pre-gate outer preference (exact 50/50 when both outer zones are zero — a real branch, not a divide-by-zero patch), renormalize. **Mid NEVER moves** — a denied drive becomes a contested jumper from distance, not a pull-up. An offense edge (gap ≥ 0) removes **exactly 0**: the weak-defender "leak" is the ABSENCE of a wall, never an added bonus.

**Placement is the whole point, and it is what the golden proves.** The gate composes on `trace.Final` — the displaced pie, no usage shift yet — because displacement reads where the defending **team** is collectively soft, and the gate then lets the ONE matched man override that invitation. A lockdown defender keeps his man out of a paint the team shape just invited him into. The fixture's `before` pies are FIXED INPUTS, so Phase 65 tests the gate in isolation and the displacement regression stays Phase 56's job (Phase 56 calls `DeriveDisplacement` directly and is structurally blind to a downstream Roll G gate — asserted and held).

**The identity branch, and why it exists.** When `removed <= 0` — orient 0 (post scorer), suppression 0 (gap ≥ 0, or a flat-50 world), `DriveGateCap = 0` (the kill switch), no eligible Rim/Short mass, or a null matched defender (bypass) — the INPUT array is returned untouched: no subtract-0, no redistribute-0, no renormalize. This is what makes a **live** gate at flat-50 bit-identical to the kill switch **for the right reason**, rather than differing by a renormalization ULP on a pie that does not sum to exactly 1.0. Conservation lives **pre-renormalization** (raw removed == raw added, so `RawSum` is 1.0 within tolerance); the renormalize that follows is float hygiene only, never the mechanism — and Phase 65 asserts the raw sum, not just the final one.

**The bypass is a real branch, not a formality.** `DefenderPicker.Pick` is a **pure same-number slot map** — it does NOT substitute another body when that slot is empty (verified on the pull). So a shooter can have four defenders on the floor and still have no man; that is a genuine bypass, distinct from the existing `populated == 0` short-circuit, and the gate does NOT fall back to a phantom default-50 defender. Phase 65's wiring proof uses a deliberately tools-POOR shooter (composite 20) so a phantom-50 bug WOULD move his pie, with a positive control proving the same shooter IS walled once slot 1 is populated.

**One call surfaced at the gate, logged not acted on.** `DefenderPicker`'s own doc says to promote the pick to a carried `PossessionState.DefenderSlot` the moment a SECOND door consumes it — this gate is that second door. Deliberately NOT promoted: the pick is a pure deterministic slot map, so both doors compute the same man and cannot disagree. The promotion becomes real the moment the pick turns mismatch-hunting. Emmett's call at the gate; recorded in the Roll G source comment.

**Two prompt corrections caught at the check-in gate.** (1) The prompt's §3 said "12 cases"; the golden has **13** (12 archetype + 1 both-zero boundary) — checked as 13. (2) Assumption 7 claimed Phase 9 (d3)'s all-75 uniform world stays neutral because "comp 75 vs perimD 75 → gap 0." It is actually an all-**75 offense** vs an all-**45 defense**: gap **+30**, an offense edge, so suppression is zero. Same outcome, different reason — and worth the correction, because (d3) is not structurally pinned the way the prompt implied; a future calibration that lowered the composite would start moving it.

**The one mover, predicted at the gate and landed exactly.** Phase 9 sub-check **(d2)** — "same-level matched control" — legitimately moves: an average-tooled shooter (composite 50) against a perimD-65 matched man is precisely who the gate should wall. Predicted at check-in as rim 53.196% → 45.398%; landed at rim **53.196% → 45.398%**, diff 3.196% → 4.602%, still inside its 6-point band (headroom reduced, not breached). Every other Phase 9 sub-check is unmoved by arithmetic, not by luck: (a)/(d1)/(e2)/(e3) sit at gap 0, (d3) at an offense edge, (b)/(c) vary RimProtection only while the matched man's PerimeterDefense stays 50, (e1) short-circuits before the gate.

**Validation — green on Emmett's machine, and the drift audit enumerated.** The new **Phase 65** check, all 42 assertions OK: (1) **golden parity** — 13 cases at 1e-12 on the after-pie per zone AND the internals (`driveComposite`/`orient`/`suppressionMult`/`removed`), constants cross-checked against the loaded `MatchupConfig` before a single number is trusted, bypass exercised through the null-matched path (its fixture internals are the oracle's bypass sentinels, which the null branch reproduces exactly); (2) **structural invariants**, the oracle's ported — bit-exact gap-0 identity, conservation across a perimD grid, monotone in perimD (removal non-decreasing AND post-gate Rim never rising) and in drive tools (removal non-increasing AND post-gate Rim never falling) stated against **named outputs**, suppression-primary (gap ≥ 0 removes exactly 0), first-step-beats-handle stated concretely (+10 FirstStep buys 6.20 vs +10 Quickness 3.80; handle above HandleHi worth exactly 0; elite burst at HandleLo → composite exactly 0 and walled 18.0pp), post-immune/guard-eligible, Mid bit-untouched with Rim/Short down and Long/Three up, raw conservation pre-renorm, both-zero 50/50 split, kill switch bit-identity, the identity branch's live-gate bit-identity, bypass bit-identity; (3) **wiring proofs** the oracle cannot do — flat-50 end-to-end bit-identity live vs Cap-0, the null-matched bypass with its phantom-defender tripwire + positive control (rim 22.76% → 12.30% once the man appears), the walled guard end-to-end at zero usage (rim 22.76% → 14.41%, three 17.42% → 23.15%, Mid bit-unmoved), the gate **surviving `ApplyDietShift`** at usage 0.30 (rim 16.72% → 10.69%), the post scorer bit-untouched end-to-end, and a placement proof by construction (a soft paint invites him in — displaced rim 26.82% vs tendency 20% — and the matched wall takes it back to 16.97%); (4) **config guards** — 12 throw cases plus BOTH legal kill states (`DriveGateCap = 0` and the redundant `DriveGateSteepness = 0`). On Emmett's machine: `ALL CHECKS PASSED`, Phase 56 unmoved as asserted.

**The §0.7 drift audit, enumerated and classified.** Every pre-existing suite line was diffed baseline-vs-live in-sandbox. **Sanctioned movers:** Phase 9 (d2) (above, predicted); the observation corpus and the 4,000-game stress buckets (named in §0.7); the Phase 55 season page and Phase 57 turnover-clock counts (real-engine runs on real populations — the same class as the corpus, and the checks that moved are conservation/reconciliation identities, not basketball targets, all still green); the config hash (11 new knobs). **Unmoved as required:** Phase 56, all other Phase 9 sub-checks, fastbreak/transition, everything flat-50. **No unexplained mover.** On the real divvy'd population the gate does exactly what Pass A wanted: league-scale rim share **36.3% → 33.8%**, three share **36.0% → 38.7%**.

**Honest correction on the parity claim.** The delivery note said the golden parity was "exactly zero — bit-for-bit." That was true of the **sandbox** and was reported as if general. On Emmett's Windows machine it is 5.55e-17 (pie) / 1.11e-16 (internals). Phase 64 shows the identical pattern (0.000E+000 in-sandbox, 2.776E-017 on Windows) and has since S58 — a pre-existing Linux-vs-Windows `tanh`/`pow` math-library difference, not something S59 introduced, and five orders of magnitude inside the 1e-12 tolerance (which is exactly why the tolerance is not bit-equality). The bit-identity checks that matter — flat-50, kill switch, bypass, Mid-untouched — compare C# against C# and are green on both. Every basketball number in Emmett's run matched the sandbox byte-for-byte (config hash identical, all eight stress buckets, all ten box rows) — the S56 sandbox==Windows finding repeating.

**The standing finding, surfaced before the docs hardened — the gate is NOT level-neutral below rating ~48.** A property of the **locked spec**, not the port (parity is exact): the unlock ramp is anchored at **28→48 in absolute rating points**, but it multiplies a composite that is then compared against a **raw** PerimeterDefense. Above 48 the unlock is maxed and the comparison is honest. Below it, the offense's number is scaled down while the defense's is not — so a **uniformly rated** world, where nobody has an edge on anybody, gets walled anyway: at an all-30 world `DriveTools = 3` vs `perimD = 30` (rim 28% → 18%); at all-40, 24 vs 40 (rim 28% → 23%); at 48+, exactly neutral. This did not surface in the archetype table because every signed-off archetype sits at 44 or above. It bumps into two standing rulings — the **relative engine** (same drama at D3 as D1, because attributes describe identity not absolute quality) and **"D3 is small and unathletic, NOT unskilled — those teams can legitimately score 90–110."** In the stress bench the WeakVsWeak bucket fell 0.787 → 0.758 PPP with rim 26% → 22%. On the actual divvy'd population it is far milder (the 2.5pp shift above), because generated players are not rated in the low 30s the way the synthetic stress roster is — so it may never bite in practice. **Ruled: ship as-is** — the shape is signed off, the kill switch works, and by the page-only calibration principle an anchor/magnitude question waits for a real population. Logged as the **first item for the Pass A tuning pass**; measuring the unlock against a population reference instead of a fixed 28–48 would be a spec change and its own session.

**What this means for the game:** a guard who can't beat his man off the dribble no longer strolls to the rim. Put a lockdown defender on an average creator and he gets pushed out of the paint and into a contested three — his rim share falls, his three share rises, and his mid-range doesn't change, because a denied drive is a jumper from distance, not a pull-up. First step is what beats the man; the handle only buys permission to try (an elite handle with no burst gets walled anyway; a blur with no handle gets walled hardest). A post scorer is completely immune — a perimeter wall doesn't reach the block. A weak defender gives nothing away; he just fails to build the wall. And crucially, this is **where he shoots from, never how well he shoots** — no make% moved. Perimeter defense finally does something on its own instead of only paying next to a rim protector; the S54 finding's other two-thirds (he passed it / the off-ball three) are Passes B and C.

**Next:** Pass B — the post-feed (R5b) and the usage-diffusion item logged in the brief §6.5a: the "he gave it up" outcome the gate deliberately does not model (a denied drive currently always becomes his own contested jumper, never someone else's shot). Then Pass C, the off-ball three lever. The Pass A page-tuning pass carries the unlock-anchor finding above as its first item. The remaining S54 defensive finding (Discipline near-inert — a candidate wiring gap) and the remaining S50 physical questions (the light block channel; Weight cosmetic) are unchanged.

## Session 58 — The live steal-forcing FLOOR SHIPPED (v1): the steal/turnover matchup is now LIVE at a normal defensive setting instead of gated to zero — an athleticism mismatch (primary) + a steal-vs-handle contest + a two-sided perimeter-gated wingspan term, plus a wingspan tilt on who gets credited; the S50 "wingspan→steals unwired" hole is CLOSED (2026-07-14)

**Scope:** The fourth engine change of the wiring arc, closing the **wingspan→steals** hole the S50 physical measurement flagged (design question 3) and the neutral-pressure half of the S52 Steals finding ("claim not creation"). The old steal/turnover matchup multiplied a steal-vs-handling gap by `pressureGate = max(0, pUnit)`, which is **exactly zero** at today's league-wide neutral pressure (Home/Away/Neutral all 5.0) — so the matchup was inert and only the flat lift moved. This session replaces that gated term with a pressure-**independent** floor that is live at neutral. Two shared static helpers on `Matchup` (`StealFloorShift`, `WingStealPerimWeight`), the Roll F (`DisruptionShares`) and Roll B (`TeamDisruptionShares`) doors rewired to call them, the Roll B generator computing two new team aggregates + the perimeter-weighted signed wingspan, a wingspan attribution tilt in `StealerPicker`, 14 knobs on `MatchupConfig` (+ `config.json`), a new **Phase 64** suite check, and the committed oracle + golden fixture. The pressure dial, the pressing/foul channels, the foul share, Roll C's live/dead split, Roll A's press disruption, and Speed/Strength/Vertical were **not** touched. Full CONVENTIONS ritual: fresh pull, every §1 read against live source, all five adversarial assumptions confirmed at the check-in gate, Emmett's explicit go before the first file. Middle-rung pre-check taken: SDK from the Ubuntu feed, tree compiled clean, full suite ran green in-sandbox before delivery.

**What shipped (the locked spec).** The steal/turnover disruption shift is now `stealFloorShift + pressureLift + hustlePressureNudge` (pressureLift is 0 at neutral, kept for the future coaching layer; the old `pressureGate × matchupShift` is gone). `StealFloorShift` sums three defender-minus-offense gaps:
- **Athleticism mismatch (PRIMARY).** `GapFn((Quickness+FirstStep)/2 gap, AthStealSteepness 0.85, exp 1.4, scale 25)` — the steepest of the three (steepness 0.85 vs the steal term's 0.38 at the same exponent/scale, a ~2.24× ratio, so athleticism dominates by construction at every gap). A quicker, faster-off-the-floor defender forces the ball loose.
- **Steal-vs-ball-control (secondary).** `GapFn(Steals − BallHandling, StealFloorSteepness 0.38, exp 1.4, ReferenceScale 25)` — the ball-hawk-vs-handle contest, now live at neutral instead of pressure-gated to nothing.
- **Wingspan deflection (two-sided, on top).** `WingStealWeight 0.45 × tanh(wingSigned / WingStealScale 22)`, where `wingSigned = (Wingspan − 50) × perimW`. Long arms add, short arms cost a little (two-sided, unlike the one-sided height make term). **Perimeter-gated:** `perimW` slides from 1.0 for a guard down to `WingStealPerimFloor 0.20` for a big, on `Matchup.Postness` (Height/PostDefense/Strength — reads no Wingspan, so it is not circular), pivot 50 over range 28. So a rangy guard's arms bother the ball; a short-armed seven-footer's length barely enters (he is not out there poking at the handle).

In Roll B the same three inputs are the guard-heavy slot-weighted aggregates (the touch-weighting already tilts toward the players who handle the ball, so a non-handling center barely enters the resistance side, and the perimeter weight is applied per-defender *inside* the aggregate before averaging). **Attribution tilt (`StealerPicker`):** on top of the existing Steals × perimeter × Hustle weight, a slight two-sided wingspan factor `1 + WingspanStealerSteepness 0.15 × tanh((Wingspan − 50)/20)` — longer arms earn a slightly larger slice of the credited steals, but the guard-favoring postness gate still dominates (a long-armed big gets fewer than a long-armed guard). Provisional magnitudes (SHAPE signed off on the archetype table; numbers tuned later on the season page).

**The anchors and kill switches fall out for free.** Setting `AthStealSteepness`, `StealFloorSteepness`, and `WingStealWeight` all to 0 is the kill switch: an S57-style identity branch in both doors reproduces today's exact pressure-gated expression byte-for-byte (no GapFns on the floor, no `0 × tanh`, no re-associated sum), so a kill-switched config reproduces the current neutral behavior to the bit. The `WingspanStealerSteepness = 0` path likewise runs today's exact two-factor picker weight with no `×1` wingspan factor.

**The one call beyond the check-in plan, surfaced at delivery.** An old suite assertion — Phase 12 sub-check (c), "pressure gates the matchup: high-pressure delta ≫ low-pressure delta" — tested the *retired* pressure-gated behavior and went red exactly as the §A1 audit predicted (a pressure sweep of the matchup legitimately differs now). It was reconciled in place to test the **new** design: the matchup is a live floor at neutral (a butterfingers-vs-ballhawk lineup swings the turnover share ~9.5pp at a normal defensive setting, where the old model gave ≈0) and is no longer amplified by pressure. This went slightly beyond the plan Emmett approved at the gate; it was flagged prominently as a reversible call, justified because §A1 sanctioned the divergence and full-suite green is the commit gate. No other prior test moved.

**Validation — green on Emmett's machine, zero-diff golden, one reconciled test, zero other drift.** The new **Phase 64** check, all 26 assertions OK: (1) **golden parity** — 18 cases (12 signed-off archetypes + 6 boundary rows pinning the continuous perimeter gate: pivot / mid / range / both clamps / wing-ref-zero) at |Δ| ≤ 1e-12 on the shift, postness, AND perimeter weight, params cross-checked against live config; worst shift diff 2.8e-17, worst postness diff 7.1e-15 (the oracle's `/3.0` postness vs the C# weighted-sum — safely under 1e-12, flagged at the gate); (2) **floor shape** — live at neutral (quick/long vs plodder shift 3.37 > 0), elite handler resists (0.71 < 3.37), wingspan two-sided (long guard +0.42, short guard −0.19) and perimeter-gated (short big −0.04, barely moves); (3) **athleticism primary** at gaps 10/20/40 (ath GapFn > steal GapFn at every gap, not merely archetype ordering); (4) **kill switch** = today's flat baseline at neutral AND floor-on moves the share (0.174 vs 0.05); (5) **credited steals rise** — expected credited steals = turnover share × Roll C's live-ball fraction (0.50), quick/long 0.087 > flat-50 0.025 per turnover-routed possession; (6) **attribution tilt** via a seeded 400k `StealerPicker` batch (long-armed guard 0.221 > short-armed 0.188; long-armed big 0.123 < long-armed guard — the postness gate still dominates); (7) **foul path independent** — the raw `finalFoulShare` is bit-identical across an athleticism/wingspan walk (no new attribute enters the foul calc); (8) **config guards** — 12 throw cases + the all-off kill switch loading. The oracle reproduced the signed archetype table exactly, and the compiled tree reproduced all 18 golden cases in-sandbox at literal zero shift diff. On Emmett's machine: `ALL CHECKS PASSED`, Phase 12 green (reconciled (c)), 4,000-game stress test reconciled, observation run all OK — team turnovers land ~12.8/game (not runaway) and the credited-steal skew is exactly as intended (guards ~1.5–2.0 STL, bigs ~0.5–0.6).

**What this means for the game:** ball pressure finally reads at a *normal* defensive setting, not only when a coach dials up a press. A quick, long-armed guard now forces turnovers against a shaky ball-handler even in a base defense, the steals he creates get credited toward him and his rangy teammates (not the centers), and a slow, short-armed defender forces almost none. Athleticism is the biggest lever, the steal rating adds to it, and wingspan is a two-sided tilt on top — perimeter-gated so a giant's arms only matter when he's actually out guarding the ball. A league-average defender at neutral plays as before, and turning the three floor knobs to zero restores today's numbers exactly. The catch worth remembering (it's in the status board): the *turnover-forcing* side of Steals that S52 parked to the coaching layer is now partly live at neutral through this floor — but the pressure **dial** itself is still unbuilt, so a coach cannot yet crank a full-court press; that stays scoped to the coaching layer.

**Next:** the wiring track continues — the remaining S54 defensive findings (perimeter-defense point-neutrality without a rim deterrent; Discipline near-inert, a candidate wiring gap) and the remaining S50 physical questions (the light block channel; Weight cosmetic). The pressure/coaching layer — which would let a dialed-up press drive the *forced* turnover side the rest of the way, and let BallHandling's protection channel and Steals' full forcing side come alive — stays the largest parked prerequisite.

## Session 57 — PostMoves interior self-creation SHIPPED (v1): a high-post player now HUNTS interior shots (diet tilt), HOLDS his interior spot under pressure (resistance), and his post buckets are credited as assisted LESS — scaled by his teammates' passing (assist discount); the S51 no-post-hunt diet gap is CLOSED, three wires, zero make% touched (2026-07-14)

**Scope:** The third engine change of the wiring arc, closing the **no-post-hunt diet gap** the S51 interior-offense measurement opened. Three wires, all reading the shooter's `PostMoves`, all anchored at 50 and upside-only (≤ 50 is exact identity): a **diet tilt** and a **pressure resistance** in Roll G, and an **assist discount** at the Resolver's assist site. Two spans added to `RollGConfig` + four knobs to `MatchupConfig` (+ `config.json`), two pure static helpers on `RollGGenerator`, one `PostAssistFactor` method + its Load guards on `MatchupConfig`, one surgical branch at the assist emitter, a new **Phase 63** suite check, and the committed oracle + golden fixture. `Matchup.OffenseRating` / the make door, Mid/Long/Three diet, the committer picker, and the pressure/coaching layer were **not** touched. Full CONVENTIONS ritual: fresh pull, every §1 read against live source, all five adversarial assumptions re-confirmed at the check-in gate (one placement call surfaced there — the diet tilt sits after `CoachingPull.Apply`, which is *below* the fast-break early-return, so a transition possession never post-hunts; Emmett's "unless it's in transition" instinct was already satisfied by construction). The gate held for Emmett's explicit go before the first file. Middle-rung pre-check taken: SDK from the Ubuntu feed, tree compiled clean, full suite ran green in-sandbox before delivery.

**What shipped (the locked spec).** Shared lift: `postLift = max(0, (PostMoves − 50) / 49)` (0 at ≤ 50, 1 at 99).
- **Diet tilt (Roll G, `TiltInteriorDiet`).** The coached Rim + Short tendency shares are multiplied by the SAME factor `1 + PostDietSpan · postLift` (authored Rim:Short ratio preserved), then all five renormalize — so interior weight rises and Mid/Long/Three shed share only proportionally. Sits on the coached vector BEFORE the matchup bend, so it flows through displacement naturally and **never calls `OffenseRating` → make% is untouched**. Multiplicative: a zero authored Rim or Short stays zero (it amplifies existing interior intent, never invents a post game). Placed after `CoachingPull.Apply`, feeding BOTH the zero-defender fallback and the normal path; transition already returned above it.
- **Pressure resistance (Roll G, `ResistPressureShift`).** When the bent-dominant zone is interior (Rim/Short), the requested usage-pressure diet shift is scaled by `1 − PostPressureResistanceSpan · postLift` — a strong post man is harder to shove off his spot. Shrinks the *requested shift* (which lowers `absorbed`), **never the intrinsicCapacity cap**; the [0,1] span bound keeps the factor in [0,1] so mass is never added back onto the dominant zone.
- **Assist discount (Resolver, `MatchupConfig.PostAssistFactor`).** A passing-scaled discount on the Rim + Short assisted rate: `dampPass(pf) = DampFloor + (1 − DampFloor)·clamp((PfHi − pf)/(PfHi − PfLo), 0, 1)`; `postFactor = 1 − PostAssistSpan · postLift · dampPass`; `assistProb = clamp(zoneBase · pf · postFactor, Floor, Ceiling)`. His post buckets are credited as assisted **less** often, and *how much* less depends on his teammates' passing — **most** self-created next to a pass-dead lineup (`dampPass → 1`), **least** beside elite passers (`dampPass → DampFloor`). Mid/Long/Three never discounted. Provisional magnitudes (shape locked, tuned later on the season page): DietSpan 0.5, ResistanceSpan 0.5, AssistSpan 0.5, DampFloor 0.25, PfLo 0.75, PfHi 1.25.

**The anchors and kill switches fall out for free.** `PostMoves = 50` reproduces today to the bit on all three wires (postLift 0 → helpers return their inputs unchanged, `PostAssistFactor` returns exactly 1.0). Each span at 0 is a clean kill switch, byte-identical on its path. The assist site branches on `postFactor == 1.0` so the identity path runs today's exact two-factor expression with **no ×1 reassociation** — the kill switch is bit-exact, not merely tolerance-close.

**The one interaction, surfaced honestly.** The Phase 9 shot-location door builds an "all-attributes-75" test shooter — so his PostMoves is 75, and the new interior hunt correctly fired, lifting his rim share above raw tendencies (rim 50.0 → 52.7%, tripping the 2pp tolerance). That case exists to prove *matchup-gap* cancellation, and PostMoves is not a matchup-gap attribute — it's a standalone diet-hunt input — so the fix pinned that one test shooter's PostMoves to its 50 anchor (a `postM` override on the local `Mk`), isolating what the case means to measure. Real players untouched; the case now reads rim 50.0 → 50.0, diff 0.0%. This is the expected "a new wire legitimately shifts a prior anchor's premise → update the anchor, not weaken the wire" pattern (the S55 height term did the same to the S50 finding).

**Validation — green on Emmett's machine, zero-diff parity, zero suite drift.** The new **Phase 63** check, all 30 assertions OK: (1) per-zone make% **leak guard** — `EffectiveRating(Rim)` and `(Short)` bit-identical as PostMoves walks 0→99 (proof the diet tilt never leaked through `OffenseRating`); (2) **assist golden parity** — 30 rows (2 zones × 5 PostMoves × 3 passing factors) at |Δ| ≤ 1e-12, **worst 0.0e0**, params cross-checked against live config, every discounted prob inside [Floor, Ceiling]; (3) anchors + three kill switches **exact-bit**; (4) diet locked-shape invariants on the pure helper (interior share rises monotonically, Rim:Short ratio preserved, zero stays zero, Mid/Long/Three shed proportionally) **plus an end-to-end wire check** (final-pie interior share rises with PostMoves under real pressure: 0.280 → 0.404 → 0.447); (5) resistance monotonicity on the intermediate absorbed (0.160 → 0.103 → 0.080 across PM 50/85/99, no effect perimeter-dominant or at zero pressure); (6) assist interaction + zone gate (discount largest at weak passing, factors 0.670 < 0.777 < 0.884; PM ≤ 50 unchanged; Mid/Long/Three factor 1.0 at every rating); (7) config guards — eight throw cases + every span 0 loading. The oracle reproduced the approved archetype table exactly (Rim 60 → 34.9/45.0/55.8, 85 → 25.8/37.4/51.0, 99 → 25.0/33.1/48.4; Short floor-saturating where the table shows it), and the compiled tree reproduced all 30 golden cases at literal zero diff in-sandbox. On Emmett's machine: `ALL CHECKS PASSED`, observation run and 4,000-game stress test reconciled and unmoved (the flat-50 bench seats PostMoves 50 everywhere → the wires sit at identity, so the aggregates are expected to be unchanged; the feature expresses on a real population with PostMoves spread).

**What this means for the game:** a real post threat now plays like one — he hunts his spots inside (more Rim/Short attempts, none of it fake FG%), he's harder to bump off the block when the defense loads up, and his post buckets read as self-created rather than assisted, the more so the weaker his team's passing. A league-average post rating (50) changes nothing. The one thing to remember (it's in the brief): the flat-50 lab bench can't show any of this — every bench player sits at PostMoves 50, the exact identity point — so the proof is the golden parity and the end-to-end interior-share climb, not a bench delta.

**Next:** the wiring track continues — the **ball-dominance/initiation layer** (the S49 reshaper, the interior analog of which this session just closed), then the S54 defensive findings (perimeter-defense point-neutrality; Discipline near-inert) and the remaining S50 physical questions. Two smaller PostMoves-adjacent notes are logged, not scheduled: the SelfCreation *perimeter* assist discount (this session did interior only — the perimeter analog is its own gap), and magnitude calibration of all three spans against a real population.
