## Session 56 — The unforced-turnover channel SHIPPED (v1): handling now moves the neutral turnover base — a shared fractional curve on Roll B (team) + Roll F (individual), anchored at 50, with a SpanFrac=0 kill switch; and the honest finding that it FLATTENS the S49 inversion rather than fully flipping it (2026-07-13)

**Scope:** The second engine change of the wiring arc, and the first of the three S49-surfaced turnover gaps. One shared pure function added to `Matchup`, its four constants to `MatchupConfig` + `config.json`, two surgical one-line edits at the Roll B and Roll F turnover base, a new Phase 62 suite check, and the committed oracle + golden fixture. The committer picker, the forced/pressure matchup math, `actionMass`, and Rolls A/K were **not** touched. Full CONVENTIONS ritual: fresh pull, every §1 read against live source, all six adversarial assumptions re-confirmed at the check-in gate (one prompt divergence flagged there — the named design record `docs/unforced-turnover-brief.md` did not yet exist; Emmett ruled create-it), the gate held for Emmett's explicit go before the first file. Middle-rung pre-check taken: the SDK installed from the Ubuntu feed, the tree compiled clean, and the full suite ran green in-sandbox before delivery.

**What shipped (the locked spec).** A dimensionless factor `g(handling)` that multiplies each door's own **flat** neutral turnover base share — Roll B by the slot-weighted team BallHandling aggregate, Roll F by the named handler's own BallHandling. `lift(h) = (1 − tanh((h − Mid) / Scale)) / 2`; `g = 1 + SpanFrac × (lift(h) − lift(50))`, clamped at `FloorFrac`. Constants (locked shape, provisional magnitudes): Mid 55, Scale 18, SpanFrac 0.443, FloorFrac 0.72. Two anchors fall out for free — `g(50) = 1` for any span (a league-average handler reproduces today's rate to the bit), and `g ≡ 1` for every rating at SpanFrac 0 (a clean kill switch, byte-identical on the turnover path). **One continuous curve, not one-sided:** bad hands raise the base (g(20) ≈ 1.15), good hands lower it (g(99) ≈ 0.72), pivoting at 50. **Diminishing returns above ~80** (Emmett's ruling — 50→70 moves g ~0.21; 85→99 only ~0.012). **The elite floor is the curve's own asymptote (~0.72×), not the clamp** — FloorFrac sits just below the in-range minimum (0.722) so it never fires for an authored 0–99 rating; only an out-of-range rating trips it. **Multiplicative on each door's own base** → proportional and exposure-free on a uniform-handling lineup: one curve, two bases, no allocation choice. `actionMass` is held flat (built from the config constants); only the turnover *numerator* is scaled, and Proceed / ShotAttempt absorbs the change via `1 − toShare − foulShare`, exactly as pressure already does.

**The honest finding — it FLATTENS the S49 inversion, it does not fully FLIP it.** The pure handling effect is now correctly signed and anchored: diffed against the kill switch on the S49 BallHandling walk, the swept player's turnovers rise for bad hands and fall for good hands, pivoting exactly at 50 (elite ≈ −0.5 TO/game, butterfingers ≈ +0.2). But the *absolute* personal-TO count still drifts **up** with handling (≈1.8 → 2.8 across 0→99), where today's engine drifts up harder (≈1.6 → 3.2). The fix **flattens** the inversion (walk slope +1.6 → +1.0), it does not flip it negative — because the dominant personal-TO channel for a high-usage guard is the usage-weighted attribution of team/bad-pass turnovers through the committer picker and Roll C, both deliberately left untouched. The rate is now honest; the attribution still climbs with usage. Fully flipping the count needs the deferred per-event attribution rework (blame following the weaker handle, not raw usage) — out of scope for v1, and the scope wall was right to leave it. The prompt's §F "reversed" headline was optimistic; the delivered truth is *flattened, rate-correct*, surfaced to Emmett before the docs hardened.

**Validation — green on Emmett's machine, zero-diff parity, zero suite drift.** The new **Phase 62** check: (1) 30-case golden parity (2 doors × [7 handlings × 2 spans + 1 out-of-range boundary]) at |Δ| ≤ 1e-12, with the fixture's constants AND its assumed flat base shares (0.030151 B / 0.090452 F) cross-checked against the live config before any case is trusted — **worst diff 0.0e0** on both the factor and the flat-base × factor final share; (2) helper tests — the g(50)=1 anchor at live span, the SpanFrac=0 identity across every rating 0–99, strict monotonic decrease 0→99, the diminishing-returns ruling made testable (85→99 < 50→70), and the floor asymptote-vs-clamp distinction (g(99) strictly above FloorFrac in-range; an out-of-range rating pinned exactly to it); (3) config guards — five throw cases plus SpanFrac=0 loading as the legal kill switch. Pre-checks in the sandbox: the Python oracle's own asserts (anchor, span-0 identity, monotone, diminishing returns, floor, and the exposure-free property on a uniform team) all passed, and the compiled tree reproduced all 30 golden cases at literal zero diff. The suite: every existing check unchanged, observation run and 4,000-game stress test unmoved, `ALL CHECKS PASSED`.

**What this means for the game:** a sure-handed player now protects the ball at a normal defensive setting, not only when pressed — a butterfingers guard coughs it up more, an elite handler less, on one continuous curve that tops out around a 28% reduction and can't drive turnovers to zero (even a 99 makes mistakes). A league-average handler plays exactly as before. The catch worth remembering (in the brief, not just here): because the biggest turnover channel — bad-pass attribution by usage — is untouched, a high-usage star still *shows* a healthy turnover count on the box; the fix corrects the underlying rate, and the visible count fully rights itself only when the per-event attribution layer lands.

**Next:** the remaining wiring track — the no-post-hunt diet gap (S51) and the dormant pressure/coaching layer (which, once live, would let the full turnover-inversion flip land). The ball-dominance/initiation layer stays ruled (S55.1: no separate initiation step — existing rolls approximate it).

## Session 55.1 — The Height/Wingspan sweeps RE-MEASURED against the live post-wire engine: the S55 height-over-defender term shows up exactly as designed, and the S50 "size doesn't score" finding is retired (2026-07-13)

**Scope:** The re-measurement S55 queued and explicitly did not claim — pure config-and-run, **no engine file, no `config.json`, no new sweep config, no Monte Carlo.** The two length walks (`sweep_height.json`, `sweep_wingspan.json`, 0→99 step 5, 2,000 games/rung, slot 5, flat-50 opponent, 42,000 games each) re-run on the live engine that now carries the S55 make-door reach term, diffed against the saved S50 pre-wire curves. Docs only: the attribute-meaning Physical Package section (design question 1 + the generation-redesign feed) and the status board.

**The one honest correction, filed at the check-in gate.** The first read of the pasted output — done before the repo was pulled — matched it against memory of S50 and called it "length barely scores, confirms S50." Wrong baseline: these are the *post-wire* numbers, and the entire reason the walks were queued was to see the S55 term appear. Pulling the source and diffing against the saved curves surfaced the miss before a word was written. The lesson is the standing one (§0 / §2c): diff against the recorded curve read from source, never against memory of a prior session's finding.

**The re-measurement — the term landed exactly as built.** Diffed against the saved S50 curves:
- **Real, one-sided lift.** Height FG% 33.6 → 34.3 → **36.3** (S50: 33.5 → 34.3 → 34.8); Wingspan 33.5 → 34.3 → **36.0** (S50: 33.4 → 34.3 → 34.5). ~+1.5pp added at the 99-rung on each, roughly doubling length's full-range scoring gain (Height +1.3 → +2.7pp, Wingspan +1.1 → +2.5pp).
- **Gated at reach parity.** Below the 50-rung the new curves sit on the pre-wire curves (both 34.3% at 50); the whole +1.5pp lands *above* 50, where the swept player out-reaches the flat-50 opponent — the one-sided design (zero for equal/shorter) visible directly on a live walk.
- **Rim-concentrated, threes flat.** 3P% unmoved on both walks (Height 23.3 → 23.5, Wingspan 23.0 → 22.9) — the Three-zone weight of 0.0 confirmed on real outcomes, not just in the golden fixture; the lift is the two-point zones only.
- **Isolated to scoring.** Rebounds, blocks, steals, and the defensive per-man line (opponent 2P% still falls as the swept player gets taller — Height 39.8 → 36.6) all unchanged from S50. The wire touched the make door and nothing else.

**What this means for the game:** the S50 "length buys almost no scoring" finding is retired. A genuinely taller player now finishes better over a smaller defender — most at the rim, nothing on threes — and the taller he is the more it helps, up to a saturating cap. Whether +1.5pp at the top is *enough* of a reward is a magnitude question — one dial (`MatchupConfig` MaxBonus 15.0), judged later on a real population, not this lab bench. With this measured, the height→skill lean sizing (Pass-2 Phase 3) can be set against real post-wire curves rather than a pending flag.

**Next:** unchanged from S55 — the **ball-dominance/initiation layer** (the S49 reshaper) leads the remaining wiring track.

## Session 55 — The height-over-defender make term SHIPPED (v1): size finally has a scoring wire — one-sided, zone-weighted, saturating reach advantage on the make door; oracle-first, 25-case golden parity at zero diff; and the oracle's stale-curve bug caught and fixed mid-session (2026-07-13)

**Scope:** The **first engine change of the wiring arc** — the measurement arc (S47–S53), the undiluted defensive reruns (S54), and the synthesis conversation are behind it. One term added to the make door in `src/Charm.Engine/Core/Matchup.cs`, its constants in `MatchupConfig`, a new Phase 61 suite check, and the committed oracle + golden fixture. Nothing about selection, diet, blocks, fouls, or rebounding moved. Full CONVENTIONS ritual: fresh pull, every §1 read against live source, the check-in gate held (one prompt divergence flagged there, a second mid-build), Emmett's explicit go before the first file.

**What shipped (the locked spec, signed on the Session 54 archetype table).** A fourth shift in `Matchup.EffectiveRating`'s sum — `baseline + skillShift + physicalShift + heightShift` — where `heightShift = HeightZoneWeight(zone) × HeightMaxBonus × tanh(gap / HeightReferenceScale)` and `gap = max(0, shooterReach − defenderReach)`, reach being `(Height + Wingspan) / 2.0` (a deliberate float divide — both are int ratings; the odd-sum 85+88 case is 86.5, never truncated; a single-source `Matchup.Reach` helper owns the read). **One-sided by design:** it rewards the taller shooter and is exactly zero for the equal or shorter one — defensive length already erases shots through the block channel; the symmetric negative side is a parked v2 call. **Deliberately not `LengthRating`** (which folds in Vertical for the block door); Vertical-in-reach is parked. Constants all in `MatchupConfig`, all tunable: MaxBonus 15.0, ReferenceScale 18.0, zone weights Rim 1.0 / Short 0.8 / Mid 0.3 / Long 0.05 / Three 0.0. Load validation is **range-only** (MaxBonus ≥ 0 with 0 a legal kill switch; ReferenceScale > 0; each weight in [0,1]) — no monotonic-zone enforcement, so era experiments can reshape the profile without fighting the loader. Because the 4-arg `EffectiveRating` delegates to the 6-arg body, one insertion covers **both make doors** — the primary shot and the **putback** (a taller rebounder now converts putbacks over a smaller defender better; a named second behavior change, not a leak). The null-defender fallbacks on both doors skip `EffectiveRating` entirely, so the term is naturally absent with no defender. `config.json` untouched — the loader tolerates missing keys and the auto-property defaults apply.

**The mid-build catch — the oracle was built against a stale make-curve (Emmett-ruled fix: regenerate against live).** The signed oracle's per-zone curve used the `RollHConfig.cs` **code defaults** — but the live `config.json` carries the **recentered midpoints** (the S31+ arc: Rim 68.76 / Short 75.93 / Mid 90.32 / Long 99.34 / Three 106.57 vs the defaults' 43.98 / 42.34 / 42.34 / 59.58 / 60.60; floors, ceilings, and K identical). The term itself was never wrong — it lives in the *rating*, upstream of whichever curve follows — and the scoring boost Emmett signed survives nearly intact under the live curve (BIG_ON_GUARD rim +5.45pp signed → +5.04pp live; TALLER_CENTER +3.05 → +3.00; TALL_WING +3.97 → +3.94; everything within ~0.4pp). But the signed table's *absolute* make% column read ~9 points high versus what the live engine produces, and a faithful C# port would have "failed" golden parity at 1e-9 against a fixture that wasn't the engine's reality. Ruled with Emmett: regenerate the oracle's curve block from the live config and re-emit the golden. The oracle file now names the live source and the bug. Lesson filed under §2c: an oracle's environment constants are load-bearing claims — read them from the live config at draft time, never from code defaults.

**A second prompt divergence, flagged at the gate:** the prompt classed `AthleticismExperiment`, `DefenderExperiment`, and `PutbackConversionExperiment` as Class 2 ("real bodies, will move"). The source says all three seat `Height = Wingspan = 50` on **both** sides — equal reach, zero shift, **Class 1 byte-identical**. That sharpened the test: any movement there would have been a leak. The real Class 2/3 movers are `SizeExperiment` and the `sweep` bench when walking Height or Wingspan — neither runs in the default suite. Also corrected: goldens live **flat in `tools/`** (the displacement/fastbreak/tendency convention), not the prompt's `tools/oracle/`; the csproj copy entry and the check's load path follow the convention.

**Validation — green on Emmett's machine, zero-diff parity, zero suite drift.** The new **Phase 61** check: (1) 25-case golden parity (5 archetypes × 5 zones including Long — the only case that proves `HeightWeightLong` and its accessor branch are wired) at dual tolerance, |rating| ≤ 1e-6 AND |make%| ≤ 1e-9, with the fixture's constants cross-checked against the loaded config before any case is trusted — **worst diff 0.0e0 on both**; the exact-zero set (POST_VS_POST every zone, SMALL_ON_BIG every zone, Three every archetype — 13 cases) exact, on the height *contribution*, never the total rating (SMALL_ON_BIG legitimately sits at 61.5 from its athletic edge); (2) helper tests — reach incl. the odd-sum 86.5 integer-divide guard, the one-sided clamp (positive/zero/negative), zone ordering Rim > Short > Mid > Long > 0 with Three exactly 0, tanh saturation strictly below the cap; (3) config guards — five throw cases plus **MaxBonus = 0 loads and zeroes the shift at every zone** (the kill switch proven, not just permitted). Players in the parity check are built from raw bodies carried **in the fixture** (emitted by the oracle), never hand-typed. Pre-checks in the sandbox: a full-precision Python mirror of the exact C# path fed the live config reproduced all 25 golden cases at literal zero diff before delivery; brace balance and stale-ref greps clean. The suite: **every existing check unchanged** — the FatigueAthleticism 6-arg==4-arg fresh anchor still bit-exact (equal reach and zone Three, doubly zero), the three equal-reach experiments byte-identical as predicted, Phases 56–60 untouched, observation run and stress test unmoved (all archetype rosters seat matched bodies within each matchup class), `ALL CHECKS PASSED`.

**What this means for the game:** a legitimately taller player now scores better over a smaller defender — most at the rim, fading through short and mid, a whisper at long twos, and not at all on threes — with the advantage saturating so an extreme mismatch approaches but never exceeds the cap. Size now compounds through five wires: block-avoidance, putback access, the physical-gap shift, gravity, and this term. That compounding is the named **post-build population watch** (journal, not this build): on a real population, watch centers' rim/short efficiency by height band, tall guards vs guard defenders, putback conversion by reach gap, and whether high-reach / low-Finishing players over-convert (they shouldn't — this is a rating shift, so a weak finisher still passes through his ordinary make curve). Also queued: **re-measure the Height and Wingspan sweeps** and diff against the saved S50 curves — the S50 "size doesn't score" finding is superseded by this wire, but the new curve is *not yet measured*; the attribute-meaning update marks it superseded-pending-re-measurement, claiming no numbers that don't exist.

**Parked from this session's scope wall:** the symmetric negative side; Vertical-in-reach; per-zone reference scales. **Next:** the remaining wiring track from the synthesis — the **ball-dominance/initiation layer** (the S49 reshaper, the highest-value design conversation of the pass) leads it.

## Session 54 — The defensive per-man readout + lineup-stack bench (harness-only instrument upgrade): the four diluted defensive walks measured UNDILUTED, and two real findings fall out — perimeter defense is point-neutral without a rim deterrent, and Discipline is near-inert even on the man it guards (2026-07-12)

**Scope:** An S47-shaped **instrument upgrade** — it changed the sweep **readout** and the sweep **team builder**, both in `src/Charm.Harness`; **no engine file, no `config.json`, no Monte Carlo.** Every number still comes from the same trusted `AttributeGame` attribution the box score already uses. Two changes: (1) a **per-man readout** — Team B's five slots each printed as their own shooting line (FGA, FG%, 3PA, 3P%, 2P%, FTA, FTr), read from the per-slot box indices (5–9) already collected but never printed, so it needed **zero new stat plumbing**; (2) **multi-slot dialing** — a per-slot dial map so one bench team can max any subset of its five slots, generalizing the old single-swept-slot builder. This session exists to **reopen part of "arc complete":** Family G (S52) and Family H (S53) both logged the same honest gap — the on-ball "guard-your-man" ratings and Discipline read as whispers on the team scoreboard because the swept defender guards only ~1/5 of the opponent's shots and the readout only printed team aggregates. That dilution is an **instrument artifact, not the ratings' meaning.** S54 builds the instrument that reads them undiluted, reruns the four diluted walks through it, and adds lineup stacks. **The synthesis pass now follows this session** (it must not read the whispered numbers as the ratings' meaning). Full CONVENTIONS ritual: fresh pull, both changes' as-is wiring re-verified line-by-line, A1–A4 attacked at the gate, the ladders + BALANCED_DEFENSE/SIEVE_5 presented as an archetype table with per-rating predicted movement, Emmett's explicit go before the first file.

**The build was small because the data already existed.** The box loop already copied all ten slots (0–4 Team A, 5–9 Team B) for every shooting field — it simply never printed Team B's five. So the per-man block is a pure new print/CSV addition reading arrays that were already reconciled by `AttributeGame`; the reconciliation (Σ per-slot + the unattributed bucket = team total for FGA/3PA/3PM/FTA) is the same one the Observation run already asserts. The multi-slot builder replaced `BuildSweepTeam(dials, sweptSlot)` with `BuildSweepTeam(perSlotMap)`; a walk or a legacy `dials` case resolves to a one-entry map, so every prior config builds byte-identically.

**The equivalence gate passed byte-for-byte — Change 2 is proven safe.** The two equivalence configs (`equiv_legacy` with `sweptSlot:1 + dials{PerimeterDefense:99}` vs `equiv_slotmap` with `slotDials:{"1":{PerimeterDefense:99}}`) produced **identical output on every line** — same team totals, same five per-man lines. The new per-slot dial map builds teams exactly like the legacy single-slot path. The regression also held: existing tables and CSV columns unchanged, only the new per-man block/columns appended; the flat control reproduced the S52/S53 anchor to the digit (A 52.8 / B 52.9; the covered man 12.8 FGA / 36.1 FG% / 39.3 2P%).

**Finding 1 — the four diluted walks, read undiluted, confirm the per-rating split exactly (A3).** On the covered man's own line: **PerimeterDefense** holds his volume flat (12.8 FGA the whole 0→99 walk) and drops his efficiency (FG 37.8→34.9, 3P 29.5→19.4) — an on-ball contest that moves no touches. **RimProtection** the same shape (volume flat, 2P% 40.5→36.7, threes untouched) — it kills interior makes, not volume. **PostDefense** is the one that takes **both** — his volume falls (13.7→12.0 FGA) *and* his efficiency (2P% 41.2→37.1) — because it is a denial rating that redistributes touches (the S52 postness/denial channel), with the same big side effects (his DRB 4.8→6.3, opponent steals dry up). Each was a whisper on the team scoreboard and a clear signal on the man's own line — exactly the dilution the session was built to undo.

**Finding 2 — Discipline is near-inert even undiluted (the read S53 could not make, now made).** Walked 0→99 on the covered man's own line, his free-throw attempts barely move — **3.7 → 3.6 across the entire walk** — and nothing else moves at all. S53 could only bound Discipline arithmetically because there was no Team B FTA column; now there is one, and the honest answer is that as currently wired Discipline does almost nothing to the man you guard. This is a candidate **wiring gap**, not a measurement artifact — logged for synthesis, nothing touched.

**Finding 3 — perimeter defense is point-neutral without a rim deterrent (the session's real design result).** The perimeter stack (1→2→3→5 slots maxed) confirmed the mechanism and surfaced something bigger. The opponent's shot-diet shift strengthens then **saturates after three slots** (Team B three-share 20.4 → 19.2 → 17.7 → 16.8 → 16.8; rim-share 28.8 → 33.0), and **uncovered men never gain volume** (slots 3–5 hold 12.1 / 10.7 / 10.6 FGA at every rung — the offense does not hunt the on-ball mismatch). **But Team B's points barely move and even tick up mid-ladder** (52.9 → 52.8 → 53.2 → 53.3 → 52.5). The reading: perimeter defense alone pushes the opponent off the three and into higher-percentage twos, and it nets out even — you trade a ~33% three for a better-odds inside shot. **Perimeter pressure only pays when a rim deterrent is waiting to punish the shots you funnel inside.** That is precisely why the balanced defense works and a pure perimeter wall does not.

**Finding 4 — help defense compounds cleanly; a real, sensibly-built defense is worth ~10.5 points.** The help stack lowers the make itself rather than relocating the shot, so it compounds **roughly linearly** with no point-neutral problem: B.PTS 52.9 → 52.3 → 51.6 → 50.9 → **49.5** at five helpers, covered men's interior FG% falling every rung (slot 4: 34.2 → 30.7). The BALANCED_DEFENSE / SIEVE_5 bookend gives the headline number: **BALANCED_DEFENSE** (two lockdown POA + a rim protector + a help anchor who also denies off-ball) holds Team B to **50.5** (covered men into the low 30s, three-share 18.6%); **SIEVE_5** (all six defensive ratings at 10 on all five) bleeds **61.0** (everyone ~42% from everywhere). **A real defense is worth roughly −10.5 opponent points against a sieve** — undiluted, and now readable man-by-man.

**A pre-existing bench property, now visible for the first time: the flat-50 usage gradient.** With the per-man block, the five flat-50 Team B men are **not identical** — guards (slots 1–2) take ~12.8 shots, bigs (slots 4–5) ~10.6, with free-throw attempts following. This is a property of the bench's usage/tendency curve, not anything S54 introduced; it is simply the first time the per-man surface exposed it. Practical rule for reading every ladder: compare each man to **his own flat-50 line**, never to the other men. Flagged for synthesis; not a bug.

**The primary-shot caveat on the per-man surface (A2).** The per-man line is the **mirror-slot opponent's** line — his defender on his primary shots is his mirror, and his putbacks (which he shoots as the rebounder) are also contested by his mirror, so the surface is clean in that sense; but it **includes all attributed attempts**, and a putback reads rim-protection rather than the swept perimeter rating, so a perimeter walk's covered-man line carries a small putback dilution. Labeled in the readout ("primary-matchup proxy; includes all attributed attempts"). Isolating his rim shooting specifically would need an engine-record expansion (per-slot-per-zone emission) and stays **out of scope** (A4).

**The generation-redesign / synthesis feed (what changed for the arc).** Four defensive reads move from "measured, diluted to a whisper" to **measured undiluted**: PerimeterDefense (on-ball contest, volume-flat, ~3pp FG% / ~10pp three on the covered man, point-neutral at team scale), PostDefense (denial rating — takes both volume and efficiency), RimProtection (interior-make suppression + the S52 second-chance channel), and Discipline (near-inert on the covered man). Two findings join the synthesis notes with evidence: **perimeter defense is point-neutral without a rim deterrent** (a genuine engine insight — do not size perimeter-defense value in isolation; it is a diet-shaper that pays only alongside rim protection), and **Discipline is a candidate wiring gap** (real per-man effect below even the undiluted instrument's floor). The instrument itself is now a permanent capability: any future family or coaching-layer question can read per-man lines and dial multi-slot lineup stacks.

**Carried flags, unchanged:** the S48 FTA micro-flag, the 3P%-at-rating-0 watch, the parked FT-curve line, the parked spacing/passing-conversion team-composition test, the S49 reshapers (ball-dominance layer, unforced-turnover channel), BallHandling's pressure-dialed prerequisite, the S50 design bundle (height-over-defender make term — still the one that most gates the height→skill lean sizing; light block channel; wingspan→steals unwired; Weight-cosmetic), the S51 no-post-hunt diet gap, the S52 parked items (PostDefense-as-size → synthesis; Steals turnover-forcing → coaching), the time-sliced fatigue bench, the JumpBall tip counter, the per-opponent-slot Discipline foul-suppression measurement (S53). Newly logged for synthesis: **perimeter-defense point-neutrality without a rim deterrent**; **Discipline near-inert even undiluted (candidate wiring gap)**; the **flat-50 usage gradient** now visible per-man. No new engine gaps opened by the instrument itself.

**Validation:** the two harness changes reasoned + hand-traced (no matchup math moved, so no Monte Carlo per CONVENTIONS §2); build green on Emmett's machine; the equivalence gate byte-identical; all runs green (the four walk reruns 168,000 games + the flat baseline + the two ladders + BALANCED/SIEVE + the equivalence pair ≈ 197,000 games); the full validation suite green as the commit gate (only harness readout/builder changed + sweep JSONs added — the suite is untouched). Next: **the synthesis pass** — read the completed `attribute-meaning.md` end-to-end (now including the undiluted defensive reads) before any engine work is scheduled (Emmett's S49 standing ruling).

## Session 53 — Cognition measured (Family H: BasketballIQ, Discipline): BasketballIQ is a perimeter make-finisher plus a small assist claim, Discipline is a real-but-diluted foul-avoidance tap — and the measurement arc is COMPLETE (config-and-run; engine untouched) (2026-07-12)

**Scope:** The sixth and final family through the S47 full-box ruler, and the smallest — **Family H, Cognition: BasketballIQ and Discipline.** Two isolation walks (0→99 in 5-point steps, 2,000 games/rung, everything else frozen at 50, slot 1) plus a seven-row interaction block — **98,000 real games**. Three text configs in `tools/sweep/`; **no engine file, no `config.json`, no readout change, no Monte Carlo** (zero engine math moved). Full CONVENTIONS ritual: fresh pull, the Family H wiring map re-verified line-by-line, assumptions #1–#6 resolved at the gate, the two walks and seven rows presented as an archetype table with predicted movement, Emmett's explicit go before the first file. **After this session, every rating on the Player has been walked through the ruler — the next session is the synthesis pass, not a family.**

**Slot 1, one block; the anchor held exactly.** The two ratings live on opposite surfaces — BasketballIQ an offensive read on the swept player's own box, Discipline a defensive read on the man he guards — but both ride slot 1 (the make bonus zone-weights toward the perimeter a guard seat exercises well; Discipline reads the same at any slot on a flat opponent; and slot 1 continues the S49 creation anchor and the floor-general archetypes). No slot-5 block — Cognition has no physical term, so there is no body×rating compound to defer. FLAT_50_CONTROL and both walks' 50-rungs reproduced **11.6 PTS / 35.5 FG% / 21.7% use / 1.5 AST / 2.6 TO**.

**The check-in audit confirmed the wiring map with two divergences from the draft prompt, both flagged before building and both resolved as whisper-scale by the data.** (1) **BasketballIQ's assist read is not purely "claim" — the same 0.15 coefficient also feeds team assist *rate*.** `AssistWeight` is read twice: by the picker (who gets credited — the claim) and by `LineupPassingFactor` (the lineup-mean drives the team's assisted rate — creation). So team AST does not stay flat by design; it drifts up a whisper (the team assist multiplier moves 0.796 → 0.811 across the full walk, ≈ +0.2 team AST/game). S49 already proved the point empirically — sweeping Passing at the higher 0.5 weight left team FG% dead flat — so "roughly flat" holds; the tiny team-AST tick is this channel, not a bug. (2) **The iqFactor channel does NOT feed the attention-share tilt (RollG/RollE) as the prompt stated** — it routes IQ → effective playmaking → the team's conversion-quality → **Roll H's C4 passing-converter** (a team halfcourt make bonus), and never touches the attention shares (those are gravity + usage, no IQ). Same conclusion (a whisper, ≈ +0.02pp team FG% across the whole walk), different mechanism and a different line to watch. Net: two of BasketballIQ's three reads have small *team-level* tails, not purely own-box — both confirmed as whispers (team points moved only 52.8 → 53.0 on the walk). IqMakeSensitivity confirmed live (0.08) on the bench at the gate.

**Finding 1 — BasketballIQ is a perimeter make-finisher plus a small assist claim, and the IQ-50 gate splits the two cleanly.** The make bonus does exactly what its clamp says: nothing from IQ 0 to 50 (own FG% pinned at 35.5), then a clean rise to **36.6 by IQ 99** (own 3P% **22.2 → 24.1, +1.8pp**), concentrated on the perimeter — the shot mix never moves and there is no rim gain, so it is "a smart player finishes the good look he already had," not more or different shots. The assist read is a genuine *claim* and is the exception to the gate: his own assists rise only **1.3 → 1.7** across the full walk, ungated, drifting up steadily on **both** halves of the range (the assist weight is linear in IQ, not clamped at 50) — the weakest of the three assist inputs by weight, as designed. Own points 11.6 → 11.9. Nothing fired below the IQ-50 knee, no rim bonus appeared, the AST swing never approached a Passing-sized slope — the suspicious list stayed empty.

**Finding 2 — the MAESTRO/IQ_ONLY pair proves the split: passing creates the assists, IQ finishes the shots.** HIGH_IQ_MAESTRO (IQ 95, Passing 85, Playmaking 85) posts **2.3 assists** — the jump comes almost entirely from the elite passing/playmaking. IQ_ONLY (IQ 95, nothing else) moves assists just **+0.2** off control (1.5 → 1.7) — the pure 0.15 claim with no passing skill to distribute. Both rows carry the **same** make-% lift (FG 36.7 vs 36.5, 3P 24.3 vs 23.9) because both have IQ 95. The two IQ effects are orthogonal and separable: elite passing/playmaking does the assist-creating; IQ only claims a slightly bigger slice while independently finishing the perimeter looks.

**Finding 3 — Discipline is wired and real, but below this instrument's resolution at team scale (the honest gap).** The swept player's own box is dead flat across the whole Discipline walk (FG% 35.5–35.6, no curve — correctly, since Discipline is a defensive read with no offensive wire; a monotonic own-FG curve here would have been the trace trigger, and it did not appear). The effect lives on Team B's foul rate, and the readout has no Team B FTA column. From the live parameters, the per-man effect is a source-real whisper: on the man he guards, the shooting-foul rate bends by roughly +0.7pp (Rim) at Discipline 0 down to −0.14pp (Rim) at Discipline 99 — **asymmetric**, because the foul ceiling sits far above the base while the floor is just beneath it, so an undisciplined defender moves more than a disciplined one. Diluted 5:1 to the man he guards, that lands as roughly **−0.02 (Disc 99) to +0.08 (Disc 0) FTA/game** on Team B. **Team B points staying flat at 52.9 is consistent with a whisper of that size — it is not a measurement of one.** Same limitation family as the Family-G on-ball wall and the S51 transition-share gap: the per-man effect is real, the instrument dilutes and hides it. (DISCIPLINED_STOPPER's Team B shot-mix shift — Rim 28.8 → 29.3, 3PA 20.4 → 20.0 — is the PerimeterDefense 80 doing its S52 job, not the Discipline.)

**The interaction block, the rest of it.** DISCIPLINED_STOPPER and UNDISCIPLINED both leave Team B points at 52.9 (the ruled dilution, no FTA column). ALL_H_ELITE (IQ 85, Disc 85) shows the perimeter make lift (36.4 / 23.8) and no visible Discipline effect. H_FLOOR_15 (IQ 15, Disc 15) sits just below control — IQ 15 is below the make gate so make% is already at floor, and the assist claim is at its smallest (1.4 < 1.5).

**Cross-wire checks all clean.** No below-knee IQ efficiency curve, no direct rim make-bonus, no Passing-sized AST swing under IQ, no Team B foul move under BasketballIQ, no real own-FG curve under Discipline — the suspicious list stayed empty across both walks.

**The generation-redesign feed (what the two cognition ratings buy).** BasketballIQ is a small, proportional **perimeter make-finisher on good looks above the midpoint** (own 3P% +1.8pp at the top, nothing at/below IQ 50, nothing at the rim) plus a **minor assist claim** (credits, does not create); its two team-level channels are real but whisper-scale. Size it as a modest efficiency-and-credit rating for perimeter players, not a volume or creation driver. Discipline is a **defender-light foul-avoidance tap** — real per-man, asymmetric (the hack-happy end moves more than the disciplined end), diluted to a whisper at team scale on this instrument; a low-magnitude foul-economy edge, not a scoreboard mover.

**The measurement arc is complete.** Six families — Scoring (S48), Perimeter creation (S49), Physical package (S50), Interior offense (S51), Defense (S52), Cognition (S53) — every rating on the Player walked through the S47 ruler. No family remains. The next session is the **synthesis pass** (Emmett's S49 standing ruling): read the completed `attribute-meaning.md` end-to-end and produce the cross-family reading the generation redesign has been waiting on — the S50 height-over-defender make term (the one that most gates the height→skill lean sizing), the S51 no-post-hunt diet gap, the S52 PostDefense-as-size coupling, and the two S49 reshapers (ball-dominance/initiation, unforced turnovers). The pressure-dialed channels (BallHandling, Steals turnover-forcing) are coaching-layer, scoped out of synthesis.

**Carried flags, unchanged:** the S48 FTA micro-flag, the 3P%-at-rating-0 watch, the parked FT-curve line, the parked spacing/passing-conversion team-composition test, the S49 reshapers (ball-dominance layer, unforced-turnover channel), BallHandling's pressure-dialed prerequisite, the S50 design bundle (height-over-defender make term — still the one that most gates the height→skill lean sizing; light block channel; wingspan→steals unwired; Weight-cosmetic), the S51 no-post-hunt diet gap, the S52 parked items (PostDefense-as-size → synthesis; Steals turnover-forcing → coaching), the time-sliced fatigue bench, the JumpBall tip counter. Newly parked: the per-opponent-slot Discipline foul-suppression measurement (the same instrument gap logged for Family G). No new design gaps opened.

**Validation:** all three runs green on Emmett's machine; the anchor exact; the full validation suite green as the commit gate (only sweep JSONs added — the suite is untouched). Next: **the synthesis pass** — no family remains.

## Session 52 — Defense measured (Family G: PerimeterDefense, PostDefense, RimProtection, Steals, HelpDefense, OffBallDefense): RimProtection is the only guard-your-man rating with a real team effect, Steals is claim-not-creation, and PostDefense mostly turns a player into a big — the family's mirror structure holds (config-and-run; engine untouched) (2026-07-12)

**Scope:** The fifth family through the S47 full-box ruler, and the largest — **Family G, Defense: six ratings.** Six isolation walks (0→99 in 5-point steps, 2,000 games/rung, everything else frozen at 50) plus **two** interaction blocks (a seven-row slot-1 block and a four-row slot-5 interior block) — **274,000 real games**. Eight text configs in `tools/sweep/`; **no engine file, no `config.json`, no readout change, no Monte Carlo** (zero engine math moved). Full CONVENTIONS ritual: fresh pull, the Family G wiring map re-verified line-by-line, assumptions #1–#6 resolved at the gate, both blocks presented as archetype tables with predicted movement, Emmett's explicit go before the first file.

**The family is structurally the mirror of A–F, and it was measured on two slots.** Every prior family landed the swept player's effect on his own box or his own team's offense; defense lands on **Team B's box** (B.PTS + the CSV's teamB zone FG%). Emmett's S52 ruling: run the six walks + a seven-row block on **slot 1** (reproducing the S49 anchor 11.6 / 35.5 / 21.7% use / 1.5 AST / 2.6 TO — Steals' one live team channel is guard-weighted, and every make-door curve reads just as fully at slot 1 as slot 5 on a flat-50 opponent), plus a four-row interior block on **slot 5** (reproducing the S48/S50/S51 anchor 9.4 / 34.3 / 49.8) where the interior archetypes carry real bodies — the body×interior-defense compound slot 1 cannot show. **Both anchors held exactly.**

**The check-in audit confirmed the wiring map with four real findings, all flagged before building.** (1) **OffBallDefense is not "make-suppression only"** — the retired Phase-46 team squeeze was *replaced* by a per-man denial (`RollEGenerator.cs:320`, OffBallDefense vs OffBallMovement), live in the source but invisible on flat clones; the "no selection path" claim and the suspicious-list line flagging any OffBallDefense selection effect were both corrected before the build. (2) **The PostDefense walk moves his own steals/turnovers/rebounds and none of it is defense** — PostDefense is one-third of `Matchup.Postness` (Height/PostDefense/Strength, equal thirds), so walking it reclassifies him as a big; all three side-effects pre-classified as legitimate before read time. (3) **RimProtection has an undiluted team-scale job the going-in map underweighted — second-chance defense** (`RollKGenerator.cs:92`, putback deterrence weight 0.55; `Matchup.PutbackBlockRate`, a five-defender team stack), so its team read is *not* the whisper the on-ball dilution predicts. (4) **The HelpDefense in-zone number was 1.6pp, not 3.7pp** (the 3.7 was the total at rating 99, not the walk movement; the squared curve front-loads the top rungs) — the team-level band (~0.45–0.6pp) was unchanged and confirmed. Bench pressure confirmed neutral (Home = Away = Neutral = 5.0), so Roll A is the only live Steals team channel and Roll B/F are whispers, exactly as S49's BallHandling mirror predicted.

**Finding 1 — RimProtection is the only guard-your-man rating with a real, readable team effect, because it also does second-chance defense.** The three on-ball "guard-your-man" ratings (Perimeter/Post/RimProtection) all suffer the slot-guards-slot dilution: the swept defender contests only ~1/5 of Team B's shots, so a 99 on the on-ball door barely moves teamB FG%. RimProtection escapes it — beyond the diluted on-ball contest, it deters and blocks **putbacks after an offensive rebound**, a five-defender team read that is not diluted. **B.PTS ran 52.9 → 51.6 (−1.3 full-walk) — the biggest team effect of the six** — with the opponent pushed off the rim (their rim attempt share 28.8 → 27.4) and his own BLK the strongest own-box signal in the family (0.7 → 0.9). This most corrects the going-in expectation: Perimeter/PostDefense's headline job is nearly invisible at team scale on this instrument, RimProtection's is not.

**Finding 2 — PostDefense barely touches the scoreboard, but it is one-third of how the engine decides a player's size.** B.PTS moved just −0.4 across the walk, but the swept player's own box moved hard: **REB 7.7 → 8.7, STL 1.3 → 0.9, TO blame 2.6 → 2.3, usage 21.9% → 21.2%.** None of it is post defense working or failing — raising PostDefense raises his "postness," and the rebound-position, steal-share, and turnover-blame pickers all read postness, so the engine reclassifies him as a big. **Consequence for the generation redesign: a "great post defender" rating currently reads more as "is a big" than "stops post scoring."** Logged for synthesis, nothing wired.

**Finding 3 — Steals is claim, not creation.** The cleanest single curve in the session — own STL 0.1 → 2.1, monotone across all 21 rungs — while **opponent points stayed flat and opponent turnovers did not rise.** The one live team-turnover channel (Roll A, guard-weighted) barely moves at neutral pressure; what the rating buys is a bigger *share* of the team's existing steals (the StealerPicker attribution weight), not more forced turnovers. BALL_HAWK confirms from the archetype side (2.2 personal STL, opponent points unchanged at 52.8). This is the S49 BallHandling finding on the defensive side — the disruption channels are pressure-gated toward zero at neutral, so steal *rating* on this bench is an attribution dial, not a turnover-forcing dial. The turnover-forcing side needs a non-neutral pressure setting; parked to the coaching layer, same as BallHandling's pressure-dialed test.

**Finding 4 — HelpDefense and OffBallDefense are the clean team-suppression pair, symmetric and undiluted.** Both aggregate the four off-ball defenders on nearly every opponent shot, so they escape the slot-guards-slot wall. **HelpDefense suppresses interior makes (B.PTS 52.9 → 52.3, −0.6); OffBallDefense suppresses perimeter makes (52.9 → 52.1, −0.8)** — right in the predicted ~0.45–0.6pp team-FG% band. Neither leaves any footprint on the swept player's own box, exactly as wired. HELP_ANCHOR (both at 90, no on-ball skill) is the marquee clean row at −1.1 opponent points. OffBallDefense's per-man denial channel (Finding 1 of the audit) is live but correctly invisible on flat clones — noted in the completeness ledger, not the retired pile.

**The interaction blocks.** Block A (slot 1): **HELP_ANCHOR** the cleanest team-suppression benchmark (B.PTS 51.8, −1.1, zero on-ball skill); **BALL_HAWK** the claim-vs-create proof (2.2 STL, 8.7 REB, opponent points *unchanged* — he stat-pads, they score the same); **DEFENSIVE_LIABILITY** (all six at 10) lets Team B score 55.0 (+2.1) and nearly vanishes from the box; **ALL_G_ELITE** (all six at 85) worth −2.3 opponent points, the terrible-to-elite swing ~4.4. Block B (slot 5, real bodies): **RIM_PROTECTOR** (RimProt 90 + Height/Wingspan 85) at B.PTS 50.9 (−2.0), BLK 1.2, REB 10.6 — against the bodiless RimProtection-90 walk row (−0.8, 0.9 BLK), the frame adds ~1.2 points and +0.3 blocks, **the body×interior-defense compound real and visible** (the S50 body amplifier on the defensive side); **INTERIOR_WALL** the biggest single-player suppression of the session (B.PTS 50.4, −2.5, BLK 1.3, REB 11.8); **POST_STOPPER** −0.7 with big glass from the body plus the postness reclassification.

**Cross-wire checks all clean.** No steals under RimProtection, no blocks under Steals, no monotonic suppression curve at a zero-weight zone, no real usage/efficiency curve on the swept player's own offense under any defensive rating — the suspicious list stayed empty across all six walks.

**The generation-redesign feed (what the six defensive ratings buy).** RimProtection is the one guard-your-man rating with a real readable team effect (via second-chance defense), and it compounds with the body. HelpDefense + OffBallDefense are the clean undiluted team-suppression pair (interior vs perimeter, no personal footprint). Steals is an attribution dial at neutral pressure (claim, not creation). PerimeterDefense + PostDefense do their headline job real but diluted to a whisper at team scale — their clean reads are the block column and (Perimeter) the opponent's diet reshape; PostDefense additionally moves size classification more than opponent scoring. One full defender ≈ −2.3 opponent points, one interior anchor ≈ −2.5 — real and clean at the archetype level even though two of the six ratings' headline jobs are diluted at the walk level.

**Design-bundle feed this measurement adds (logged with evidence, nothing touched).** The **PostDefense-as-size coupling** joins the synthesis notes (a post-defense rating currently reads more as "is a big" than "stops post scoring"). The **pressure-dialed turnover-forcing side of Steals** is parked to the coaching layer (same prerequisite as BallHandling). The **per-opponent-slot suppression** limitation is a known instrument gap, not a fix. All three are synthesis/coaching conversations, not more sweeps.

**Carried flags, unchanged:** the S48 FTA micro-flag, the 3P%-at-rating-0 watch, the parked FT-curve line, the parked spacing/passing-conversion team-composition test, the S49 reshapers (ball-dominance layer, unforced-turnover channel — the latter adjacent to the Steals attribution machinery), BallHandling's pressure-dialed prerequisite, the S50 design bundle (height-over-defender make term — still the one that most gates the height→skill lean sizing; light block channel; **wingspan→steals — the Steals findings confirm it stays unwired: Steals is an attribution dial, not a deflection engine**; Weight-cosmetic), the S51 no-post-hunt diet gap, the time-sliced fatigue bench, the JumpBall tip counter. Newly parked: the PostDefense-as-size coupling; the pressure-dialed Steals turnover-forcing test.

**Validation:** all eight runs green on Emmett's machine; both anchors exact; the full validation suite green as the commit gate (only sweep JSONs added — the suite is untouched). Next: **Family H — Cognition (BasketballIQ, Discipline)** per Emmett's standing order, then the synthesis pass reading the completed attribute-meaning doc end-to-end before any engine work is scheduled.

## Session 51 — Interior offense measured (Family F: PostMoves, Screening): the tweener-post exists, Screening is the biggest team channel on the bench, and PostMoves buys touches that arrive at a generic diet — the no-post-hunt gap opened with numbers (config-and-run; engine untouched) (2026-07-12)

**Scope:** The fourth family through the S47 full-box ruler, and the smallest — **Family F, Interior offense: PostMoves and Screening.** Two isolation walks (0→99 in 5-point steps, 2,000 games/rung, everything else frozen at 50, slot 5) plus a seven-row interaction block — **98,000 real games**. Three text configs in `tools/sweep/`; **no engine file, no `config.json`, no readout change, no Monte Carlo** (zero engine math moved). Full CONVENTIONS ritual: fresh pull, the Family F wiring map re-verified line-by-line, assumptions #1–#4 resolved at the gate, the two walks and seven rows presented as an archetype table with predicted movement, Emmett's explicit go before the first file.

**Slot 5 again; the anchor held exactly, three places.** Every Family F channel is attribute-driven or an all-five aggregate — nothing is slot-weighted — so slot 5 carried the S48/S50 anchor directly with no debate. FLAT_50_CONTROL and both walks' 50-rungs reproduced **9.4 PTS / 34.3 FG% / 49.8 FT%** — the world unmoved since S48.

**The check-in audit confirmed the wiring map with one footnote; assumptions #1–#3 all resolved.** PostMoves has exactly three gameplay reads (Roll E usage score `RollEGenerator.cs:131`, its raw contribution identical to Close's at equal weight; the denial post-channel `:321–322`; gravity postAccess `Player.cs:398`) — footnote: the gravity read has **two downstream consumers** (AttentionGenerator and the passing-converter's postRoute, both fed by `GravityContribution`), still one read site, both whisper-scale. Screening has exactly one read: `RollHGenerator.cs:330–348` (C5.5), an all-five offensive aggregate with the shooter included (no exclusions), halfcourt-only (`!state.FastBreak`), bonus-only, applying to **all five zones** (Phase 44 removed the interior gate). The postness pin (assumption #3) confirmed at source: `Matchup.Postness` reads Height/PostDefense/Strength only — none swept — so both turnover-attribution multipliers (committer picker's BallHandling×perimeterMult, interior picker's Strength×interiorMult) are pinned, while post-selection turnovers credit SelectedSlot directly, so his TO/game rises purely through involvement. **The missing transition/fast-break-share column was reported at the gate** (assumption #2): no such column exists in the readout and no stored flat-50 transition measurement exists in the tree, so the Screening dilution was **banded, not computed** — a stated +1.7 to +2.3pp expected team-FG% band before any walk was read.

**Finding 1 — Screening is the largest team-wide single-rating channel measured on the bench to date.** Team A FG% ran **33.2 → 35.5 (+2.3pp full-walk)** — the top of the predicted band, so halfcourt share is on the high side of the 0.60–0.75 assumption. Team points +2.7 (51.4 → 54.1). That dwarfs everything prior — S48's best gravity lift was under a point. It lifts all five zones including threes (3P% 22.0 → 24.4 — the Phase 44 all-zone gate confirmed live). The swept player's own points rose 9.1 → 9.6 purely through his own FG% climbing with the team on **flat 18% usage** — Screening buys him nothing individually, only a share of the better team looks. **Usage, steals, and blocks were dead-flat across all 21 rungs**, exactly as wired (no usage/picker/defensive read exists). Rebound ripple ran **down** (RebΔ flipped −0.6 → +0.2 as fewer team misses were left to grab — the S48 make-raiser signature).

**Finding 2 — PostMoves buys a rising pile of touches that arrive at a totally generic shot diet: the no-post-hunt gap, now the family's first-order design result.** Usage climbed **12.7% → 23.9%** on a curve steeper than Close's S48 14%→22% at both ends — the two stacked ball-getting channels (usage score *and* denial survival) are visible exactly as predicted. But the shot mix stayed motionless across the whole walk (Rim 28.4 → 28.2, Short/Mid/Long/Three all flat). **The engine has no way for a post player to hunt post shots through PostMoves** — his extra possessions spread across the same generic rim/short/mid/three mix everyone shoots, because the displacement diet bend reads `OffenseRating(zone, shooter)` (Outside/Mid/Close/Finishing only) and PostMoves is not in that map. His FG% fell 35.3 → 33.8 (−1.5pp, no make term — more volume through flat zone skills costs efficiency, the milder SelfCreation shape), and his personal TO rose 1.9 → 2.7 (more touches, more giveaways). Steals and blocks flat. Logged for the design bundle, nothing wired.

**Finding 3 — the tweener-post exists: the parked existence requirement closed affirmative.** TWEENER_POST (Height 15, Wingspan 20, Strength 45, PostMoves 90, Close 75 — a guard-sized body with a post skill package) posted **13.5 PTS on 35.4 FG%, 25.4% usage**: a genuine interior threat whose skill overrides his size for both getting the ball and keeping it. The missing size leg shows exactly where the divisional-sorting principle predicts — his rebounding collapses (7.7 → 5.8 REB), his rim protection drops (BLK 0.7 → 0.5), his efficiency barely clears control (35.4 vs 34.3) — but none of it strands him. He functions as a D2/D3 big and, with a modicum of perimeter skill, would unlock D1. **The requirement made flesh, and the generation redesign is now cleared to produce him.** (One curiosity, classified as composition/noise: his steals read 1.6 vs 1.2 control with no wire connecting his low height to steals and five dials moving in the row — worth a CSV glance, nothing points at a bug.)

**The interaction block, the rest of it.** POST_SCORER (PostMoves 90, Close 90, Finishing 90, Strength 75) is the dominant interior line — **17.6 PTS on 42.9%, 28% usage, +4.7 team-points margin**, clearing S48's rim-only elite (12.9) easily, and it **does** tilt the diet inside (Short 17.5 → 19.5) — but through his Close/Finishing, not his PostMoves, confirming Finding 2's mechanism from the other direction. POST_HANDS_NO_FINISH (PostMoves 90, Finishing 10, Close 10) scored **below control** (8.7 vs 9.4, 31.2 FG%) — the interior Hack-a-Shaq: gets position, bricks, and the offense partly quarantines him (Rim 28.8 → 28.0). SCREEN_BIG (Screening 90 + a real body) is pure team value — 9.8 personal PTS but **A.PTS 55.0 (+2.2 margin)** and 10.8 REB (the S45 body amplifier). ALL_F_ELITE and F_FLOOR_15 bracketed the control as expected (11.6 / 22% use up; 7.1 / 14% use down).

**The design-bundle feed this measurement adds (Emmett's ruling, logged with evidence, nothing touched).** The **no-post-hunt gap** joins the bundle: PostMoves gets a post player the ball but the engine cannot express "he hunts post shots" — his volume arrives at a generic diet, the interior analog of the missing ball-dominance layer from S49. Sits alongside the S50 questions (the height-over-defender make term — still the one that most gates the generation redesign's height→skill lean) and the S49 reshapers. The tweener-post requirement is **removed from the bundle — closed affirmative** by Finding 3.

**The generation-redesign feed (what PostMoves and Screening actually buy).** PostMoves is a pure touch-getter: +11pp of usage across a full walk, zero diet shaping, a mild efficiency tax, no make term. Screening is a pure team-make multiplier: +2.3pp team FG% fully stacked, nothing individual. Neither should be sized as a scoring rating in isolation — PostMoves' value is entirely downstream of the zone skills it feeds touches into (POST_SCORER vs POST_HANDS_NO_FINISH is the whole story), and Screening's value is a five-man team good. Recommendation recorded: size these after the synthesis pass, with the no-post-hunt gap ruled first.

**Carried flags, unchanged:** the S48 FTA micro-flag, the 3P%-at-rating-0 watch, the parked FT-curve line, the parked spacing/passing-conversion team-composition test, the S49 reshapers (ball-dominance layer, unforced-turnover channel), BallHandling's pressure-dialed prerequisite, the S50 design bundle (height-over-defender make term — gates the height→skill lean sizing; light block channel; wingspan→steals; Weight-cosmetic), the time-sliced fatigue bench, the JumpBall tip counter. Newly parked: the no-post-hunt diet gap (Finding 2). Newly closed: the tweener-post existence requirement (Finding 3, affirmative).

**Validation:** all three runs green on Emmett's machine; the anchor exact three places; the full validation suite green as the commit gate (only sweep JSONs added — the suite is untouched). Next: **Family G — Defense** per Emmett's standing order, then H (Cognition), then the synthesis pass reading the completed attribute-meaning doc end-to-end before any engine work is scheduled.

## Session 50 — Physical package measured (Families A + C, ten ratings): Weight is proven cosmetic, length buys possessions while explosion buys points, and the size-should-score design question is opened with numbers attached (config-and-run; engine untouched) (2026-07-12)

**Scope:** The third family through the S47 full-box ruler, and the biggest — **Families A (Body: Height, Wingspan, Weight) and C (Athleticism: Strength, Speed, Quickness, FirstStep, Vertical, Endurance, Hustle) combined into one Physical package** by Emmett's S49 close-out ruling (the engine mixes them in shared composites and they feed the same generation decision). Ten isolation walks (0→99 in 5-point steps, 2,000 games/rung, everything else frozen at 50) plus a nine-row body×athleticism interaction block — **438,000 real games**, the longest run yet. Eleven text configs in `tools/sweep/`; **no engine file, no `config.json`, no readout change, no Monte Carlo** (zero engine math moved). Full CONVENTIONS ritual: fresh pull, the physical-package wiring map re-verified line-by-line, assumptions #1–#3 resolved at the gate, the slot ruling and nine rows presented as an archetype table with predicted movement, Emmett's explicit go before the first file.

**Slot ruling: back to slot 5, reclaiming the S48 anchor — and the anchor held exactly.** S49's move to slot 1 existed for BallHandling's guard-weighted channel; this family's heavy channels (make door, denial, displacement, putbacks, rebounding, blocks, postness) are all slot-blind or slot-paired, so slot 5 buys direct comparison against the Scoring family at the cost of muting Roll A's minority entry aggregates. FLAT_50_CONTROL and every walk's 50-rung reproduced **9.364 PTS / 34.33 FG% / 49.75 FT% to the third decimal** — twelve runs (eleven this session + S48's memory), one deterministic answer. The world had not moved since S48.

**The check-in audit found three divergences from the draft prompt, all flagged before building.** (1) **Roll A's slot-weighted aggregate reads TWO of this family's composites, not one** — `RollAGenerator.cs` runs both EffectiveAthleticism *and* `Matchup.LengthRating` through the same guard-heavy [0.35…0.08] weights, so slot 5 mutes a length whisper as well as the athleticism one. Same trade, wider footprint; accepted. (2) **Displacement's physical term is ONE channel, not two, and it reads RAW athleticism** — `DisplacementDefender.FromPlayer` feeds `Player.Athleticism` verbatim (doc-comment confirms) and the physLevel at `Matchup.cs:640` compares raw shooter vs raw lineup mean; the draft listed it among the fatigue-discounted consumers and double-counted it against the shooter-vs-lineup read. Consequence: Endurance does not flow through the shot-diet bend. (3) **The denial-blend postness wake-up is invisible on the Height walk by arithmetic** — the blend slides weight between the perimeter gap and the post gap, but on a flat-50 bench a Height walk leaves *both gaps at zero* (postGap = 50 − (50+50)/2 = 0), so the mix shift moves nothing. The denial post-channel only expresses under **Strength**, which moves the gap itself (at 99: postGap ≈ −24.5, post-weight ≈ 0.66). The interpretation key was corrected before any walk was read.

**Finding 1 — Weight is proven cosmetic, the cleanest possible version of the finding.** All 21 rungs of the Weight walk are **byte-identical in every stat column** while the CSV's `meta_swept_value` column steps 0→99 — the dial demonstrably landed (and `BuildSweepTeam` throws on unknown fields, so a silent drop is impossible), and the game demonstrably did not move. A whole-tree grep at the gate confirmed the source story: `Player.Weight` is read only by `Validate()` (range check), the Pass-2 generator (drawn, stored), and two roster/bench copies. Zero gameplay reads. Whether Weight should feed Strength-adjacent channels or stay cosmetic until a body-contact layer exists is a **flagged design question for Emmett** — recorded, not fixed.

**Finding 2 — Height creates AND claims blocks, suppresses turnover blame and steal share by design, and buys almost no scoring.** Boards 6.45 → 9.47, blocks 0.57 → 0.88 with the rate/share triple splitting cleanly: team blocks rise 3.47 → 3.75 (creation — the length door is real) *while* his share rises 20% → 23% (claiming — the blocker picker). The designed postness suppression printed exactly as predicted from the config coefficients at the gate (1/3 each, PostFloor 0.1, scale 40): his turnover blame fell 2.55 → 2.07 across the walk, monotone. **A fourth postness channel fired that the walk predictions missed:** his *steal share* collapsed 26% → 14% while team steals stayed dead flat at ~6.3 — the `StealerPicker`'s designed post-suppression (verified in source at the gate, same tanh shape), predicted for the archetypes but not listed for the walk. Classified direct-by-design. And the headline gap: FG% moved just 33.5 → 34.8 (+1.35pp), **all of it block-avoidance through LengthRating** — there is no height-over-defender term in the make chance. FGA flat (10.65 → 10.74): no usage-shaped curve under any body rating, the suspicious list stayed clean.

**Finding 3 — Wingspan is the purest length rating in the engine.** Boards 6.61 → 9.36, blocks 0.55 → 0.89 (creates and claims, same triple as Height), FG% +1.1pp (his own shots get blocked less), and *everything else flat* — steals, turnovers, usage all motionless, exactly as wired (Wingspan is in no postness, no picker base weight). The JumpBall max-wingspan read is recorded as **wired-but-unmeasured**: no first-possession column exists and one tip per game is hopelessly confounded with Wingspan's own block/rebound effects on full-game totals.

**Finding 4 — Vertical is the best athletic rating for a scorer; the explosion trio is real but shallow.** Vertical: FG% 33.3 → 35.5 (+2.2pp — the only composite member that is also length), blocks 0.62 → 0.84, points 9.2 → 9.7. Speed, Quickness, and FirstStep each buy ~+1.2pp of FG% across the full range — the predicted one-fifth-strength composite doors, directionally identical as required. Their divergences are fully explained by documented private channels: Speed and FirstStep see usage *dip* at the top (18.2% → 17.6% — their gravity-access term draws defensive attention, which taxes the denial contest), while Quickness (no gravity read) stays flat. Residual divergence: none.

**Finding 5 — Strength is the grab-bag, and the interior double-up lost its tug-of-war.** Boards 6.42 → 9.46 (tied with Height), FG% +1.9pp (second-best of the family — the composite doors *plus* the denial post-channel getting-open effect from divergence #3), blocks correctly flat (Strength is in no block weight). Its turnover curve was mixed-by-construction on paper (postness suppression cutting general blame vs the interior picker running Strength as base weight *and* multiplier), but the measurement answers it: TO fell smoothly 2.49 → 2.09 — **the general suppression wins**; the interior double-up is the smaller force at this scale. Steal share suppressed 26% → 15%, same postness machinery as Height.

**Finding 6 — Endurance's magnitude verdict is made: a whisper.** 0 vs 99 moves FG% by 0.2pp and points by nothing; MARATHON_MAN (End 95) and GASSED (End 5) are indistinguishable in the block. The channel is live — fatigue accrues every possession on the sweep path (`Governor.cs:527`, confirmed at the gate, with the sweep's default `FatigueConfig` byte-identical to `config.json`'s) and nobody ever sits, so the swept player carries his full drain difference all game — it just doesn't cash out on a whole-game aggregate readout. The **temporal shape is unmeasurable on this instrument** (no period/time-slice columns); whether Endurance matters late-game specifically needs a time-sliced bench, recorded not built. The finding is aggregate-only by construction.

**Finding 7 — Hustle is textbook share-not-creation.** His boards climb 6.6 → 8.7 and his steals 1.1 → 1.4 while the *team's* totals stay flat (boards 38.5, steals ~6.3) — he claims a bigger slice of the same pile through the three picker tilts, the first swept player of the whole pass to move his own defensive box. FG% dead flat across all 21 rungs (Hustle is in no composite and no make door — the suspicious-list check passed). The team-mean hustle nudges (Roll F disruption, defensive-foul cost) are below noise with one player moving the mean ~+9.8.

**Finding 8 — the marquee: explosion buys points, length buys possessions, and the full package laps both.** POCKET_ROCKET (tiny bouncy guard: 10.3 PTS on 38.1%, 5.8 REB, +2.0 margin) **outscores** STIFF_GIANT (plodding seven-footer: 9.1 PTS on 34.0% — *below an average player* — 11.7 REB, +1.5 margin, living entirely on boards, block share, and the lowest turnover blame on the board). FREAK (both halves at 90, zero skill) laps them: 12.0 PTS on 42.9%, 11.9 REB, 1.2 BLK, +6.4 margin — the strongest single-player team effect measured on this bench so far, on nothing but body. ALL_PHYS_ELITE (all ten at 85) confirms the ordering (11.5 / 41.5% / 12.6 REB, +5.6) and its Weight-85 contributes nothing. PHYSICAL_FLOOR_15 proves the floor is real: 8.0 PTS on 29.4%, 4.3 REB, −3.9 margin — a physically sub-floor player is a genuine team liability with all skills average. Both designed postness effects showed on cue in the post-shaped rows (FREAK/STIFF_GIANT steal and TO numbers fall).

**The design-question bundle this measurement opens (Emmett's ruling, logged with evidence attached, none touched this session).** Emmett's in-session read, sharpened by the numbers: (1) **There is no height-over-defender term in the make chance** — a 99-height player gains +1.35pp FG%, all block-avoidance; near the rim and in the post, shooting over a smaller defender is real efficiency the engine cannot express. A missing wire, not an undersized one — and the one that most directly affects how hard the generation redesign's height→skill lean can push (if height itself buys efficiency, the tax can lean harder; **do not size the lean until this is ruled**). (2) **The block channel is modest even fully stacked** — FREAK blocks 1.2/game; a 99-length walk adds ~0.3 team blocks. Magnitude call, waits for a real population per standing rule, but flagged as likely light. (3) **Wingspan feeds steals nothing** — whether long arms should buy deflections is a wiring question. (4) **Weight is cosmetic** (Finding 1). All four in `docs/attribute-meaning.md` with the curves as evidence.

**The generation-redesign feed (what body and athleticism actually buy, for the height→athleticism lean sizing).** Length is a possession engine, not a scoring engine: boards +~3/game and blocks +~0.3 team/game across a full walk, FG% nearly untouched. Explosion is a modest efficiency engine: +1–2pp FG% per rating, stacking to FREAK's +8.6pp. The physical floor is punitive (−3.9 margin at 15s). So under **current wiring** the height→skill negative lean prices tall players out of very little scoring — but design question (1) would change that materially. Recommendation recorded: run the remaining families and the synthesis pass, rule on the size-should-score question, *then* size the leans.

**Carried flags, unchanged:** the S48 FTA micro-flag, the 3P%-at-rating-0 watch item, the parked FT-curve line, the parked spacing/passing-conversion team-composition test, the S49 reshapers (ball-dominance layer, unforced-turnover channel), and BallHandling's pressure-dialed prerequisite. Newly parked: the time-sliced fatigue bench (Finding 6), the JumpBall tip counter (Finding 3).

**Validation:** all eleven runs green on Emmett's machine; the anchor exact; the full validation suite green as the commit gate. Next: **Family F — Interior offense (PostMoves, Screening)** per Emmett's standing order, then G (Defense), H (Cognition), then the synthesis pass reading the completed attribute-meaning doc end-to-end before any engine work is scheduled.
