## Session 49 — Perimeter-creation family measured on the point guard: usage and getting-open work, assists attribute correctly, and ball-handling reads inverted — surfacing the missing ball-dominance and unforced-turnover layers (config-and-run; engine untouched) (2026-07-12)

**Scope:** The second family through the S47 full-box ruler — Perimeter creation (BallHandling, Passing, Playmaking, SelfCreation, OffBallMovement), and the first measured on **slot 1 (the point guard)** instead of slot 5. Five isolation walks (0→99 in 5-point steps, 2,000 games/rung, everything else frozen at 50) plus an eight-row within-player interaction block — 232,000 real games, six text configs in `tools/sweep/`, **no engine file, no `config.json`, no readout change, no Monte Carlo** (zero engine math moved). Full CONVENTIONS ritual; the check-in gate was honored — fresh pull, the perimeter-creation wiring source map re-verified line-by-line, the slot ruling and the eight rows presented as an archetype table with predicted movement, Emmett's explicit go before the first file. SelfCreation, ruled out of Family D at the S48 gate, was measured here.

**The check-in audit found two divergences from the draft prompt, both flagged before building.** (1) **SelfCreation has two engine reads, not three** — a whole-tree grep found only the Roll E usage-score coefficient (`RollEGenerator.cs:130`) and the gravity perimeter-access term (`Player.cs:397`); the claimed "bonus-FT-putback picker reads SelfCreation" does not exist in the tree (the putback shooter is the offensive rebounder, weighted by rebounding). Retired on the record. (2) **BallHandling's Roll F/Roll B mute is a config-scalar mechanism, not a null-coach fallback** — `CoachProfileFor` appears only in comments (a migration path), and `CoachProfile` has no `Pressure` property; pressure comes from `MatchupConfig.HomePressure/AwayPressure = 5.0 = PressureNeutral`, so `pUnit = 0` closes the gate. And the live team-turnover channel is **Roll A only** (fixed `StandardGate = 0.5`, pressure-independent), **not "Rolls A/B"** — Roll B routes through the same pressure-gated path as Roll F and is muted at neutral. This reframed the BallHandling prediction at the gate: team turnover *rate* would barely move while attribution climbed, so his personal turnovers would likely rise, not fall.

**Why slot 1, and the honest scope of the choice.** The audit established that in the flat-50 lab world four of the five ratings are **slot-blind** (assist picker, usage score, denial contest, gravity/spacing are all attribute-driven), so the *only* thing slot 1 buys over slot 5 is readability of BallHandling's team-turnover channel, which flows through guard-heavy position weights (slot 1 = 0.35 vs slot 5 = 0.08). A second rationale offered at check-in — a post-vs-guard committer penalty — was **withdrawn on inspection**: in a flat-clone world every player has identical body attributes, so nobody is more of a post and that penalty is inert. The re-anchor cost was stated up front: the S48 slot-5 scoring control does not carry; slot-1 flat-50 (11.6 PTS / 35.5 FG% / 21.7% use / 1.5 AST / 2.6 TO) is the new Family-E anchor. All five walks' 50-rungs and FLAT_50_CONTROL are that same box — determinism held at the new slot; Team A ≈ Team B (52.8 / 52.9); STL/BLK and Team B flat everywhere.

**Finding 1 — SelfCreation is the volume king, exactly as wired.** The single largest usage coefficient in the engine (0.35 on one rating) produces the steepest usage curve yet measured: use share 13.4% → 21.7% → 36.2%, points 7.3 → 11.6 → 18.6, with FG% sliding 37.8 → 33.0 (the designed volume tax), his own ORB falling 2.30 → 2.00 (shooter-nerf), and the shot diet tilting off the rim (28.8 → 26.9 rim share) as he creates his own looks. Inherits the whole S48 usage bundle as expected secondaries; the gravity whisper (~+4 gravity points at 99) is below noise here, as predicted.

**Finding 2 — OffBallMovement is getting-open with no make read.** It lifts his surviving usage share 20.3% → 23.0% purely by beating the Roll E denial contest (`OffBallDefense − OffBallMovement`), with flat FG% — a smaller, cleaner mirror of the volume channel.

**Finding 3 — Passing and Playmaking are almost pure assist-attribution ratings, and the attribution is passing-dominant (correct); the predicted make-conversion dip did not appear.** Both raise the swept player's assist *share* monotonically (Passing 0.9 → 2.1; Playmaking 1.1 → 1.9), Passing moving it more per its larger weight (0.5 vs 0.35) — correct basketball. But team FG% is dead flat across the Passing walk (35.4/35.5/35.6) and at WEAK_LINK (Pass 5 → 35.4): **the RollH passing-conversion bonus is invisible on this instrument.** Two stacked reasons, both honest: the below-pivot passing discount (below), and — the larger — the bonus is gated on gravity/spacing *openness*, near-zero in a flat world, so like spacing in Family D it needs a team-composition test to fire and is parked with it. My check-in prediction of an asymmetric team-FG% dip was wrong at this scale; corrected on the record.

**Finding 4 — BallHandling reads inverted: blame without protection.** The better handler is charged *more* turnovers. The interaction block isolates it in one triple, identical but for the handle: BUTTERFINGERS_VISIONARY (BH 10) **1.8 TO**, FLAT_50_CONTROL (BH 50) 2.6, PURE_POINT (BH 85) 3.1 — matching the walk (1.6 → 2.6 → 3.2). The only live BallHandling turnover channels here are the committer-attribution picker (weight ∝ BallHandling — the ball is in his hands, so he catches more of the team's giveaways) and the Roll A aggregate (small); the half that should make a good handler *lose it less* is pressure-gated to zero at neutral pressure. So BallHandling is a net negative on the bench. Not a bug to patch this session — the headline **design finding**.

**The two reshapers this measurement surfaced (the real value of the run).** **(A) The missing ball-dominance / initiation layer.** The engine models who *shoots* (the usage score) but not who *initiates* or *holds* the ball — which caps passing magnitude (a great passer can only claim a bigger slice of a small fixed assist pie; even PURE_POINT tops out at 2.3 assists) and leaves ball-handling protection with nowhere to live (a good handle can't reduce turnovers if it doesn't earn more touches). One absent subsystem explains both; recommended as the highest-value design conversation of the whole attribute-meaning pass, intersecting the coaching layer's ball-distribution dials. **(B) The missing unforced-turnover channel.** The base turnover rate is a flat constant identical for a maestro and a butterfingers; BallHandling only enters through a defense-relative matchup (needs a defender, muted at neutral). There is no offense-only "lost it yourself" rate — travel, ball off the foot, pass out of bounds. The engine already names the split (dead-ball = self-inflicted; live-ball = stripped), so low BallHandling should drive the dead-ball rate directly, offense-side, while the forced channel stays the pressure matchup. Attribution sub-call recorded for the build: lean unforced blame toward the *weaker* handle (the current picker blames the best handler — correct for steals, backwards for dead-balls).

**Two interpretation notes for the record.** (1) **The flat-50 bench is a below-average *passing* world, by the same logic as Family D's "what 50 means."** The assist lineup-passing pivot was recentered to 71.31 in S41 to track the real population (starters average ~71 assist-weight) and the zone assisted-rates calibrated to the season page (13.7 assists) at that pivot — so a flat-50 lineup runs assist existence at ~0.80× normal. The assist *level* is read on the season page, never on this bench; these curves are read for shape and attribution. Emmett's own analysis surfaced this in-session (the "far too mellow" observation), and it maps onto the closed S41 ruling exactly. (2) **A separate calibration lever exists but was not touched:** the lineup-passing swing band is ±25% (`AssistPassSwing = 0.25`), a hard ceiling on how much team passing skill can move assist existence (all-50 → all-99 team ≈ +50%; one player to 99 ≈ +9%). Whether ±25% is the right band is a future basketball call, recorded not acted on.

**What shipped:** six text configs in `tools/sweep/` — `sweep_ballhandling.json`, `sweep_passing.json`, `sweep_playmaking.json`, `sweep_selfcreation.json`, `sweep_offballmovement.json` (walk mode, 0→99 step 5, 2,000 games/rung, sweptSlot 1, baseSeed 1000) and `perimeter_creation_interaction.json` (eight cases: FLAT_50_CONTROL, PURE_POINT, ISO_ALPHA, MOVEMENT_MAN, BUTTERFINGERS_VISIONARY, WEAK_LINK, ALL_E_ELITE, COMPOSITE_NONCREATOR). No engine file, no `config.json`, no readout or suite change. Validation: all six runs green on Emmett's machine; the standing full-suite green confirmation is the commit gate (the `sweep` path returns before the suite). Docs after: this entry; **`docs/attribute-meaning.md` — the main deliverable**, a new Family E section (the five curves, the interaction table, the four findings, the two reshapers, the muted-channel notes, the below-pivot grain note, the generation-redesign feed); `design.md` — the attribute-sweep-bench section's pointer gains Family E; `status.md` — Family E moved to measured, BallHandling marked *partially measured* with the pressure-dialed test as its named prerequisite, the two reshapers (ball-dominance layer, unforced-turnover channel) added to the design/parked queue, the next family named per Emmett's order.

**Next (S50 — the next attribute family, Emmett's order):** the remaining families are Body (Height/Wingspan/Weight), Athleticism (7 ratings), Interior offense (PostMoves, Screening), and Defense (6 ratings) — each a pure config-and-run against the same ruler. Emmett's order rules; the §6 pipeline drafts the prompt as its own audited pass, ChatGPT reviews before build. The two reshapers surfaced here (ball-dominance / initiation layer, unforced-turnover channel) are logged as engine design conversations that gate a "correctly valued" verdict on the perimeter-creation ratings, to be scheduled when Emmett chooses.

## Session 48 — Scoring family measured: six curves, one interaction block, the ruler's first real haul — and gravity verified live as a byproduct (config-and-run; engine untouched) (2026-07-11)

**Scope:** The first measurement against the S47-generalized ruler — the Scoring family (Close, Mid, Outside, Finishing, FreeThrow, FoulDrawing) swept through the `sweep` bench as pure config-and-run: six isolation walks (0→99 in 5-point steps, 2,000 games/rung, swept slot 5, everything else frozen at 50) plus a seven-row within-player interaction block — 266,000 real games, seven text configs in `tools/sweep/`, **no engine file, no `config.json`, no readout change, no Monte Carlo** (zero engine math moved). Full CONVENTIONS ritual; the check-in gate was honored — fresh pull, the scoring-wiring source map re-verified line-by-line against the tree (every claimed site held: the zone→skill map `Matchup.cs:51–55`, the FoulDrawing contest `:395`, the Rim/Short displacement gates `:683/:685`, the linear FT make `RollLGenerator.cs:87`, the config-driven Roll G base weights, the `Governor` MissFouled FGA/3PA exclusions, all six ratings in `BenchRatingFields`), the six walk configs and the interaction rows presented as an archetype table with predicted movement per row, and **SelfCreation ruled OUT at the gate** (its only direct engine read is the Roll E bonus-FT-putback shooter picker — no make-curve role — so it is Family E's, per status.md's grouping, correcting the S47 journal's stale "Next" line). Emmett's explicit go preceded the first file.

**Every validation gate passed, and the instrument re-proved itself beyond spec.** FT linearity exact — FT% tracks the rating to within 0.74pp at worst across all 21 rungs (0 → 0.0%, 50 → 49.8% matching the S47 flat-50 finding, 99 → 99.0%). All six walks' 50-rungs and FLAT_50_CONTROL identical **to three decimals** (9.364 PTS / 34.33 FG% / 49.75 FT%) — seven independent runs, one deterministic answer, a free extra self-proof. Team A ≈ Team B at control (52.8 / 52.9). Rebound ripple down under every make rating, including the FreeThrow signature: at FT=0 the total-board line is *elevated* (39.3 vs 38.7 baseline — every bricked FT is a live rebound chance), falling to 37.9 at FT=99. STL/BLK flat under every scoring rating; Team B's box flat under every walk. Nothing on the suspicious list survived undispositioned.

**The direct curves, pinned at CSV grain.** Personal: 3P% **17.2 → 23.2 → 44.8** across the Outside walk (the make curve's floor means a 0-rated shooter still converts ~17% — "open-only, not a non-shooter" holds); FT% ≈ rating. Team-zone directional lines (diluted by four flat teammates; the personal curves are steeper): Close → Short FG% 32.7 / 34.2 / 40.5; Mid → Mid 27.1 / 27.9 / 34.5; Outside → Long 24.8 → 31.1 **and** Three 22.8 → 28.7 (one rating, two zones, as wired); Finishing → Rim 52.8 / 54.5 / 59.7. FoulDrawing: FTA 2.65 → 3.11 → 4.20/g, FTr 0.246 → 0.291 → 0.406, and his **FGA falls 10.75 → 10.34** — the MissFouled-leaves-the-denominator mechanism visible in the raw counts, with recorded FG%/3P% rising only ~+0.5/+0.4pp compositionally, exactly as the source predicted.

**Finding 1 — usage follows skill: the other half of the standing ruling, measured for the first time.** Raising any zone make skill lifts the swept player's possession-use share from ~14% (rating 0) to ~22–23% (99); FreeThrow and FoulDrawing move it not at all — the offense hunts shooting skill, not line-trips. Finishing's response is smaller (16.3 → 19.9), plausibly because rim volume partly flows through putbacks and transition rather than half-court selection (recorded as an observation; the selection site was not opened). The quarantine corollary: team zone lines barely dent at the bottom of a walk because a bad shooter takes few shots (8.2 FGA/g at rating 0 vs 13.3 at 99) — the offense quarantines weakness and amplifies strength automatically. Micro-fingerprint: his own ORB falls as his skill rises (2.25 → 2.12; the composite non-scorer grabs 2.34) — he is the shooter more often and the rebounder-picker's shooter-nerf engages.

**Finding 2 — the shot-diet tilt is direct-by-design (traced), correcting the draft prompt's claim.** Each zone skill tilts the team attempt mix toward its own zone (Short 16.7 → 19.4 under Close; Mid 15.6 → 18.6; Rim 27.5 → 30.5 under Finishing; both Outside zones up; the FT and FoulDrawing mixes dead flat). Traced to the S36 displacement derivation: Stage 2 computes per-zone gaps via `OffenseRating(zone, shooter)` — the same zone→skill map the make curve reads — and Stage 5 bends the diet by the residualized gap, with the Rim/Short inward gates (Finishing/Close) stacking on top. So the prompt's adversarial-preamble claim "no scoring rating directly drives shot frequency" was true of the Roll G **base weights** but too narrow: the bend reads zone skills on purpose. Skilled players hunt their spots — corrected on the record.

**Finding 3 — gravity verified live, as a byproduct.** Every make skill faintly lifts the *other* zones' Team-A FG% at the high end, and the lift order matches the `GravityContribution` weights exactly: Finishing (0.35 of gravity) produces the biggest glow (+2.0–2.4pp at 99), Close (0.25) next, Mid (0.10) small, Outside (0.05) essentially nothing — with Team B flat throughout, confirming an offense-side relief effect. That is the gravity → attention → relief chain (`Player.GravityContribution` → AttentionGenerator → Roll H C1 relief) firing to spec in a test that was never aimed at it. It also explains the interaction block's oddity: ELITE_RIM lifted **team** points above ELITE_SHOOTER (56.0 vs 55.5 A.PTS) despite fewer personal points — rim threat carries 60% of gravity vs the perimeter's 5%; an interior monster warps the defense hardest and teammates eat. Two boundary lines recorded: "verified" means the **wiring** fires correctly (whether +2.4pp of teammate lift is the right *size* is a calibration question deferred to a real population), and only gravity — the saturating top-threat composite — was exercised; **spacing**, its accumulating twin, stayed quiet as designed (one player cannot move a team environment) and gets its day in a perimeter-family or team-composition test.

**Finding 4 — hack-a-Shaq emerged.** FOULS_BUT_BRICKS (FoulDrawing 90 / FreeThrow 20) scored **8.56 PTS vs the 9.36 control** — drawing fouls you can't cash is net negative, because each fouled trip replaces a shot worth ~0.75 expected points with two 20% free throws worth 0.4; FREE_POINTS (FT 90 on the same trips) cashes to 11.30. Nobody authored this; it fell out of the math. Also from the block: ELITE_SHOOTER's FTr *dropped* (.253 vs .291) despite more FTA — his extra attempts are perimeter-tilted and threes draw few whistles, so FTr reads as a zone-mix composite, not a FoulDrawing proxy; ALL_SCORING_ELITE posted 21.95 PTS on a 29.3% use share with the usage tax visible (TO 2.3 → 3.1); COMPOSITE_NONSCORER got 3.70 PTS on 9.9% use — the offense routes around him. One micro-flag recorded, not chased: FOULS_BUT_BRICKS drew 3.77 FTA/g vs FREE_POINTS' 4.08 at identical FoulDrawing 90 — ~8%, too large for noise, mechanism untraced (candidate: missed-FT rebound/possession composition).

**Two interpretation notes for the record.** (1) **The floors are asymmetric:** every make curve has a floor (rating 0 still converts), but the FT make is pure `rating/100`, so FreeThrow 0 made **literally 0.0%** over 2,000 games — a true zero exists; the full linear line is now charted for the parked FT-curve ruling. (2) **What 50 means:** rating 50 is *not* the league-average player — the make-curve recentering (S31-era, Emmett's standing ruling: recenter, never compress) anchored the **league's** average shooter, whose effective level sits well above 50, to the real per-zone targets. The flat-50 bench player is therefore a below-D1-average shooter facing a no-weak-link defense, and his 34.3% FG coexists coherently with the season page's calibrated 44.9%. The bench anchor is a lab reference, not a world prediction; curves here are read for shape and mechanism, and "is this level right?" is judged only on the season page.

**What shipped:** seven text configs in `tools/sweep/` — `sweep_close.json`, `sweep_mid.json`, `sweep_outside.json`, `sweep_finishing.json`, `sweep_freethrow.json`, `sweep_fouldrawing.json` (walk mode, 0→99 step 5, 2,000 games/rung, sweptSlot 5, baseSeed 1000, matching the S45 template) and `sweep_scoring_interaction.json` (seven cases: FLAT_50_CONTROL, ELITE_SHOOTER, ELITE_RIM, FREE_POINTS, FOULS_BUT_BRICKS, ALL_SCORING_ELITE, COMPOSITE_NONSCORER). No engine file, no `config.json`, no readout or suite change. Validation: all seven runs green on Emmett's machine; the standing full-suite green confirmation is the commit gate (the `sweep` path returns before the suite). Docs after: this entry; **`docs/attribute-meaning.md` — the main deliverable**, a new Family D Scoring section (the six curves, the interaction table, the three traced mechanisms, the open flags, the what-50-means note, the generation-redesign feed); `design.md` — the attribute-sweep-bench section gains its one-line Scoring pointer; `status.md` — Scoring moved to measured, the Bridge-#3 FoulDrawing diagnostic marked answered, the FT-curve parked note updated with the charted line, the FTA micro-flag added, Family E named as the recommended next.

**Next (S49 — recommended: Family E, perimeter creation):** BallHandling, Passing, Playmaking, SelfCreation, OffBallMovement — SelfCreation was explicitly deferred here at the S48 gate, and the usage/creation channel the Scoring measurement surfaced is this family's home turf. Emmett's order rules; the §6 pipeline drafts the prompt as its own audited pass, ChatGPT reviews before build.

## Session 47 — The sweep readout goes full-box: one trusted ruler for every future attribute family, proven against Rebounding (harness-only; engine untouched) (2026-07-11)

**Scope:** Turn the `sweep` findings bench from a **rebounding-only** readout into a **full-box** readout — every counting stat, for the swept player and both teams, plus each team's shot mix by zone — so every future attribute family (Scoring, Body, Athleticism, Defense) is a pure config-and-run against a trusted instrument. This session builds the **ruler**, it does not **measure** with it: no new attribute family was swept. Harness-only — no engine file, no `config.json`, no engine math; the readout only reads and prints what the engine already produces, so it changes zero outcomes and no Monte Carlo was required. Its own session (not bundled with the first new family) for a specific reason recorded at the §6a gate: studying a new family with an untrusted instrument means that when a scoring change legitimately moves a dozen stats at once, you can't tell a **readout bug** from **real engine behavior**. Build and trust the ruler first; measure with it next. Full CONVENTIONS ritual, check-in gate honored — fresh pull, all required reads (the sweep bench in full, `PlayerBoxTotals` + `AttributeGame`, the record zone fields, the `sweep` dispatch), the audit findings reconfirmed, the exact CSV schema + console layout + reuse-vs-new split presented, no file touched until Emmett's explicit "build."

**The key structural fact the build inherited (and why it was low-risk): the full box already existed, correctly attributed.** The sweep already calls `AttributeGame(result, game, gameSeed)` — the *same* per-player attribution pass the observation box score is built from — and was reading only `OReb`/`DReb` out of it. That call returns a `PlayerBoxTotals` carrying the **full 13-field per-player box** (`Fga, Fgm, Tpa, Tpm, Fta, Ftm, OReb, DReb, Blk, Stl, To, ShFoul, Ast`), every stat already credited to the right player regardless of which team was on offense — blocks, steals, and defensive boards go to the **defender**; assists and offensive boards to the **offense**; that is `AttributeGame`'s job and it is already trusted. So the generalization was literally *"read the other eleven fields out of the call the sweep already makes."* There was **no ownership table to build** and no risk of mis-assigning a defensive stat to the wrong side. The one thing keyed by offense — `r.Offense` — is the **team zone mix** only (a team's own shooting that possession is offensive), never the per-player defensive box (assumption #2 of the preamble, held).

**What the readout now captures, per rung.** (1) **The swept slot's full box** — PTS, FGM/FGA, 3PM/3PA, FTM/FTA, ORB/DRB/REB, AST, STL, BLK, TO, SFL, plus the derived rates FG%, 3P%, FT%, 3PA/FGA, FTr, and a usage proxy. (2) **Both teams' aggregate box** — the same stats summed over each team's five slots (Team A = the swept slot's team; Team B = the opponent, which a future defensive family will read to see what the swept player's defense does to opponents). (3) **Both teams' zone mix** — Rim/Short/Mid/Long/Three attempt-share and per-zone FG%, from the record's zone fields keyed by `r.Offense`. PTS and REB are **derived, not stored** (`PTS = 2·Fgm + Tpm + Ftm`, so a made three scores 3 because it increments both Fgm and Tpm; `REB = OReb + DReb`). The usage proxy is deliberately named **`PossessionUse`** (not `USG%`): `FGA + 0.44·FTA + TO`, with `PossessionUseShare = playerPossessionUse / teamPossessionUse` — a bench proxy, not basketball-reference usage (which needs minutes and team pace this bench does not model); the non-official name is on purpose so it is never mistaken for the real stat.

**Parity discipline — the legacy path kept byte-identical, the new columns appended alongside.** The existing rebound accumulation and its console/CSV formatting path were preserved **verbatim** (the only change to the legacy code was aliasing the tuple accessor — every arithmetic expression, aggregation order, conversion point, and format specifier is unchanged); the generalized box is a separate accumulator read from the same `AttributeGame` call, printed in two new console tables and appended CSV column groups. This is what keeps the parity gate clean and interpretable: displayed parity can break even with correct underlying counts via a changed aggregation order or recomputed team totals, so the old path was left intact rather than rewritten through a new abstraction. New CSV groups are prefixed and suffixed for machine-safety: `meta_*` (walk traceability), `swept_*`, `teamA_off_* / teamA_def_* / teamA_zone_*`, and the `teamB_*` mirror; every counting stat emits both `_total` (cumulative rung total) and `_pg` (per-game), rates emit once with a `_rate`/`_pct` suffix, and zero denominators produce `0.0`, never NaN. One deliberate naming call (flagged at delivery, reversible): the `_rate` suffix is applied **uniformly** to every derived rate, so FTr ships as `swept_ftr_rate` / `teamA_off_ftr_rate` — consistency of the machine-parseable suffix over exactly matching the prose column list.

**Verification — the parity anchor is exact, and the new columns are internally consistent (green on Emmett's machine).** Full suite `ALL CHECKS PASSED` + `STRESS TEST PASSED` with every engine calibration figure unmoved (combined FG% 43.5%, pace 141, the 7/8 mirror gap 1.4%) — proof the readout is inert on the suite path, exactly as designed (the `sweep` token returns before the suite). The three S45 rebounding configs re-run through the generalized readout **reproduced the S46 numbers to the digit** (combined swept-center boards = the legacy S5.ORB + S5.DRB): FLAT_50_CONTROL 2.20+5.49 = **7.69**, FREAK_BODY_ZERO_REB 1.38+3.48 = **4.86**, BODY50_REB0 (average-no-hands) 0.37+0.95 = **1.32**, TERRIBLE_BODY_ZERO_REB (weakling-no-hands) 0.18+0.49 = **0.67**, TERRIBLE_BODY_GREAT_REB (weakling-elite) **8.65**, BODY50_REB99 (average-elite) **12.27**, FREAK_BODY_GREAT_REB (freak-elite) **17.54**, RebΔ freak-no-hands **+2.1**; the two walk endpoints matched the post-S46 split values exactly (OffReb=0 → S5.ORB 0.37, DefReb=0 → S5.DRB 0.96), both curves monotone. The **new** box columns cross-checked against the legacy source: the swept REB column equals the legacy S5.ORB+S5.DRB total on every rung (FLAT 7.7 = 7.69, FREAK_BODY_GREAT 17.5 = 17.54), proving the box readout reads the same reconciled attribution rather than a second source; A.PTS ≈ B.PTS on the all-50 control (52.8 / 52.9), zone shares summed to ~100% with A ≈ B, no impossible values, every column populated for both teams.

**Two honest findings the readout surfaced — faithful reports, NOT readout bugs, and out of this session's scope.** Both are rock-stable across all rungs (moving only in the third digit), which is precisely the signature of a *correct* read of a flat input rather than a wiring artifact. (1) **A flat-50 free-throw rating makes ~49.8%** — the observation run's ~70% came from higher-rated shooters, not from a 50; whether a 50 FT rating *should* make ~50% is an FT-curve calibration question for a later session, not now. (2) **Flat-50 FG% ~34%** — consistent with the engine's low-rating FG% behavior already visible in the AverageVsAverage stress bucket (33.5%), so sane. Both are recorded as observations for the eventual calibration/scoring work, not acted on here.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.AttributeSweep.cs` — **EDIT** (a new `SweepBoxTotals` accumulator reading the eleven previously-unread `PlayerBoxTotals` fields for both teams out of the existing `AttributeGame` call, plus team zone-mix arrays keyed by `r.Offense`; the return type widened to a `SweepRungResult(Reb, Box)` pair; two new console tables — the swept-slot + team-scoring headline and the team shot-mix table — and the appended CSV column groups built by a single header/row-aligned helper; the `PossessionUse` proxy. The legacy rebound accumulation, its console table, and its CSV columns are byte-identical). No engine file, no `config.json`, no suite check, no new record field, no engine attribution change. Docs: this entry; `design.md` — the attribute-sweep-bench section's readout note updated in place (the readout is now the full per-player box for both teams plus team zone mix, not rebounding-only; the ruler is general for every future family); `docs/attribute-meaning.md` — untouched (no new family measured); `status.md` — the "light aim-and-record session" promise is now REAL (readout generalized + proven), Scoring (S48) is the next family and is now pure config-and-run.

**Next (S48 — the first measurement against the trusted ruler):** aim the generalized `sweep` bench at the **Scoring** family — the six scoring ratings (Outside, Mid, Close, Finishing, SelfCreation, FreeThrow) each swept in isolation at 5-point steps, plus an interaction block where they plausibly fight another attribute, read through the full-box readout. Because a scoring change legitimately moves many stats at once (more threes → more long caroms → different rebounds), the session opens with the scoring-wiring source map and a direct/secondary/suspicious causal framing so cross-stat movement is *interpreted*, not treated as a bug. Pure config-and-run — no engine or readout change expected. Its own audited pass; the §6 pipeline drafts the prompt, ChatGPT reviews before build.

## Session 46 — Rebounder-picker body floor: a freak body finally corrals boards on its own, and the mushy bottom of the height ladder separates (2026-07-11)

**Scope:** Fix the S45-diagnosed engine bug in the individual rebounder pickers — a big body with a zero rebounding rating grabbed ≈0.2 boards/game (the same near-nothing a 5'6" weakling gets), because both pickers wired the body as a *multiplier on the rating* (`max(1, Rating × PositionalWeight × WingspanMultiplier × HustleMultiplier)`), so a zero rating floored to 1 and the giant's body gave *him* no individual claim even though it lifted his team's glass margin to +2.1. Give both `OffensiveRebounderPicker` and `DefensiveRebounderPicker` a standalone **additive** body term (the block-picker parallel — `BlockerWeight` is additive, so a freak with a zero shot-blocking rating still swats on body alone). **The 55/45 team split (`OffensiveReboundShare`) was NOT touched** (S45 ruling — the team battle already credits the body via its size term; the bug was purely step-2 attribution). Engine change on LIVE paths (both pickers run every game), oracle-first with the archetype table as the sign-off medium, full CONVENTIONS ritual. The check-in gate was honored — fresh pull, all required reads (both pickers, `BlockerWeight` + config, `ReboundPhysical`/`Postness`/`ReboundWingspanMultiplier`, the two Resolver call sites, `OffensiveReboundShare`, the `MatchupConfig` rebound block), assumptions #1–#4 reconfirmed, the reuse-vs-new split reported, no engine/config/docs file touched until Emmett's explicit rulings. Two design rounds happened in-session (below); both shipped and both validated green on Emmett's machine.

**Round 1 — the luck weight + the relative body pull (shipped, validated).** Two moving parts, both ruled off the archetype table:
- **The retired floor-of-1 became a flat `ReboundLuckWeight` (5.0).** Emmett's observation: sheer odds alone — weird bounces, long caroms off a three — should give *any* body on the floor a baseline, and the old floor-of-1-against-teammates-weighing-~50 gave an inert player only ≈1/200 of his team's boards (the whole 0.2). The luck weight is every populated slot's **equal** claim on uncontested bounces ("a weird bounce doesn't care who you are"), added to all five; it subsumes the floor-of-1's every-slot-can-draw guarantee (weight ≥ Luck > 0). Ruled so a totally inert zero-rating player lands ≈0.9 boards/game instead of 0.2.
- **A one-sided additive body pull, `ReboundBodyPullWeight` (0.35) × max(0, ReboundPhysical − lineupMean).** The block-picker's additive shape, using the team battle's own body composite (`ReboundPhysical` = 0.525·Strength + 0.4875·Height + 0.4875·Wingspan) so "body" means one thing in both rebound steps. One-sided by ruling: a below-lineup-mean body gets zero, **never a second penalty** (its size cost already lives in the positional/wingspan multipliers). A signed (negative-capable) term was modeled and **rejected** at the design table — any coefficient large enough to give the freak-no-hands 3–4 boards dragged the 5'6" elite rebounder below the 9–10.5 window (double-penalty on the skilled small rebounder). On the offensive side the shooter nerf multiplies the **whole** weight (luck and body included) — Emmett's ruling: the nerf models reduced availability after shooting, not a skill-specific penalty. Round-1 sweep result (swept center's total boards/game): freak-no-hands **0.2 → 4.56**, elite anchors held (freak-elite 17.99, weakling-elite 9.00, average-elite 12.50), controls uniform, both curves monotone. Every predicted number landed within a rounding error.

**Round 2 — the saturating loose-ball floor (the S46b refinement, shipped, validated).** Emmett caught a real hole in the round-1 result: **average-no-hands (0.85) and weakling-no-hands (0.71) were too close.** Diagnosis, traced to the formula: the relative body pull only rewards being *bigger than your own lineup*, so an average body on an all-average team sits exactly at its lineup mean → earns nothing from the pull → ties with a small body, which also earns nothing. Shown across the whole zero-rating height ladder, the entire bottom third (5'2 → 6'0) was mushy/flat at ~0.7–0.85; the ladder only woke up above 6'0. **The fix: a second, ABSOLUTE body channel — a saturating "big-target" floor.** A big body helps on the glass two ways: it out-positions specific smaller teammates for a contested ball (the relative pull, already in), and it is just a big target near the rim so loose balls find it *regardless of who it is next to* (the missing piece). The floor is `ReboundBodyFloorCeiling (4.0) × tanh(max(0, ReboundPhysical − ReboundBodyFloorReference (22.5)) / ReboundBodyFloorScale (40.0))` — measured against a **fixed** reference (the physical of a ~5'2 extreme body), not the lineup mean, so raw size is rewarded; **tanh-saturated** so once a player is a genuine big, being even bigger adds little loose-ball presence (that extra size shows up in the relative pull instead), which keeps the freak from ballooning while lifting the mushy bottom into a clean monotone rise. Fixed reference → flat-50 control stays exactly uniform (every body equal → every floor equal).

**The three S46b rulings, off the zero-rating height ladder (the sign-off medium this round).** (1) **Gentle setting** (ceiling 4.0 / scale 40) — average-no-hands ≈1.3, ~2× the weakling — over the wider alternative. (2) **A 5'8 no-rebounder landing at ≈1.2 boards is right** ("rebounding as a random element of weird bounces, and the taller you are the more likely you benefit from them" — Emmett), so the floor reference stays at the 5'2 extreme rather than starting the lift higher. (3) **Accept weakling-elite settling from 9.00 to ≈8.6** as the structural cost — lifting average bodies necessarily lets the weakling-elite's four average-bodied teammates compete a little better for boards; every shape that separates the no-hands pair pays this toll, and 8.6 for a 5'6" elite-instinct rebounder is still elite (arguably *more* realistic — his teammates aren't glass-inert). One clarification recorded at the table: "average" (body 50) is the scale midpoint ≈ 5'11"/6'0" per the generator's authoritative height-bin table, and the sweep's "freak" (body 99) is tall/long/strong but average-hops (Vertical is not dialed); Emmett ruled 50-vs-50 is the correct neutral baseline and to rule against it as-is.

**Verification — green on Emmett's machine, the only verification that counts.** Full suite `ALL CHECKS PASSED`, stress test `STRESS TEST PASSED`, all three sweeps clean, no FAIL anywhere. The interaction sweep (swept center's total S5.ORB + S5.DRB) matched every S46b prediction essentially dead-on: **average-no-hands 1.32** (predicted ~1.3) vs **weakling-no-hands 0.67** (predicted ~0.67) — the tie is gone, the average body now grabs ~2× the small body purely from the loose-ball floor; freak-no-hands **4.86** (from the original 0.2), weakling-elite **8.65** (the accepted cost), average-elite **12.27**, freak-elite **17.54**, FLAT_50_CONTROL **7.69 uniform** (== BODY50_REB50, the anchor held). Team margins unchanged (freak-no-hands still **+2.1**, matching S45/S46 round 1 — pure attribution, no team-total movement). Both isolated curves stayed monotone with the rating-0 ends lifted onto the luck floor (OffReb=0 S5.ORB 0.06 → 0.37; DefReb=0 S5.DRB 0.13 → 0.96). The observation corpus and all eight stress buckets stayed green with sane box scores (bigs ~10–12 REB, guards ~3–5, ORB% ~28%). The four suite picker bounds were re-verified in the Monte Carlo under the final formula and all held (dominant multiplier ~7×, buried guard ~3.5%, PG floor ~10.6%, nerf still cuts the shooter ~37% → ~16%). **The pre-check was end-to-end both rounds:** the mandatory Python Monte Carlo mirrored the C# weight formula constant-for-constant, anchored opportunity counts to the measured sweep totals, produced the archetype table + the full height ladder Emmett ruled on, and predicted the sweep to ~0.02 boards/game.

**Two honest notes carried forward.** (1) **The putback-shooter ripple was negligible** — on the offensive glass the fix also makes the big body the putback shooter (assumption #2, the load-bearing exception), so a rebound-monster/poor-finisher would now take more putbacks; but team ORB totals did not move (freak-no-hands margin +2.1, identical to S45), because the sweep pins Finishing at 50 and so never constructs that archetype. That coupling is real and correct basketball (the guy who got the board takes the putback) and will surface only when a real population exercises it — noted, not a concern here. (2) **The generation-layer rebounding-floor note (S45) must be re-evaluated** — the passive-individual-floor picture changed: a body now confers standalone rebounding pull independent of rating, so the "tall players need a rebounding-rating floor or they rebound like guards" note should be re-sized *after* this ships, not carried forward unchanged.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Engine/Core/OffensiveRebounderPicker.cs` — **EDIT** (the weight expression: luck + rating×multipliers + one-sided body pull + saturating floor, all inside the `× shooterNerf` grouping; retired the `Math.Max(1.0, …)` floor and its stale comments; doc-comment formula updated). `src/Charm.Engine/Core/DefensiveRebounderPicker.cs` — **EDIT** (the same, no shooterNerf; `physicals[]` + `meanPhysical` stages added mirroring the existing wingspan-lineup-mean pattern). `src/Charm.Engine/Config/MatchupConfig.cs` — **EDIT** (five new rebound properties — `ReboundLuckWeight` 5.0, `ReboundBodyPullWeight` 0.35, `ReboundBodyFloorCeiling` 4.0, `ReboundBodyFloorScale` 40.0, `ReboundBodyFloorReference` 22.5 — each range-checked; luck strictly > 0 as it carries the every-slot-can-draw guarantee). `src/Charm.Harness/config.json` — **EDIT** (the five keys, defaulted to the locked values). `tools/rebounder_body_floor_model.py` — **NEW** (the committed archetype-table + height-ladder derivation record, mirroring the C# formula constant-for-constant, with the locked spec and the share→boards/game conversion basis documented). No golden fixture invented (the pickers have none; the sweep bench + Monte Carlo are the proof). No engine file outside the two pickers, no other config, no suite check touched. Docs: this entry; `design.md` — the Phase 10 + Phase 11 per-player-attribution notes updated in place (the pickers are built and now carry the luck + relative-pull + saturating-floor shape; the ORB putback-shooter coupling noted); `docs/attribute-meaning.md` — Family B's flaw subsection updated to "fixed in S46" with the new numbers and the generation-floor re-evaluation flag; `status.md` — the rebounder-picker body floor moves Open → Built, the S46/S46b rulings enter Closed-by-ruling, the family sweeps resume as the next track.

**Next (resume the attribute-meaning family sweeps, the S45 plan the picker fix jumped ahead of):** aim the `sweep` bench at the next attribute family — likely **Body** (Height, Wingspan, Weight) or **Athleticism** — each following the rebounding template (each rating in isolation at 5-point steps + an interaction block where it plausibly fights another attribute). This layer unblocks the generation redesign (height→skill and height→athleticism leans). Its own audited pass; the §6 pipeline drafts the prompt, ChatGPT reviews before build.

## Session 45 — Attribute-Meaning layer, Session 1: the general attribute-sweep findings bench, proven on Rebounding (harness-only; engine untouched) (2026-07-11)

**Scope:** Build the **attribute-sweep findings bench** — one harness instrument, general to any attribute, that pins a flat all-50 world, walks ONE rating on ONE player up its 0–99 range (or runs a set of named stress rows), runs N seeded games per rung through the REAL Resolver/Governor wiring, and tabulates rating → real outcome. This is the first build of the **attribute-meaning layer**: reverse-engineer our own engine one rating at a time so "is SelfCreation 50 good?" finally has an answer measured in a currency that exists. Deliberately a **generalization**, not a from-scratch build — the sweep-one-attribute-and-run-real-games pattern was already hardcoded three times (`SizeExperiment`/`sizetest`, `AthleticismExperiment`/`athtest`, `DefenderExperiment`/`deftest`) and the S24 lab bench already had the flat-50 builder + strict config reader + per-player attribution. The honest job was to factor the common thing into one parameterized bench where *which attribute* and *which stress rows* are inputs, not baked in. **Proven on Rebounding** (the chosen first family: two ratings, and Emmett had a sharp test). This session ships WORKING code, not a plan — the bench ran three times on Emmett's machine and produced the findings below. **No engine constant moved**; the bench MEASURES the current 55/45 rebound split, it does not touch it. The check-in gate was honored — fresh pull, all required source reads (the three experiments, the lab-bench builder pieces, the rebound resolution + both rebounder pickers, the `PossessionRecord` ORB fields, `Program.cs` dispatch), the reuse-vs-new split and the four mechanics calls reported, no file touched until Emmett's explicit "build" (which ruled the four calls: swept player = Team A slot 5 alone, terrible body = 15, 2,000 games/rung, text-config aimed).

**The instrument (`Program.Checks.AttributeSweep.cs`, token `sweep`).** Reuses verbatim: the lab bench's flat-50 baseline (`BenchRatingFields`/`BenchRatingBaseline`), its dialable-field whitelist (`BenchDialableFields` — confirmed to carry both rebounding ratings AND Height/Wingspan/Strength), its per-slot validity rules (`ValidateBenchSpec`) and typed constructor (`BenchSpecToPlayer`), the shared `StampPlayerId`/`SeatRoster`/`AttributeGame` seam, and the 20-argument Resolver + Governor game-run block copied straight from `RunBenchMatchup`. Genuinely new (~560 lines): a strict JSON config reader (two modes — `walk` steps one field, `cases` runs named stress rows), the rung loop, the rebound-focused tally, the console table, and the CSV writer. **Isolation discipline (Emmett's ruling):** every dial except the one under study is pinned to 50 — no random-rolled context — so each curve is the swept rating's pure, exactly-repeatable signal. The swept player is one slot on logical Team A; the opponent is flat all-50. Dispatched by one `sweep` token that `return 0`s before the validation suite (checked directly against `Program.cs`, not inferred from a green suite — assumption #3 of the preamble). Aimed by a live-path text file (`--no-build`, read fresh each run), so every later family session just edits a config and reruns with no recompile.

**Per-player rebound credit is engine truth, not a guess.** The readout reads which individual player grabbed each board from the same engine-stamped attribution the box score uses (`AttributeGame` → `OReb`/`DReb` per slot), so the CSV answers "does *he* personally rebound?", not merely "does the lineup win the glass?". The team ORB rate uses the real `OrbWon/OrbChances` denominator off the possession records; per-player DRB has no chances denominator (the prompt anticipated this), so per-player stays boards-per-game counts. Team totals (summed per-player attribution) and the records-side `OrbWon` are the same boards counted two ways — an internal reconciliation.

**The three proof runs (2,000 games/rung; ~100k games total).** Run 1: OffReb 0→99 by 5 (21 rungs), everything else frozen at 50. Run 2: same for DefReb. Run 3: the interaction block — eight named body×rating stress rows (the cases the isolated sweeps *can't* produce, because they move body and rebounding together).

**The instrument proved itself trustworthy before any finding was read.** `FLAT_50_CONTROL` sat at zero margin (RebΔ −0.2, swept slot ≈ ⅕ of the team's boards); `BODY50_REB50` was numerically identical to the control (same player, different label — the sanity anchor held); each walk moved only its own column (OffReb never bled into DefReb and vice-versa); both curves climbed smoothly with no spikes. Real signal, not noise.

**The finding — rebounding is a rating-gated skill; the body multiplies it, it does not grant it.** The swept center's total boards per game: freak body + zero rebounding instinct = **0.2**, exactly equal to a 5'6"-weakling + zero instinct (0.2) and an average body + zero instinct (0.2). **A 7-foot freak with no rebounding rating grabs the same near-nothing a tiny weakling does.** The head-to-head Emmett asked for is not close: little-guy-with-great-hands **9.6** vs freak-body-no-hands **0.2**. But the body is a real amplifier *once the rating is present*: at elite instinct, weakling 9.6 → average 12.9 → freak 17.3 (≈ +34% average→freak). So: **the rating decides whether you rebound at all; the body scales it once you do** — the multiplicative "weakest-leg" relationship the design aimed for, working. The isolated curves are near-linear across the whole 0–99 range: no dead zone at the bottom, no saturation at the top, the rating pays off continuously (OffReb individual boards 0.06→2.20→3.66; DefReb 0.13→5.49→9.30).

**The flaw the finding exposed (traced to source, NOT fixed this session).** A rebound resolves in two engine steps: (1) which TEAM gets the board — `OffensiveReboundShare` blends team-mean body (45%) and team-mean rating (55%); here the freak's body works exactly right, lifting Team A's glass margin to **+2.1** even with zero rating. (2) which of the five PLAYERS on that team is credited — the rebounder pickers weight each player `max(1, Rating × PositionalWeight × WingspanMultiplier × HustleMultiplier)`. Because the body enters **only as a multiplier on the rating**, a zero-rating freak's product is zero, floored to 1, so he draws ≈1/200 of his team's boards — his huge body helped the team win the board but gives *him* no claim to it. That is the whole 0.2. **This is the one and only per-player selector where a body attribute that should confer standalone individual credit was wired multiplicatively.** The cross-selector audit (all seven pickers read this session) proved the point sharply: **blocks are the correct template** — `BlockerWeight` is *additive* (`BlkHeight·Height + BlkWingspan·Wingspan + BlkVertical·Vertical + BlkRimProtection·RimProtection + …`), so a freak with a zero shot-blocking rating still swats shots on body alone. Steals, assists, and both turnover pickers share the floor-of-1 *shape* but are NOT flawed — they aren't stats where a giant should earn free credit for being tall (steals = hands/instinct; assists = passing; turnovers = a blame stat; interior turnovers are already Strength-based). So the fix is single and well-scoped: make the rebound selector look like the block selector — give height/wingspan/strength their own standalone terms so a freak body has individual rebounding pull independent of his rating.

**Ruling recorded: the 55/45 team split stays.** It delivers the design goal (rebounding is a genuine skill regardless of size); the culprit is the picker's body-as-multiplier, not the team blend. The generation-layer corollary (logged, not acted on): because the engine gives the body almost no passive individual rebounding floor, a tall player's board count lives or dies on his rebounding *rating*, so the eventual generation redesign must give tall players a rebounding-rating floor — otherwise a big with a low draw rebounds like a guard. That is exactly the kind of "what does the population need?" answer the measurement layer exists to produce.

**Verification — the three proof runs are green on Emmett's machine (the only verification that counts).** Build succeeded; all three runs completed and produced sensible, self-consistent output with every built-in control anchor holding (control at zero margin, `BODY50_REB50` == `FLAT_50_CONTROL`, ratings isolated, curves monotone). The bench is a pure addition (one new file) plus a single early-return dispatch line that fires before `RunAllChecks`, so the validation suite path is untouched by inspection of the diff — the standing green-suite confirmation is the commit gate. **No matchup-math Monte Carlo was required or written this session** — the bench changes zero engine math; it reuses existing engine paths, so its correctness is structural (real-engine seam + engine-stamped attribution), verified directly against source.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.AttributeSweep.cs` — **NEW** (the general sweep bench: config model, `walk`/`cases` rung construction, the flat-plus-one-dialed-slot team builder reusing the lab-bench pieces, the game-run loop, the rebound tally, console table + CSV, strict JSON reader). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.cs` — **EDIT** (one line: the `sweep` token dispatch, grouped with the other instrument tokens, `return 0` before the suite). `tools/sweep/sweep_offreb.json`, `sweep_defreb.json`, `sweep_interaction.json` — **NEW** (the three pre-specified rebounding proof configs). No engine file, no config.json, no suite check touched. Docs: this entry; `design.md` — the lab-bench section gains the attribute-sweep-bench subsection (a sibling instrument on the same flat-50 machinery); `docs/attribute-meaning.md` — **NEW**, the findings doc (the rebounding curves + interaction table + the two-step model + the rebounder-picker flaw + the cross-selector audit + the 55/45-stays ruling + the generation floor note); `status.md` — the attribute-meaning layer opens as an active track (bench Built, Rebounding measured), the **rebounder-picker body-floor fix** enters Open as the active next build, the 55/45 ruling enters Closed-by-ruling.

**Next (the obvious redirect, NOT the stale "aim at the next family" plan):** the measurement pass surfaced a concrete, source-confirmed engine bug, so the next session is the **rebounder-picker body-floor fix** — give the offensive and defensive rebounder pickers standalone additive body terms (the `BlockerWeight` shape) so a freak body corrals boards on physical tools alone, oracle-first with an archetype table for Emmett's sign-off (freak-no-hands 0.2 → a sane 3–4, elite holds, weakling-no-hands stays ≈0) before any engine code. Family sweeps (Body, Athleticism, Scoring, …) resume after, each following the rebounding template. Its own audited pass.

## Session 44 — C# port, Phase 2: the LIVE skill-first generator + the statistical population audit (standalone; divvy/season untouched) (2026-07-09)

**Scope:** Build the Pass-2 **live generator** as a standalone path: the three distribution samplers on the RNG interface, the thin 40-slot draw loop that calls the Phase-1 (S43) transforms, the dormant Player seats, and a Phase 60 harness gate that proves the samplers analytically and the 46k population statistically. **Deliberately narrower than the S43 "Next" line planned** — the draft-time audit established that "delete the enforcers + swap the season pool + re-check the page" is not a port: the two enforcers are called from BOTH the `gen` demo and the season talent-pool divvy (`Program.Divvy.cs:239-240`), the divvy is built on positional quotas (80G/60W/60B, coverage roles, the opening-five shape), and the skill-first cohort is **positionless by construction** — it cannot feed a quota-based divvy without a positions-from-orientation apportionment design that does not exist yet. So enforcer deletion, the population swap, and the season re-check are **Phase 3**, which opens with that design conversation; Phase 2 lands a provably-correct generator first so Phase 3 consumes a trusted input instead of debugging generation and apportionment at once. The check-in gate was honored — all seven required reads done and reported, one engineering call flagged, two bands widened with rationale, no file touched until Emmett's explicit go (which carried one ruling: **class variation is legal** — a cohort with zero 7'3"+ players is an honest draw; some classes have more than one).

**The samplers (`Sampling.cs`) — statistical parity, never bit parity.** C#'s `System.Random` is a different stream from Python's `random`, so byte-identical draws are impossible by design and never asserted; what is asserted is closed-form moment agreement (below). **Gaussian:** the `ClockDraw` Box-Muller cos-branch core, UNTRUNCATED (ClockDraw truncates + rejects for the shot clock; generation noise keeps its full tails); the sin twin discarded, matching ClockDraw's own approach. **Exponential:** inverse-CDF `-ln(1-u)/λ`, matching Python's `expovariate`, log guarded the way ClockDraw guards its log. **Beta:** the two-gamma identity `G(a)/(G(a)+G(b))` with Marsaglia–Tsang gamma draws — and the honest-scope call: every Beta parameter pair in this spec has a ≥ 1 and b ≥ 1 (least is orientation's 2.007), so only the k ≥ 1 path exists; the unused k < 1 boost branch is a loud entry assertion, not dead code.

**The live loop (`PlayerGenPass2Live.cs`) — drawing only, zero math.** `GeneratePlayer` fills the fixture-shaped `Pass2Draws` in the locked 40-slot order (the fixture's `draw_order`, asserted by Phase 59) and returns `PlayerGenPass2.BuildFromDraws(draws)` — the math that runs live is the math the fixture replay proves bit-for-bit every harness run. The height branch draws ONE noise value on either branch (Gaussian upper / Exponential lower), preserving the constant per-player budget of 40 semantic draws (each Gaussian slot consumes a Box-Muller uniform *pair* internally — the 40-slot contract is semantic values, not uniform calls). The loop gets `sigma_up` from the new shared `PlayerGenPass2.ComputeHeightShape(o)` — a **pure extraction** of the three contiguous height-shape lines out of `BuildFromDraws` (same expressions, same order), so the loop and the locked transform can never drift on the height shape; Phase 59 re-proves the extracted transform bit-for-bit on every run, which is exactly what protects the lock. One engineering call, flagged at the gate: `Pass2Result` deliberately does not carry the latent dials q and s, which the population audit needs — so the cohort builder returns a tiny `LivePlayer` pair (Draws + Result) rather than widening the locked result type. `BuildCohort(seed, n=46000)` mirrors the oracle's `build_cohort`: n players off one seeded stream.

**The Player seats — dormant by the standing discipline.** `LatentSkills` / `CurrentSkills` / `Runway` (keyed maps, defaulting empty — the Phase-1 result already carries them keyed and a future development layer reads them by key; parallel authored int fields would explode Player.cs by ~60 members), `Arrival` ([0,1], the ruled mechanism), and `PlayerClass` (the S42.1 placeholder label, empty = not Pass-2-generated). None enter `Validate()` — they are not 0–99 authored ratings — and nothing reads them, same as Endurance/Gravity/Spacing: proven occupied seats for the development/season layer, not future placeholders.

**Phase 60 — moments first, then bands; every band one a broken wiring fails.** Gate (0) runs BEFORE any cohort is trusted: N=200k draws per sampler, sample mean/variance against the closed forms — **all four live Beta pairs** (orientation 2.007/2.493, skill 2.3/2.7, athletic 2.2/2.2, spec 2.0/2.0), so a bad orientation path can't hide behind a correct Beta(2,2); tolerances are ~10+ standard errors (a swapped orientation α/β shifts the mean 0.108 against a 0.006 tolerance). Then one canonical 46k cohort (seed 20260706) against design-invariant bands: [A] schema 33 keys in-range; [B] perimeter share 0.55–0.65; [E] |corr(q,Height)| < 0.05 — the core architectural claim; [C] 7'3"+ in **0–40** (widened per Emmett's ruling: canonical is 2, requiring ≥1 would false-red ~13% of honest cohorts; the failure this catches is the *hundreds* a miswired upper tail produces); [C2] stretch bigs > 0 / point-centers ≤ 5 on the recruitable pool; [F2] spike top1−top2 gap strictly above broad; [F3] census max ≤ 7% and **PostMoves ≥ OffBallDefense − 0.5pp** (widened with numbers: the two are near-parity by design, 0.09pp apart canonically, and a strict ≥ would false-red ~30% of honest cohorts, while a broken port — offsets not applied — misses by 2.6pp); [G] recruitable 20k–30k; plus a determinism assert (two same-seed cohorts identical — the reproducibility guard the season layer will lean on).

**The pre-check was end-to-end this session.** The mandatory Monte Carlo mirrored the C# samplers exactly in Python and plugged them into the LOCKED oracle's own `generate_player` as a drop-in RNG shim — so the traced population is what the C# generator produces, statistically. All seven moment checks and all eight bands green on three full 46k cohorts (seeds 20260706 / 777 / 424242). The trace also **validated the [F3] widening empirically**: on the canonical seed the C#-style samplers drew PostMoves 0.12pp BELOW OffBallDefense — an honest draw a strict band would have failed.

**Verification — green on Emmett's machine, the only verification that counts.** Phase 60: all seven sampler moments OK (orientation mean 0.4457 vs 0.4460; exponential mean 6.9798 vs 7.0); bands [B] 0.597, [E] +0.004, [C] 5 giants, [C2] 168 stretch / 1 point-center, [F2] 34.6 vs 11.3, [F3] max Playmaking 6.14% with PostMoves 5.89% vs OBD 6.02% (below strict parity — the widened band's exact case, held), [G] 25,825 recruitable, determinism OK. **Phase 59 re-ran green at 306 players / 51,714 checks / 0 failures / max deviation exactly 0.0 — the proof the extraction changed nothing numerically.** Phases 54 and 55 unchanged, `ALL CHECKS PASSED.` — Phase 2 disturbed nothing downstream.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Engine/Core/Sampling.cs` — **NEW** (Gaussian/Exponential/Beta on `IRng`; Marsaglia–Tsang k≥1 only). `src/Charm.Engine/Core/PlayerGenPass2Live.cs` — **NEW** (the 40-slot draw loop, the `LivePlayer` pair, `BuildCohort`; the oracle's four inline noise shapes named as constants with line cites). `src/Charm.Engine/Core/PlayerGenPass2.cs` — **EDIT** (the pure `ComputeHeightShape` extraction; no other line of the locked transform touched). `src/Charm.Engine/Core/Player.cs` — **EDIT** (the five dormant seats; `Validate()` untouched). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.GenPass2Live.cs` — **NEW** (Phase 60). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.cs` — **EDIT** (one line: Phase 60 joins the chain after Phase 59, so no prior phase renumbers). Enforcers, divvy, season path: untouched. Docs: this entry; `design.md` — the player-generation subsystem gains the Pass-2 live-generator section (the Phase-1 deferral lands, written against the real ported code); `status.md` — Phase 2 → Built, Phase 3 → Open with the reshaped scope recorded.

**Next (Phase 3):** the bridge — how positions/quotas *emerge* from the positionless orientation-drawn cohort, opening with an oracle-side design conversation before any code; then the divvy/season swap, deletion of `GenEnforceFloors`/`GenEnforceLegHealth` (the honest-draw ruling made executable), and the season-page re-check against the S39–S41 calibration. Its own audited pass.

## Session 43 — C# port, Phase 1: the Pass-2 generation MATH, proven exact against the S42.2 replay fixture (2026-07-08)

**Scope:** Port the *deterministic math* of the locked Pass-2 skill-first generation oracle (`tools/gen_pass2_skillfirst_oracle.py`) to C#, and prove it reproduces the committed S42.2 replay fixture **exactly** — integers bit-for-bit, floats at the fixture-declared tolerance. RNG-free transform code + one parity gate + one csproj fixture-copy line; **no live generation path touched**, so the season page cannot move. `design.md` **untouched** (deferred to Phase 2 by ruling at check-in). The port was split into two sessions: Phase 1 (this one) is the math library + its fixture proof; Phase 2 is the live generator, samplers, Player fields, enforcer deletion, population regen, and the statistical audit. The check-in gate was honored — all seven required reads done and reported, one tolerance ruling taken, no file touched until Emmett's explicit go.

**The one ruling taken at the gate — absolute 1e-9 everywhere (Emmett's call, option (b)).** The S42.2 fixture header declares an **absolute** 1e-9 float tolerance; the repo's other cross-language parity gates (tendency, displacement) use a **hybrid relative** form. The prompt recommended editing the fixture header to the hybrid form for one-source-of-truth; Claude recommended the opposite and Emmett ruled with Claude: keep absolute 1e-9, matching the locked fixture, so there is **zero contract drift** and Phase 1 stays pure C# (no Python re-run, no re-commit of a locked artifact). Justified because every compared float in this pipeline sits in roughly [−2, 100], where absolute 1e-9 is *stricter* than the hybrid form and worst-case exp/tanh ULP error amplifies nowhere near it. Integers compare exactly, no tolerance. The C# gate declares and uses the same 1e-9 the fixture header declares.

**The three classic port traps, each attacked at draft time against source and handled once.** (A1) Python's `round()` is banker's rounding (half-to-even); `Math.Round(x, MidpointRounding.ToEven)` agrees — but only if the port never uses `(int)(x+0.5)`, which is round-half-up and silently disagrees on exact halves. Every float→int in the port goes through one `RoundHalfEven` helper. (A2) Round/clamp **order** is per-site and was verified line-by-line: Height alone is round-*after*-clamp (oracle :311), every other integer is clamp-*after*-round; each site mirrors its oracle line exactly, cited in a comment. Confirmed every `int(...)` in the oracle wraps a `round(...)` — no truncation of a raw fraction anywhere. (A3) Both weapon argmaxes take the **first** maximum in DRAWN_SKILLS scan order (replace only on strictly-greater), matching Python's `max()`; a `>=` or LINQ `MaxBy` would take the *last* max and flip the identity on any tie — and the census offsets make ties reachable (fixture player 0 is a live offset-flip: `weapon_raw = Mid`, `weapon = Playmaking`, and the gate checks both fields for all 306).

**The port's shape — a pure transform layer the live generator will reuse.** The new engine file holds the 57 frozen constants transcribed verbatim (oracle names, oracle line cites), the 33-key taxonomy, and pure transform functions that each take their drawn value(s) as **explicit parameters** and draw nothing — height branch/clamp, the 20 base skills, weapon eligibility + both argmaxes, the athletic card, Wingspan/Weight/rebounding, arrival/expression, latent/current per skill, the FreeThrow derivation (the ONE shared `ft_idio` feeding both latent-FT and current-FT), the runway vector, and the recruiting `rscore` + parts. Results land in a plain object — deliberately **not `Player`** (the Player data-shape decision for ~46k actives at scale is Phase 2's, made against that number). The design rule that makes it reusable: in Phase 2 a thin live generator draws from the RNG and calls **these same functions**, so the math proven here is the math that ships — no transform is duplicated between the gate and the future generator.

**The gate — the executable twin of the S42.2 reference reader.** It validates the fixture contract loudly first (schema present; 40-slot draw order exact; all five key-orders exact; the **57-constant echo** asserted against the C# transcriptions — the tripwire; players non-empty) and refuses to replay on any drift, printing itemized mismatches. Then for every one of the 306 players it feeds the recorded draws through the transform layer and asserts every checkpoint, card value, latent/current/runway rating, and recruiting field: integers `==`, floats within 1e-9, weapon strings equal, `eligible` sequence-equal and non-empty, age/class equal-as-recorded (placeholder-output, asserted never recomputed as spec per the S42.1 ruling). On any failure it throws with player index + field + expected/actual and "the oracle wins — fix the port," exactly as the tendency gate does. It runs twice: joined to the default check chain as `Phase59GenPass2ReplayParityCheck()`, and at the start of `RunGen` beside the tendency parity. Seed-independent by construction — it reads the fixture, it generates nothing.

**Verification — green on Emmett's machine, the only verification that counts.** The full harness run showed, under Phase 59: `constants echo vs C# transforms: 57/57 match — tripwire clear`, then `gen pass2 replay parity: 306 players, 51714 field checks, 0 failures; max float deviation 0.000E+000 (tolerance 1E-009 absolute)`, then `ALL CHECKS PASSED.` at the end with every prior check (tendency, displacement, season, stress, observation) unaffected — confirming Phase 1 touched no live path. The C# reproduced the fixture to **exactly 0.0** float deviation, matching the same-interpreter Python round-trip; the port is bit-for-bit the oracle on every one of the 51,714 checks. Sandbox pre-check before delivery: a Python mirror transcribed from the *C# file* (not the oracle) replayed the same 306 players / 51,714 checks / 0 failures / 0.0 deviation, so the transcription was proven before Emmett ran anything.

**One honest miss, caught by Emmett's first run.** The first csproj delivery put the oracle's `--fixture` flag inside an XML comment; XML comments cannot contain a double-hyphen, so MSBuild rejected the project file before compiling. The sandbox has no MSBuild, so the brace/XML pre-checks did not catch it. Fixed by rewording the comment (verified the file parses as valid XML and no illegal `--` remains), re-delivered the single file; the second run was clean. Named plainly, one fix, no other file touched.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Engine/Core/PlayerGenPass2.cs` — **NEW** (the pure transform layer: 57 constants + 33-key taxonomy + the transforms + the `Pass2Draws` input and `Pass2Result` output types; no RNG, no state, no `Player`). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.GenPass2.cs` — **NEW** (the Phase 59 fixture-replay gate + the 40-slot draw-order contract + the constants tripwire). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.cs` — **EDIT** (one line: Phase 59 joins the default chain). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Gen.cs` — **EDIT** (one line: the gate runs at `RunGen` start beside the tendency parity). `src/Charm.Harness/Charm.Harness.csproj` — **EDIT** (one `<None Include>` line copying the fixture beside the binary). No engine logic outside the new file, no config, no golden fixture regenerated, no live generator, no `Player` change. `design.md` — **untouched**, per the check-in ruling (the design.md-level commitments — live generator architecture, Player data shape, enforcer deletion, RNG interface — are made at Phase 2 against real ported code; Phase 1 is a parity-proven math library whose spec already lives in the locked oracle). Docs: this journal entry; `docs/status.md` (the C# port item split — Phase 1 → Built, a new Phase-2 Open item; Last-updated).

**Next (Phase 2):** the live generator — C# Beta/Gaussian/Exponential samplers on the RNG interface (reusing the `ClockDraw` Box-Muller shape for Gaussian), the thin generator that draws and calls the Phase-1 transforms, the `Player` latent/current/runway/arrival fields, deletion of the retired role/leg machinery and the two floor enforcers, the ~46k population regen, a **statistical** population audit against the oracle's targets (NOT byte-parity — the C# RNG stream will not match Python's, by design), and the season-page re-check. The one clamp edge the fixture leaves unexercised (Height == 99) rides along. `design.md` is edited at that session. Its own audited pass.

## Session 42.2 — The replay-fixture micro-session: a deterministic math-replay reference for the Pass-2 C# port; no generation math touched (2026-07-08)

**Scope:** Build the deterministic **math-replay fixture** the upcoming C# port validates against, plus a committed reference reader. Python only — no C#, no `src/`, no harness, and **no generation-math change of any kind**: the session only *records* what the locked Pass-2 oracle already computes and writes it to a fixture. `design.md` untouched. The check-in gate was honored (all reads done, findings reported, no file touched until Emmett's explicit go); five rulings were taken at the gate and all five shipped as ruled.

**The problem this solves.** A stored-output fixture (final cards only) would let the port prove it can *deserialize* a card, not that it *computes* one the same way — and three raw draws are destroyed downstream by clamps (the arrival draw when it binds the [0,1] edge, the height noise by the abs/clamp/round, the age noise by its round/clamp), so a final card cannot be replayed back to its inputs. A true replay fixture records the raw random draws plus every named intermediate, so the port recomputes each value from inputs and checks it — math parity, never mere file-reading. RNG is factored out entirely: the fixture is the frozen record of one seeded run.

**The recording seam is invisible by construction.** `generate_player` gained an optional recorder argument that is written to strictly *after* each draw is assigned and never itself draws a random number; with the recorder absent — every audit path, and the default — the function is byte-for-byte its S42.1 self. Proof: the default oracle run diffs **0 bytes** against the S42.1 baseline output, and all six generation-math functions (`derive_ft`, `build_skill_state`, `rscore_parts`, `rscore`, `build_cohort`, `high_for_size_residual`) are AST-identical to the locked source. About ten inline draws were hoisted to named locals so the recorder could capture them (`x = f(); use(x)` is identical to `use(f())` — the RNG call order is unchanged); the full 40-call-per-player stream order is now a contract, declared in the fixture header rather than inferred from JSON key order.

**Emmett's five gate rulings, all implemented as ruled.** (1) **Schema approved**, with the height branch split into `height_branch_selector_raw` (the raw float draw) and `height_branch` (the derived `upper_gauss`/`lower_exp` string) so the raw float is never confused with the branch. Every recorded final value has a recorded-input recompute path; destroyed raw inputs (clamped arrival, age noise, pre-`abs` height noise) are recorded explicitly. (2) **N = 300 prefix + targeted edge indices**, with the fixture header declaring the full `selection_policy` (prefix count, targeted indices beyond the prefix, and each edge filter's definition + matched index) so the sparse rows are never mysterious later. This is a parity fixture that must exercise branches, not a statistical sample. (3) **Path `tools/gen_pass2_replay_fixture_s42_2.json`** — beside the oracle, following the repo's existing golden convention (`displacement_golden.json`, `fastbreak_golden.json`, `tendency_golden.json`), not a new top-level `fixtures/` directory for one file. (4) **The replay checker is committed** as `tools/gen_pass2_replay_check.py` — a reference reader that reimplements every formula from scratch (zero oracle-function calls, verified by grep) so it demonstrates exactly what "replay from recorded inputs" means for the port, with the **guardrail** that it cannot become a silent second oracle: it imports the constants from the oracle module *and* asserts them against the fixture's constants echo, failing loudly and itemized on any drift before it runs a single replay. (5) **`--fixture` flag** rather than an env var; per the precise wording ruled, the default run stays byte-identical to S42.1 and the `--fixture` run appends trailing announce lines only (it still emits the full normal audit above them, so it is never a silent dump-only path).

**Verification — and this one ran green on Emmett's machine, the only verification that counts.** Every predicted number matched byte-for-byte on his run. (a) Default run vs the S42.1 baseline output: **0-byte diff**. (b) `--fixture` run: the entire `[A]`–`[I2]` audit table is unchanged, with exactly three `[S42.2]` lines appended. (c) Fixture determinism: two `--fixture` runs byte-identical. (d) Recorder cross-check: the recorder pass regenerated **33,795 players, 0 mismatches** against the canonical cohort (the in-run seam proof — same seed, same code path, same people, since the recorder never draws). (e) Replay round-trip: **306 players, 51,714 field checks, 0 failures, max float deviation exactly 0.000e+00**, constants tripwire 57/57 clear — every checkpoint, card value, and recruiting field rebuilt from recorded draws + frozen constants alone. (f) Negative controls (sandbox): a perturbed constant fires the tripwire and blocks replay; a perturbed single draw cascades 11 failures through base→latent→current→card→rscore, exactly the trail a real port mismatch will leave.

**Edge coverage: 12 of 13 targeted creatures present on the canonical seed, the one absence flagged for the port.** A genuine FT hitch exists at index 330 (no fallback needed), the 7'3"+ Gaussian-tail giant at 33794, the tiny-post family at 1416, both FT clamp bounds hit (25 at 4022, 95 at 3918), the arrival [0,1] clamp bound at 110. The single miss is `height_high_clamp` (Height == 99): legitimately absent — 99 is ~4.5σ on the post height branch — recorded as `NONE` in the fixture header and noted so the port session knows that one clamp edge is unexercised by this fixture rather than assuming coverage.

**The contract the port inherits, written into the fixture header.** Comparison convention: integer checkpoints exact; float checkpoints |diff| ≤ 1e-9 (the cross-language allowance for `exp`/`tanh`, which Python's libm and .NET may land ~1 ulp apart; every other operation is plain IEEE-754 double arithmetic and reproduces bit-identically given the same operation order — the same-interpreter replay observed exactly 0.0). Weapon selection contract: `eligible` = `DRAWN_SKILLS` in list order minus excludes/mismatches; the non-empty-eligible invariant (Mid, PAXIS 0.0, never excluded, always passes) held for every fixture player, so the code's fall-back to all skills is unreachable; tie semantics are first-maximum in scan order (replace only on strictly-greater, matching Python's `max`). Ten explicit recompute obligations are listed. The age/class field is recorded for stream completeness but header-labeled **placeholder-output** per the S42.1 ruling: the port asserts the recorded age/cls values and never recomputes them as spec.

**What shipped:** `tools/gen_pass2_skillfirst_oracle.py` — **EDIT** (the recording seam + the opt-in `--fixture` dump section: the 40-slot `DRAW_ORDER` contract, the constants echo, the edge-creature filters, the selection policy, and the fixture writer; all additive, the default path unchanged). `tools/gen_pass2_replay_check.py` — **NEW** (the committed reference reader / round-trip proof). `tools/gen_pass2_replay_fixture_s42_2.json` — **NEW** (the committed fixture, ~1.98 MB, 306 players, seed 20260706). The two evidence text files (audit output in fixture mode, replay-check output) are deliverables but **not committed**, matching the repo's standing convention of not committing oracle output. `design.md` — **untouched**, per scope (it is edited at the port session against real ported code).
