## Session 42.1 — Oracle repair micro-session: weapon census offsets, shared FT idiosyncrasy, age placeholder labeled; the Pass-2 oracle re-locks (2026-07-07)

**Scope:** Three bounded fixes to the locked Pass-2 oracle (`tools/gen_pass2_skillfirst_oracle.py`), then re-lock. Python only — no C#, no `src/`, no harness, `design.md` untouched. The S42 reviewer's "do not reopen calibration" condition did not bind: these were concrete population problems found by audit after the lock, which is exactly the reopening condition it named. The generation architecture is untouched — the three independent draws, the causal dependencies, the recruiting line, the height tail, and the honest-draw doctrine all stand as ruled at S42.

**2a — the weapon census had a selection artifact, fixed with audited offsets on the argmax (Option A, ruled).** The S42 weapon was the natural-best argmax over the eligible set, and that set is asymmetric: neutral skills are weapon-eligible for ~100% of players, axis skills for ~67–88%, so universal skills got more chances to be the maximum (a multiple-comparisons effect) and PAXIS lean amplified it (Mid, never suppressed for anyone, beat Outside even at equal 100% eligibility). Result in the locked census: the most common identity in the universe was "mid-range specialist" (8.94%), third was "foul-drawing specialist" (6.94%), while post-play identity (4.15%) ran rarer than off-ball-defense identity (6.76%) — in a modern-era world whose tendency layer spent two sessions suppressing the mid-range. The fix preserves the chosen-weapon architecture: `weapon = argmax of base[k] + WEAPON_CENSUS_OFFSET[k]` over the eligible set. The offsets (a printed 17-line constant block, the thing Emmett rules on) shift the argmax comparison ONLY — `base[k]` and every piece of downstream card math are untouched, and the weapon's bump and support drain still apply to the true base. The selected identity is the strongest eligibility-CORRECTED candidate; after offsets it may not be the highest raw base — the accepted tradeoff, stated honestly in the source. **Option B — converting the mechanism to a random weighted lottery — is the rejected alternative** (a larger semantic change, explicitly not taken). Offsets were tuned against the census table to a near-flat default target (~5.9% for each of the 17 eligible skills), which Emmett ruled at the table. Proof is the new **[F3] paired-counterfactual census**: both selection rules applied to identical generated pre-weapon bases and eligibility sets (the offsets changed the weapon for 11.2% of players), with the unchanged downstream card math run separately from each counterfactual weapon choice and the unchanged recruiting line evaluated on each resulting card — same person, two candidate weapons, two cards, one recruiting screen. AFTER: every identity lands 5.70–6.02%, Mid demoted to 5.85% (#11), and Emmett's named row answers **PostMoves 6.02% ≥ OffBallDefense 5.93%** on the canonical seed (six-seed mean dead even at 6.02 vs 6.05; six-seed census flat 5.5–6.1% across all skills).

**2b — FreeThrow gains ONE shared player-level idiosyncrasy draw (FT_SIGMA ruled 9.0).** FT was derived purely from Outside and Height — identical inputs gave identical FT every time, contradicting the Session 29 ruling ("skilled players usually shoot better FTs, with real oddballs in the tails handled by the wide draw distribution"): the tails did not exist and the deferred FT-hitch archetype was unreachable (the tanh shape bottomed near ~49; FT_MIN=25 was never hit). The fix is exactly the ruled structure: `ft_idio = gauss(0, FT_SIGMA)` drawn ONCE per player, the SAME value feeding both the latent-FT and current-FT derivations — a persistent shooter-specific trait, not a second development axis (two independent draws would give one player two FT identities and pollute the runway vector, which includes FT, with measurement noise instead of development). Clamped inside `derive_ft` as always. **[F4] proof, with operational definitions fixed in the build prompt so the audit could not be shaped after the fact:** three predeclared Outside×Height bins (n 668–2,846, all ≥100) show SD ≈ 9 in every bin with real min/max spread — a weak-shooting big genuinely reaches the FT floor of 25; the skilled low-FT hitch (Out≥70 & FT<50) runs 2–8 per 46k across six seeds, nearest card a ready junior guard with Outside 87 shooting FT 48 — a genuine broken-stroke player; the auto-line weak big (H≥71 & Out≤40 & FT>80) runs 13–22 per 46k. Rare-but-reachable is the pass condition and it passes; judgment on the hitch archetype itself stays deferred to the season layer per the standing ruling. Reachability proves the tail exists; whether the rates are sensible was Emmett's FT_SIGMA ruling — 9.0 as shipped.

**2c — age/class labeled a placeholder, not redesigned.** Age is hard-coupled to arrival, so "guards arrive developed" was implemented as "guards arrive old" (developed guards average 20–21; ready 18-year-olds occur ~0.03%) — and the ready freshman is a defining creature of modern college basketball. Redesigning now would be the named premature-crystallization failure: whether that cohort is one recruiting class or a standing multi-class pool is exactly the question Session 29 deferred. Verified first that nothing functional consumes the labels (the [G3] decoupling audit is the only substantive reader; the recruiting line reads ratings/Height/orientation only), then added the ruled label to the oracle's output header and the code comment at the age assignment: the season layer owns the real population structure, the one-class-vs-standing-pool question, and the ready-freshman existence requirement; do not port the age/class labels as spec — arrival is the ruled mechanism, the labels are decoration on it. Matching Parked line added to the status board.

**Outside review (one round) came back with two findings; both were correct and both were folded — no pushback needed.** (1) The G4 output *asserted* the "rebound-only 7'3\" scrub stays below the line" invariant in prose while the PRNG-shifted canonical cohort displayed no such scrub — both 7'3\"+ candidates this cohort happened to carry real interior tools and cleared. A proof failure, not a model failure — this project's own §2c discipline caught in the output. Fixed: G4 now searches for and prints the rows instead of asserting — tallest real-tool giant (H=95, interior skill 57, RECRUITABLE at 48.0), tallest canonical rebound-only scrub (H=91, skill 13, glass 65 gated down to +3.0, **below line at 15.5**), and the strict 7'3\"+ scrub via the cross-seed fallback (seed 22: H=93, skill 20, below at 10.3). (2) The `derive_ft` comment claimed the shared draw "never pollutes the runway (latent−current cancels it)" — a load-bearing absolute that fails at the [FT_MIN, FT_MAX] clamp edges, where the shared term can still shift the FT runway entry by a point or two. Softened to the honest claim: no *independent* measurement noise between the two states, not perfect cancellation.

**Re-lock — the full S42 invariant suite re-run and printed, all holding.** Recruitable pool **24,784 → 25,736** canonical, six-seed mean **25,792** — the census fix opens more genuine post identities to the post pathway; still inside 20–30k, so R_LINE stays 17.0 untouched per the prompt's condition. Tall-perimeter cliff six-seed mean 3.2; corr(q, Height) −0.006 global and ~0 within every orientation band; specialization gap 34.6 spiked vs 11.3 broad; tiny-post family 0 via the POST pathway (2 clear legitimately via PERIMETER on real guard tools); guard floor clears via perim and big floor via post; cross-path 1.7%/1.1%; point-centers 0. **Shifts reported to the table, not silently accepted:** stretch bigs 192 → 149 (still exist at scale) and the LeBron two-way wing moved 3/6 → 5/6 worlds [1,3,1,0,3,2] (Wemby holds at 1/6 — marquee unicorns stay generational-and-sometimes-absent). The PRNG caveat was honored throughout: inserting the FT draw shifts every subsequent draw, so no byte-parity against the S42 output is claimed anywhere; determinism is proven within the new code (two runs diff byte-identical), pure stdlib preserved.

**What shipped:** `tools/gen_pass2_skillfirst_oracle.py` — EDIT (the `WEAPON_CENSUS_OFFSET` block + offset argmax with `weapon_raw` kept solely for the paired census; `derive_ft` and `build_skill_state` factored to module level so [F3] can rebuild the same player under the counterfactual weapon — construction is RNG-free, so the factoring does not move the stream; the athletic-loop local renamed off `base`, which the factoring made live past that loop; the once-per-player `ft_idio` draw; the [F3] and [F4] audit sections; the G4 proof rows; header + age-placeholder labels). No C#, no config, no engine change, no golden fixture — parity fixtures generate at the port session against this re-locked oracle, and the [F3] counterfactual scaffolding (`weapon_raw`, `cf_player`) is oracle-audit-only and does not port. Docs: this entry; `docs/status.md` (the S42.1 census and FT rulings amended into the S42 Closed-by-ruling block with its stale numbers corrected in place; the age-placeholder Parked line; Last-updated).

**Next:** unchanged — the **C# port** of the re-locked oracle. The S42 port scope carries forward plus three S42.1 additions: the port implements the offset argmax (the offset table is part of the spec), the shared FT idiosyncrasy draw, and honors the age-placeholder non-porting rule (arrival ports as mechanism; the age/class labels do not port as spec). The next-session prompt is its own audited pass.

## Session 42 — Player-generation Pass 2: the skill-first generation oracle is locked as the C# port spec (2026-07-07)

**Scope:** Build and lock the Pass-2 **skill-first** player-generation Python oracle (`tools/gen_pass2_skillfirst_oracle.py`) to the §3 model. Oracle-only, by ruling: no C#, no `src/`, no harness, and `design.md` deliberately untouched (it is edited at the C# port session, not now). The oracle is both the port specification and the calibration reference; the port is the next session. The "v1 skill-first oracle" the original brief referenced **never existed** (it was the retired body/package-gate oracle) — Emmett ruled build-fresh, so there is no legitimate v1→v2 before/after, a rejection pushed back through the outside review twice and documented in the oracle's own output header.

**The model — skill-first, no-gate, column-by-column** (orientation → height → size → athletic quality → skill → potential/runway). Three **independent** quality draws (skill-quality q, athletic-quality a, specialization s) plus orientation o, and only **three causal dependencies**: orientation conditions the height ceiling, size conditions the athleticism landing, orientation conditions arrival/runway (guards arrive developed with short runway; posts arrive raw as fundable projects). Quality is body-independent by construction — `corr(q, Height) = +0.001` globally and within every orientation band. The card emits the full **33-key** contract; `current` is the expression-adjusted 21 skills, `card` the full physical+skill card, latent skill drawn at birth and suppressed toward baseline by arrival stage, `runway` the 21-skill latent−current vector.

**Chosen-weapon specialization is a true single-identity mechanism, not a cluster contrast.** After orientation sets the legal skill family, ONE skill is the weapon (`WEAPON_BUMP 0.62`, `SUPPORT_DRAIN 0.42`, glue skills — IQ/Discipline/HelpDefense — never eligible): broad at low s, one spiked identity at high s. Proven at the archetype table: spiked cards show a top1−top2 gap of 34.5 versus 11.3 in the broad group.

**The population shape Emmett ruled at the table.** A height→orientation logistic knee toward post plus a Gaussian upper height tail cut 7'3"+ giants from a bloated ~470/cohort to **3** — a realistic pyramid, not a warehouse of centers. Shooting was made orientation-neutral (Outside/Mid don't lean perimeter) so **stretch bigs exist** (~190 6'8"+ shooters with no handle) while **point-centers stay ~0** (handle stays perimeter-locked). Marquee unicorns are generational-and-sometimes-absent by design — the strict Wembanyama identity appears in 1/6 sampled worlds, the LeBron two-way wing in 3/6; exact once-per-century framing is deferred to the season layer, not forced onto generation.

**The recruiting line — the one piece that took five adversarial-review rounds.** It is an **oracle-only downstream export proxy** that sizes the recruitable pool (~24.8k canonical, six-seed mean 24,872, inside the 20–30k target); it is not part of the card and does not alter one. It hardened into a continuous, orientation-weighted, pathway-gated score through a sequence of Emmett rulings, each folded only after verification against the live oracle:
- **A body or one weapon may amplify a pathway; neither substitutes for every other tool.** Rebounding is gated by interior skill (it can amplify a real post game, never solo-carry) — so a 7'3" scrub whose only asset is physical-card rebounding, with interior skill at replacement (~26–27), stays **below the line**; only a genuine interior tool (the interior-34 giant) exports.
- **Interior skill cashes by height access** — a logistic curve with its inflection at ~6'2, plus a sub-6'0 taper (released to full at 6'0, so 6'1 and 6'8 are untouched). A 5'8" post savant is stranded (RScore 4.8), a 6'1" post is genuinely borderline (19.1), a 6'8" raw tool is real. The **entire tiny-post family** (12 canonical 5'8"–5'9" post-scorer candidates) now clears **zero** times through the post pathway — the population rule, proven in the audit, not just a named case.
- **Mid is access-gated** — a lone midrange rating is not a guard entry; it only cashes paired with handle/off-ball/shot.
- **Orientation-weighted selection** — `perim_weight = 1 − 0.45·o`, `post_weight = 0.55 + 0.45·o`, applied before the max, so a perimeter card cannot clear on a post spike nor a post card on a perimeter spike unless genuinely hybrid. Cross-path exceptions are modest and honest: 1.2% perimeter-class clear via post, 1.7% post-class via perimeter — continuous blur concentrated near the hybrid band, not a role table.

**The honest-draw doctrine held through every round.** No redraws, no competency repairs, no rating floors added post-draw, no role/position packages — the generator stays an honest cohort and the recruiting line is pure downstream selection. The reviewer's final verdict was green: lock as the C# port spec, and do not reopen calibration unless the port reveals a fidelity mismatch or the first real rosters produce a concrete population problem.

**Proof lives in the oracle's own output**, so a reviewer inherits the proof rather than the chore: `[G4]` pathway export audit (every 7'3"+ candidate with verdict + winning pathway; the tiny-post family split by pathway; the lowest recruitable guard clearing via perim and lowest big via post; the cross-path counts), `[I2]` marquee-unicorn frequency across six seeds, the specialization audit, the threshold-sensitivity table, the arrival/class-decoupling audit, and the rare tall-perimeter cliff (six-seed mean 3.0 recruitable 6'10"–7'0" perimeter players). Deterministic; runs on pure stdlib (`random`/`math`) for a clean C# port.

**What shipped:** `tools/gen_pass2_skillfirst_oracle.py` — **NEW** (the locked oracle, ~800 lines, with its self-documenting output header including the v1-absence note). No C#, no config, no engine logic, no new golden fixture (parity fixtures are generated at the port session against this oracle). `docs/design.md` — **deliberately untouched**, per the standing ruling that it is edited in place at the port session, so the port's structural decisions are written against real ported code rather than an intended spec. Docs: this journal entry; `docs/status.md` (Pass-2 oracle locked; the C# port promoted from Parked to the next-session build; the Pass-2 generation-model rulings recorded under Closed-by-ruling).

**Next:** the **C# port** of this oracle — the live-generator rewrite that adds Player fields for latent/current/runway/arrival/class, deletes the retired body/package-gate floors (`GenEnforceFloors`/`GenEnforceLegHealth`), and validates against a golden fixture generated from this locked oracle. Preserve the contracts the review named: three independent draws; only orientation→height, size→athleticism, orientation→arrival dependencies; chosen-weapon specialization; current/latent/runway separation; full 33-key emission; honest cohort followed by downstream recruitable export; orientation-weighted continuous pathway selection; and no generator repair, rejection, redraw, or role-package resurrection. The next-session prompt is its own audited pass.

## Session 41 — The scoreboard session: assists recentered to target, the turnover mix goes 50/50 live, the rebound instrument audited (2026-07-06)

**Scope:** Three small, independent calibration fixes to make the season page trustworthy before player-generation Pass 2 changes the population underneath it. (A) the assist dials are recalibrated so the league lands 13.5 (from 17.4 HIGH); (B) the halfcourt turnover mix moves to the ruled 50/50 live/dead so steals rise toward 6.2 (from 4.5 LOW); (C) the rebound page gets an explicit provenance audit and — since the reconciliation could not be met page-only — an honest credited-only caveat plus an unreconciled candidate-endings diagnostic, so the LOW verdict is *understood* rather than falsely resolved. **No committed engine-logic change:** (A) and (B) are config values plus their C# default twins; (C) is one harness page file. The committed diff is exactly four files.

**A was measured, not assumed — and the measurement rewrote the plan.** The build prompt's arithmetic assumed the lineup passing factor sat at ~1.09 (a modest bump above the placeholder midpoint of 50). A temporary, uncommitted resolver probe — recording the pre-clamp `LineupPassingFactor` on every eligible non-putback made FG across the full 5,205-game season, then reverted before any committed edit — measured the actual **eligible-make-weighted mean factor at 1.192** over 252,084 eligible makes, with the drafted-starter population mean AssistWeight at **71.77**. The placeholder midpoint of 50 assumed lineup AssistWeight centers at the middle of the 0–100 scale; generated starters average ~71, so the tanh sat well up its curve and inflated every assist by ~×1.19. This is exactly the divergence the oracle-first / measure-first discipline exists to catch: the prompt's ×0.776 estimate was built on the wrong factor. (`PossessionRecord` carries no `Putback` field — only `OrbWon`, an imperfect proxy — so the clean eligible-make weight was not reconstructable from records; the temporary resolver probe was the route, per the A1 preflight, and it never entered the committed diff.)

**A2 — recenter, then trim, and the divergence made the trim *gentler*, not harsher.** The midpoint was recentered from 50 to **71.31** by solving the tanh zero-balance condition (bisection over the probe's factor histogram, inverting `factor → x` bin-by-bin), which drives the eligible-make-weighted pre-clamp factor to exactly 1.0. Because the recenter did far more work than the prompt planned, the follow-up uniform zone-base trim came out at **×0.8909**, not the estimated ×0.776. That relieved the flagged call: the prompt worried a uniform trim would push the three-point assisted share to the "high-60s%," below the real-world ~80%; instead every zone landed near real-world (three ~78% / long ~55% / mid ~45% / short ~38% / rim ~48%), because the milder trim only had to close the residual the recenter left. The five bases moved 0.88→0.784, 0.62→0.5524, 0.50→0.4455, 0.43→0.3831, 0.54→0.4811 — uniform, preserving the ordering.

**A realized-assist model, fitted to the live run, is what let the recenter and trim ship together.** Rather than run recenter-only, read the page, then derive the trim from that read (the strict S38.1 two-pass), a per-zone realized-rate model was built over the probe's factor distribution and the page's zone-make mix — and it reproduced the live 17.4 assists to within 0.2% (model 17.36). That fit is what earned confidence to **bundle** recenter + trim in one committed pass, with the one-iteration allowance as backstop. It landed **13.7 (t13.5, OK)** on the first run — no iteration needed. (This bundling was flagged to Emmett as a call, deviating from the prompt's literal recenter-read-trim sequencing; the model fit was the justification, and it held.)

**B — the halfcourt turnover mix goes 50/50 live/dead (Emmett's ruling).** A weights-only rebalance, no Roll C code: Base live .34→.50 (BadPassIntercepted .18→.265, LostBallLiveBall .16→.235), the dead menu scaled to .50 with its internal shape preserved; EntryBackcourt live .30→.50 the same way (tiny volume, scaled for consistency, the last dead digit carrying the rounding remainder so each context sums to exactly 1.0). Transition was already at 50/50 and untouched. Steals rose **4.5 → 6.5 (t6.2, OK)** — landing on target, not even HIGH, a hair better than the honest 6.6–6.9 expectation. The realized `steals/turnovers` box proxy is ~47% (below the configured ~50% because Roll K's live-ball turnovers are steal-less — the known parked dilution, reported not fixed). Total turnover rate held at 13.8 (Roll C mass preserved — the reweight is within-context). The "to start" ruling landed on-target, so no follow-up back-off of the live share is needed yet.

**C — the rebound instrument audited; the reconciliation gate (C0) degraded to diagnostic-only, as expected.** Before building any verdict, each candidate dead-ball ending was traced to source. `OutOfBoundsOffOffense` and `LooseBallFoulOnOffense` are Roll I/M terminals; `MissOutOfBoundsLost` is the Roll H shot-miss terminal — all provably rebound-opportunity-only. But **completeness could not be proven page-only**: a `JumpBallArrow` label carries no rebound-origin provenance, and jump balls feed in from Rolls A/B/F/I/J/K/M, so the rebound-scramble arrows cannot be separated from the rest without a new counter (which the session forbids). So the page does **not** build a verdict row against 34.5. Instead it prints a footnote on `rebounds (credited)` (the public target includes uncredited team rebounds this instrument does not yet fully measure) and a pure diagnostic line — `candidate dead-ball possession endings (NOT reconciled to rebounds)`: OutOfBoundsOffOffense 0.99 | jump-ball arrows 1.44 | LooseBallFoulOnOffense 0.37 | MissOutOfBoundsLost 1.08 | sum 3.88. The ~3.88 sum is numerically close to the ~3.8 credited gap, but that near-match is explicitly labeled NOT a reconciliation — a possession-ending count must not wear a rebound's clothes. A reconciled team-rebound line is now a named future item needing rebound-provenance instrumentation.

**One honest miss.** The first Delivery-2 build failed to compile on one line of the Phase C page block: two interpolated strings were concatenated *inside* a single `Inv(...)` call (`Inv($"…" + $"…")`), which produces a `string`, but the local `Inv` helper takes a `FormattableString`. The file's own idiom is `Inv($"…") + Inv($"…")` — each piece wrapped separately. A brace/paren pre-check can't see a type error without a compiler; fixed on the next delivery, everything else in the four files was already correct.

**Validation — green, all three targets in band, no iteration.** The full suite ran **ALL CHECKS PASSED** (stress test included): the Roll C batch check re-baselined itself against the new configured pie, and Phase 39's assist check is rate-agnostic (it asserts picker mechanism — shooter self-exclusion, clamp math — not any rate), so neither the reweight nor the recenter broke it. The 347-page (seed 20260703, 5,205 games) landed **assists 13.7 (OK), steals 6.5 (OK)**, and the rebound diagnostic exactly as designed (credited 30.7 unchanged with its footnote + the sum-3.88 candidate line). Two expected second-order drifts, both pre-authorized as routing composition: FG% nudged 44.9 → 45.0 (now a hair over the +1.0 band edge) and fast-break FGA share 14.1% → 15.4%, both because more live turnovers push more possessions into transition — small, explained, not a defect. Blocks 4.1 HIGH and turnovers 13.8 HIGH are pre-existing and out of scope.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Harness/config.json` — EDIT (assist midpoint 50→71.31 + five zone bases trimmed ×0.8909; Roll C Base and EntryBackcourt live/dead reweighted to 50/50, byte-consistent with the C# defaults). `src/Charm.Engine/Config/MatchupConfig.cs` — EDIT (assist defaults + the stale "midpoint=50 the league-average reference" comments corrected in place). `src/Charm.Engine/Config/RollCConfig.cs` — EDIT (Base + EntryBackcourt turnover weights). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Season.Calibration.cs` — EDIT (rebound-provenance footnote + unreconciled candidate-endings diagnostic). No committed engine-logic change, no new field, no new counter, no oracle (the "oracle" here was the reverted measurement probe + the fitted realized-rate model, both offline). The temporary A1 probe (`AssistProbe.cs` + a one-line resolver hook + the harness enable/dump/secondary walk) was reverted and never committed. **Micro follow-up flagged, not fixed:** `AssistPicker.cs`'s doc comment still cross-references "AssistPassMidpoint = 50 the league-average reference" — left stale deliberately to hold the four-file committed diff; correct it on the next touch of that file. ## Session 40 — Shooting fouls count toward the team-foul total: the bonus fills, league FTA lands on target (2026-07-06)

**Scope:** One engine line plus its proof. Until now **only non-shooting fouls incremented the team-foul total** — a shooting foul (the majority of all fouls) resolved straight to free throws and never touched `FoulTracker`. So teams crawled toward the 7-foul bonus far slower than real basketball, the bonus free-throw bucket stayed mostly empty, and the season page read FTA LOW (15.8 vs 19.5) and FT-rate LOW (0.27 vs 0.34) while FT% itself was fine — the shooting was healthy; players just didn't get to the line enough. This session makes a shooting foul count toward the opponent's bonus, exactly like every non-shooting defensive foul already does. No shot-resolution change, no make-curve touch — a pure correctness fix whose page movement is measured, not asserted.

**The one-line fix (Emmett ruled the clean version first).** At the conductor's `ResolveShootingFreeThrows` resolution, alongside the shooting-foul record, one statement: `_game.Fouls.Increment(c.State.Defense)`. A shooting foul is a defensive team foul; it now feeds the tracker like any other. Deliberately the **direct** increment, **not** `DefensiveFoulCharge.Resolve` — that shared node reads the bonus and *forks*, which would wrongly convert the shooter's own trip into a one-and-one. The shooting-foul branch always calls `DriveFreeThrows(..., oneAndOne: false)` on the shot-derived 1/2/3 count and never reads `BonusFor`, so charging the team foul only moves *future* possessions' bonus reads — the shot the whistle was on is untouched. `FoulTracker.Increment` draws no RNG, so the pre-bonus stream stays byte-identical; only post-bonus game flow diverges, which is the intended effect. The engine now has exactly **two** foul-increment sites (non-shooting via `DefensiveFoulCharge`, shooting via this line) and still **one** bonus-fork site (`DefensiveFoulCharge`); the two paths are disjoint, so there is no double-charge.

**The re-baseline turned out to be zero edits — and that was surfaced at the check-in, not discovered by surprise.** The build prompt (correctly) framed this as the §2a stateful-accumulation class: the bonus now arrives earlier, so any check that drives many possessions on one shared `GameState` and asserts foul counts, bonus state, or FTA source could move and would need re-baselining to the new, correct behavior. Auditing the candidate set against live source before touching anything showed the ripple would land only in checks that do not *assert*: the per-roll bonus-fork checks (D/I/J/K/M) inject non-shooting fouls directly on fresh/controlled state, so the shooting path never fires in them; `GameLifecycle`'s first check *reports* its post-run foul number (its hard assertions are possession-conservation) and its sub-checks use direct increments / NoShot configs; and `Program.Observation.cs`'s free-throw-source and fouls-per-game lines are explicitly *recorded, not judged*. The honest verdict given up front was: the movement should surface in diagnostics that are supposed to grow, not in failing assertions — but that could not be *proven* without running the suite, so Phase 3 was "ship, run, re-baseline anything that actually FAILs." It ran clean; the whole-suite FAIL count was **zero**. Phase 3 resolved to no edits, as flagged.

**The mechanism check is the suite-side proof (`ShootingFoulFeedsBonusCheck`).** The exact-count identity is only valid under isolation: a shooting-foul trip whose final FT *misses* goes live → Roll M, whose loose-ball-defense arm would charge an *incidental* team foul and contaminate the count. So the fixture pins **Roll L to Make = 1.0** (every trip ends on a made final FT and never reaches Roll M) and **Roll M to its DefensiveRebound terminal** (belt-and-suspenders) — the same isolation `RollLFreeThrowCheck` uses. Shooting fouls are driven **through the resolver** (so they exercise the real S40 line); non-shooting fouls via `DefensiveFoulCharge.Resolve` directly; both mutate the same shared `game.Fouls`. Six tests, all green on Emmett's compiled binary: (T1) six shooting fouls leave the defense at 6, bonus None; (T2) a seventh, non-shooting foul turns the bonus on at exactly 7 and routes `ResolveFreeThrows`/`OneAndOne`; (T3 — the load-bearing one) a shooting foul driven *as* the seventh increments the count once **and** still resolves as a 1-shot and-1, never a one-and-one (trip spins = 1, bonus now on for the future); (T4) the next non-shooting foul reads the persisted post-shooting count (8, still OneAndOne); (T5) an offensive foul charges nobody (charges stay turnovers); (T6) conservation — the defense's total equals shooting + non-shooting fouls charged to it, zero leak to the offense. T3 is what guarantees the fix cannot corrupt the shooter's own trip.

**Validation — green on the first run, no scaffolding bugs.** The full suite ran **ALL CHECKS PASSED** with zero FAIL lines anywhere, including the new mechanism block and every re-baseline candidate (unmoved). The payoff shows in the free-throw-source split on the frozen corpus (identical rosters, identical shot math — so it isolates the bonus-timing change cleanly): the **bonus share of FTA rose to ~42%** (picker 24.8% + selected 17.2%), up from the ~27% it sat at before — the starved bucket filling. On the two instruments this run captured, **FTr (FTA/FGA) landed 0.34** (frozen-corpus observation) and **0.348** (20-school Phase-55 fixture calibration, 11,859 FTA / 34,058 FGA), and **FTA/team/game ≈ 19.1 / 19.8** — bracketing the 19.5 target, up from 15.8. No regressions: every per-zone FG% held in band (rim 60% / three 33%), pace fine (70.4/team), mechanics reconciled (zero parks, no throws), and the 4,000-game stress test passed all eight buckets with side-neutrality intact.

**The 347-page confirms it (seed 20260703, 5205 games).** FTA **15.8 → 19.3** (target 19.5, OK) and FT rate **0.27 → 0.34** (target 0.34, OK) — both landed on target from the bonus fix alone, no shot math touched. Every per-zone FG% held in band (rim 61.1 / short 42.9 / mid 39.3 / long 36.4 / three 33.8), FG% 44.9 (OK, still the high edge), 3PA rate 0.39 and pace 70.2 unmoved — confirming the fix rippled only through foul timing, nothing else. The remaining out-of-band page gaps are untouched and unchanged (rebounds 30.6 / offensive 8.8 and steals 4.5 LOW; assists 17.4, turnovers 13.8, blocks 4.1 HIGH; OT 2.5% LOW), correctly — the bonus fix was never going to move them. **Residual read for bridge #3:** FTA reached target from the bonus fix alone, so the parked shooting-foul-*rate* bump, the `FoulDrawing` diagnosis, and late-game intentional fouling stay parked and are **no longer urgent** — the whistle rate did not need raising to close the gap; the missing fouls were the ones the tracker was silently dropping.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Engine/Core/Resolver.cs` — EDIT (one line at the `ResolveShootingFreeThrows` resolution: `_game.Fouls.Increment(c.State.Defense)`, with the direct-not-`DefensiveFoulCharge` rationale in comment). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.Fouls.cs` — EDIT (new `ShootingFoulFeedsBonusCheck`, T1–T6, with the Roll L Make=1.0 / Roll M DefensiveRebound isolation fixture). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.cs` — EDIT (one registration line). No config, no new field, no RNG draw, no oracle (there is no math curve here — the fix is a state increment, validated by the mechanism check + the page read). Docs after the green run: this entry; `docs/design.md` (the `DefensiveFoulCharge` section's "single place fouls cross the bonus" claim refined in place to "single charge point for non-shooting, sole fork point, two increment sites as of S40"; the Roll L shooting-FT sequencing paragraph noted the edge now charges the team foul); `docs/status.md` (FTA/FT-rate driver → the bonus fix shipped; the three bridge-#3 items logged under Parked as no-longer-urgent; FTA-LOW verdict → improved, 347-page residual pending).

**Next:** with FTA closed by the bonus fix, the remaining season-page gaps are the open field — **rebounds-LOW / steals-LOW** (the credited-rebound / live-ball reconciliation) and **assists-HIGH / turnovers-HIGH / blocks-HIGH** (likely probabilistic-attribution artifacts more than real over-production), plus **OT-LOW**. **Player-generation Pass 2** (tweener-post existence, weakest-leg development) remains bridged and ready. Pick the gap before drafting; the next-session prompt is its own audited pass.

## Session 39 — Three-point volume: the era profile is retuned so the population takes more threes, and the realized league 3PA rate lands on 0.39 (2026-07-06)

**Scope:** Oracle-first math retune of the tendency era profile — five weight-space multipliers — plus its C# mirror, a re-sync of the fast-break Mean denominators, and both golden fixtures regenerated. This is the **third and final** three-point piece: S38 fixed the transition diet (5% → 34.5%), S38.1 fixed the make curve (all five per-zone FG% on target), and S39 fixes **volume**. It is the first change to the population-selection (generation) layer — the smallest step toward Pass 2 — and it is a pure *selection* change: no make-curve touch, no new engine logic, only a retuned constant and a re-pinned denominator.

**The basketball (Emmett ratified at the archetype table).** The era profile encodes shot-selection *culture* as five numbers applied after peakedness, cleanly separated from individual *capability*. It moved **Mid 0.50 → 0.44, Long 0.70 → 0.63, Three 2.10 → 2.44** (Rim and Short untouched): the three multiplier up, the mid-range the primary donor, long twos additionally trimmed, the rim protected but not invariant. That lifts the population's three diagnostic from **~35.5% to ~39.0%** (seed-stable across three seeds). Every archetype that can actually shoot takes more threes — pure shooter 77→79, floor general 41→46, multi-level wing 43→48, stretch big 65→69 — while the three players who *cannot* shoot (post bruiser, rim runner, true non-shooter big) do not move at all, staying pinned at their ~4% occasional-heave floor. The era shifts the culture; it does not hand threes to players who can't take them. The illustrative "modern shape" the build prompt sketched landed at 40.0; the live derivation was tuned a hair gentler to hit the 39.0 target dead-on.

**The one structural ruling — guard the identity, retire the stale absolute.** The bump pushed the multi-level wing's diet to `31/6/10/5/48`, breaking the oracle's era-stale `max <= 45` check. That number was always a proxy for "this is a multi-level scorer, not a pure shooter"; it was retired for a five-part **identity-guard set** that names what actually matters: bounded three (≤50), protected rim (≥25), live mid-range (≥8), not three-lopsided (Three − Rim ≤ 20), and still flatter than a pure shooter (max < shooter's max). The proposed diet passes all five (48 / 31 / 10 / 17 / 48<79). This guards the archetype's basketball identity against future era retunes instead of pinning it to a single number that any culture shift invalidates.

**The ripple — re-sync the fast-break Means so the break stays calibrated, not double-counted.** The fast-break diet bends each runner's transition shot menu by the ratio of his own three tendency to the *league mean* tendency (`(share / mean) ^ Beta`). Those `FastBreakMean{Zone}` denominators are a hardcoded copy of the tendency oracle's population diagnostic, carried in three places (the engine config default, the harness config.json, and the fast-break oracle's `MEAN`). When the era retune raised every player's three tendency, leaving the mean stale at 0.355 would have inflated every ratio — the population would take more threes in the half court *and* the break would balloon on top, double-counting the same culture shift. Re-syncing the mean to the new diagnostic (**0.335/0.155/0.098/0.058/0.355 → 0.324/0.147/0.084/0.056/0.390**, byte-consistent across all three copies, deliberately NOT renormalized — they are a five-coordinate denominator, not a pie) keeps the transition bend calibrated to the new baseline. The realized transition three barely moved (32.0% → 32.2% in the oracle, 34.9% on the page) — which is correct: the volume gain lands honestly on the half-court side, where raw tendencies drive selection, not on the break.

**One tooling fix folded in.** The tendency oracle's golden-fixture emit was CWD-relative (`open("tendency_golden.json")`) — a false-green hazard, since regenerating from the repo root would drop the new fixture there while the committed one at `tools/` stayed stale and the harness validated the stale copy. It now resolves `Path(__file__).with_name(...)` like the fast-break oracle already did, so a regeneration from any working directory always overwrites the committed fixture.

**Validation — clean on the first run, no bugs, no ladder bump.** Unlike S37 and S38 (each had test-scaffolding bugs caught on Emmett's first run), this session went green first try — because there was no new code path to break: the only C# change was a mirrored constant, and the stage-wise parity check that guards it already existed. The three gates, in order: **tendency parity** (`-- gen`) read *19 vectors, all stages within tolerance, all diets exact* — the era-profile mirror proven exact against the regenerated fixture; **the full suite** ran ALL CHECKS PASSED, including **Phase 58** reproducing all 14 fast-break vectors × 2 paces with zero mismatches and no config-vs-default drift (the three Mean copies agree); **the season page** (seed 20260703, 347 schools, 5205 games) landed the payoff: **3PA rate 0.36 → 0.39 (OK, on target)** and **aggregate FG% 45.3 → 44.9 (OK, back in band)**, together, in a single pass — the pre-authorized ladder bump was not needed. 3P% held at 33.9 (OK) and all five per-zone FG% stayed in band (RollH untouched, no make-curve drift — the extra threes came purely from selection).

**One honest note, flagged not chased.** FG% landed at 44.9 — inside the ±1.0 band but at its high edge, not dead-center on 44.0. This is a pure shot-MIX result (more 33.9%-make threes pulling the aggregate down from 45.3), with every per-zone FG% clean, so it is a composition observation to record, never a reason to touch the make curve. The other standing page misses (FTA-LOW, FT-rate-LOW, rebounds-LOW, steals-LOW, assists-HIGH, turnovers-HIGH, blocks-HIGH, OT-LOW) were all out of band before this session and are out of scope; they are the open calibration candidates for a future ruling, FTA-LOW the front-runner.

**What shipped:** `tools/tendency_oracle.py` — EDIT (pathlib import; emit resolves beside the oracle, unused `path` param dropped; `ERA_PROFILE` retuned to `[1.00, 0.66, 0.44, 0.63, 2.44]`; the `max<=45` structural check replaced by the five-part identity-guard set). `tools/tendency_golden.json` — REGENERATED (19 vectors, new profile). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Gen.cs` — EDIT (`TendEraProfile` mirrored constant-for-constant). `src/Charm.Engine/Config/RollGConfig.cs` — EDIT (five `FastBreakMean` defaults + the comment quoting them). `src/Charm.Harness/config.json` — EDIT (five `FastBreakMean` values). `tools/fastbreak_diet_oracle.py` — EDIT (`MEAN`). `tools/fastbreak_golden.json` — REGENERATED (14 vectors, off the new mean + new tendency). No engine-logic change; `FastBreak{Zone}` base pie, Beta, caps, PaceTilt, and all RollH midpoints untouched. Docs after the green run: this entry; `docs/design.md` (era-profile section rewritten in place with the new numbers, the identity-guard ruling, and the emit-path fix; the fast-break Means quote updated); `docs/status.md` (three-point thread → Closed; 3PA-rate + FG% verdicts → OK; the era-profile volume lever recorded as a Closed ruling; the generation-layer bridge noted).

**Next:** the three-point arc is closed; the season page's remaining calibration gaps are the open field, with **FTA-LOW / FT-rate-LOW** (a population-sensitive whistle/foul-rate tune, deliberately deferred past the generation build) the front-runner standalone miss. **Player-generation Pass 2** (tweener-post existence, weakest-leg multiplicative development) is now bridged by this first generation-side change and its proven oracle→archetype-table→parity workflow. Target is Emmett's ruling; the next-session prompt is its own audited pass.

## Session 38.1 — Perimeter make-curve tune: the two cold outer zones land on target in one oracle iteration (2026-07-06)

**Scope:** Config-only calibration micro-session (two midpoint values, no code), run off the S38 fast-break season page. That page showed the two perimeter zones shooting ~1 point cold — long FG% 34.9 (target 36.0) and three FG% 32.9 (target 34.0) — while rim/short/mid were on target. This is the make *rate*, independent of the three-point *volume* thread: recentering a zone's midpoint changes how well a given rating shoots, not how many of those shots get taken. Fixing the shot before adding volume to it is the agreed sequence.

**Oracle-first, exactly as designed.** `tools/make_midpoint_oracle.py` was run with the five per-zone observed/target pairs from the page. Per protocol only the two out-of-band zones were applied; the three in-band zones (rim +0.2, short −0.1, mid +0.6 — all inside ±1.0) were left untouched, since nudging a passing zone risks knocking it out the other way (the oracle's proposed mid +2.16 would have shoved a passing 39.6 down toward 39.0). Applied: **LongMidpoint 102.6819 → 99.3440** and **ThreeMidpoint 109.9675 → 106.5661** (lower midpoint = the shot is a touch easier per rating = observed FG% moves up).

**One clean iteration — both zones landed dead center.** Re-run at seed 20260703: **long FG% 34.9 → 36.1** (target 36.0, +0.1) and **three FG% 32.9 → 33.9** (target 34.0, −0.1), both OK with no overshoot; the untouched zones held (rim 61.1, short 42.9, mid 39.7). The aggregate 3P% line moved 32.9 → 33.9 (OK). No second iteration needed — the derive-apply protocol landed in one pass, the textbook outcome.

**One honest side effect, flagged not chased.** Correctly raising the two cold outer zones lifted aggregate FG% from 44.9 (OK) to **45.3 (HIGH by 0.3 vs the 44.0 blend)**. This is a shot-MIX consequence, not a make-curve one: the zone mix under-weights threes (3PA rate 0.36 vs 0.39), so the average isn't diluted by enough low-FG% three attempts. It routes to the already-parked **three-point-volume / generation-tendency** thread — and that fix (generating players a touch more three-inclined) pulls aggregate FG% *down* toward 44 while raising 3PA at the same time. The two move together. Not a reason to touch the make-curve, which is done.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Harness/config.json` — EDIT (two RollH midpoints: LongMidpoint 99.3440, ThreeMidpoint 106.5661). No code. Docs: this micro-entry; `docs/status.md` (per-zone FG% all OK, make-curve done; the new FG%-HIGH verdict noted as routing to the volume thread); `docs/design.md` make-midpoint section (a S38.1 current-state note). Recommended before commit: one full check-suite run (`dotnet run --project src/Charm.Harness`) to confirm the config-relative shooting checks stay green — the season page proves the calibration, the suite proves nothing structural broke.

**Next:** the three-point-volume / generation thread (raise the population's three inclination via the tendency oracle) now also owns the aggregate-FG%-HIGH consequence — the two move together. Player-generation Pass 2 (tweener-post, weakest-leg development) and the larger FTA-LOW / assists-HIGH misses remain the other open candidates; target is Emmett's ruling. ## Session 38 — Fast-break shot diet: the frozen 5%-transition-three break becomes a modern base diet that bends to whoever runs it (2026-07-06)

**Scope:** Engine build (Roll G's fast-break branch + read-only accounting counters threaded through the possession record) plus a season-page fast-break shot-diet line, a new harness Phase 58, a rewrite of the Phase 16 (7) sub-check, and docs. Until now every fast break produced the **same** flat rim-heavy shot menu (Rim 0.70 / … / Three 0.05) regardless of who was running it. That frozen 5%-of-transition-attempts-are-threes diet was the last big runtime drag on the realized three-point rate — the Session 34/35 tendency retune set a good neutral-matchup half-court baseline, but transition possessions (~39% of all possessions) kept dumping their threes to 5%, pulling the league 3PA rate down toward the low-30s when the generated players want ~39%. This session makes the break **bend to the shooter**: the break dictates a modern base diet, and that base is pulled zone-by-zone toward the featured runner's own tendencies, with the coach's pace preference tilting the three share.

**The basketball (Emmett's ruling).** The break sets a modern base — Rim 0.57 / Short 0.08 / Mid 0.03 / Long 0.02 / **Three 0.30** — the long two nearly gone, a real transition three share instead of a token. That base then bends to identity: a stretch big trailing the break gets his threes, a rim-runner keeps running, a shooter fills the corner — the same "the shooter's own profile decides his diet" principle the half-court derivation already runs, now applied to the break. **PaceBias** (the coach's tempo dial) tilts the three share both ways: run-and-gun raises transition threes, grind-it-out trims them. Deliberately **out of scope this session** (parked): a coach shot-selection philosophy on the break, an era three-multiplier, and teammate-spacing/gravity bends — the break reads only the shooter's raw tendencies and tempo, nothing else.

**Oracle-first, and the fixture is the locked spec.** A Python oracle (`tools/fastbreak_diet_oracle.py`, LOCKED SPEC v1) and its 14-vector golden fixture (`tools/fastbreak_golden.json`, zone order Rim/Short/Mid/Long/Three, each vector at pace 5 and pace 8) were committed before any C#. The archetype table the oracle prints — pure spot-up shooter, 3&D wing, slasher, floor general, mid-range maestro, post bruiser, rim runner, **stretch big**, pick-&-pop big, weak shooters, open-only guard, **true non-shooter big** — is where Emmett ratified the math in plain basketball language (transition three share, today's 5% vs proposed, per archetype). The C# mirrors it constant-for-constant; **if the two ever disagree, the oracle wins.**

**The mechanism.** `RollGGenerator.DeriveFastBreakPie` (public static, so the harness reproduces every fixture vector directly — the same shape as the displacement port) is the locked-spec math: per zone, read the neutral tendency as a share of 100 (a fixed constant, **not** the tendency sum), form the identity ratio `(share / mean) ^ Beta` (Beta 0.70) clamped to `[0.15, 2.2]`, multiply the base diet; then tilt the three share by `1 + PaceTilt·(PaceBias − 5)` (PaceTilt 0.035); one renormalization yields the pie. **No additive floor** — a non-shooter's tiny three ratio keeps his break a rim-run. The `FastBreakMean{Zone}` denominators (Rim 0.335 / Short 0.155 / Mid 0.098 / Long 0.058 / Three 0.355) are pinned to the tendency oracle's population diagnostic, not free knobs. In `RollGGenerator.Generate` the shooter is now fetched **before** the fast-break branch, and the branch is **three-way**: present shooter → the bent, PaceBias-tilted pie; null shooter → the flat configured base (`BuildFlatFastBreakPie`) — explicitly **not** `BuildStubPie`, which is the 35/36 half-court diet and would silently turn a missing-shooter break into a half-court-looking possession. The break reads the shooter's **raw** stored tendencies, never `CoachingPull.Apply` — coach shot-selection philosophy is a future layer; only PaceBias tilts the break now.

**The accounting (read-only page instrumentation).** The resolver counts fast-break FGA / 3PA / 3PM — an ordinary Roll-G-selected FGA whose stamped state carries `FastBreak = true`, **excluding Roll K putbacks**. A transition possession's putback carries `FastBreak` forward (only `ResetOffense` clears it) but was rim-forced by Roll K / resolved on Roll H's putback pie — it never touched the fast-break diet, so counting it would inflate fast-break FGA with rim-forced shots and drag the reported three-rate below its true value (the `!c.Putback` guard). The counters nest so `0 ≤ fbThreePm ≤ fbThreePa ≤ fbFga ≤ Fga` on every possession, thread `RoutingOutcome → PossessionRecord`, and surface as a season-page line (the direct read of the realized transition three share). The observation run asserts the subset chain at batch scale.

**Two harness bugs, both caught on Emmett's first run, both test-only.** The engine compiled and ran clean on the first delivery — Phases 54–57 green, the full 1,000-game observation and 4,000-game stress runs completed with every conservation identity intact — but **Phase 58 failed twice, and both failures were in my test scaffolding, not the basketball code.** (1) **Golden parity tolerance too tight.** The oracle writes the fixture with `round(x, 10)` (10 decimals), so the stored values differ from full-precision output by up to ~5e-11. My check reused the displacement check's *relative* 1e-9 tolerance, which at these small values (~0.027) is ~2.7e-11 — tighter than the fixture's own rounding, so 34 values failed by ~4e-11 of pure rounding. My sandbox pre-check had used an *absolute* 1e-9 threshold and passed, which is exactly why I missed it. Fix: an absolute floor of 1e-8 (still 1e5× tighter than any real constant/formula bug, which shift values ≥1e-5). (2) **Empty-roster accounting fixture threw.** I routed the seeded fixtures through an empty `GameState`, reasoning the accounting reads only state fields — but a **made** shot credits an assist, and `AssistPicker` requires eligible teammates, so it threw "no eligible non-shooter offensive players." Fix: a populated game (the counters read state, so which players are present doesn't change the assertions). Both fixes touched only `Program.Checks.FastBreakDiet.cs`; the engine was never changed between the red run and the green run (the observation/stress numbers were byte-identical across both, confirming it).

**Phase 58 and the Phase 16 (7) rewrite.** Phase 58: (1) golden parity — `DeriveFastBreakPie` reproduces all 14 vectors × 2 paces under **both** the built-in defaults **and** the loaded config, with a config-vs-default drift guard so a divergence fails loudly; (2) ShotSelectionBias isolation — swinging it 1↔10 at fixed pace 5 leaves the break diet identical (proves shot-selection philosophy does not leak into the break); (3) resolver accounting — a fast-break three increments all three counters, a half-court three touches none, and a putback carrying `FastBreak` increments `Fga` but not `FastBreakFga` (the putback exclusion, driven by routing Roll K's `PutBack` output verbatim). Phase 16 (7), which used to assert every shooter gets the *identical flat* pie, was rewritten to the bent truth: rim-runner vs pure-shooter break diets differ and the pure shooter takes more transition threes (0.62 vs 0.03); both sum to 1; PaceBias moves the pure-shooter three share both ways (pace 2 < pace 5 < pace 8); non-FastBreak diets still differ (tendencies active); and the null-shooter fallback equals the flat configured base exactly, pace-invariant, and is **not** the half-court stub.

**Validation — reasoned + oracle-traced, then harness-confirmed on Emmett's machine (after the two test fixes).** The full suite ran **ALL CHECKS PASSED**. The calibration payoff is **read, not asserted, and not visible in this run**: the season calibration page (347 schools) owns the new fast-break shot-diet line and the league 3PA rate, and it is a separate invocation from the checks + frozen-corpus + stress run. The frozen-corpus 3PA rate in the observation output (~27%) is one fixed, non-representative pair of rosters and must not be read as the league figure. Whether the transition-three fix actually lifts the realized league three-point rate toward the ~39% target is the read to take on the season page next — a tuning conversation, not a gate.

## Session 37 — Court-aware turnover clock: turnovers draw a short, court-dependent band instead of the shared possession clock (2026-07-04)

**Scope:** Engine build (the Governor's elapsed draw + a new terminal marker) plus the season page's turnover-length-by-court split, a new harness Phase 57, and docs. Until now every possession — a made basket, a missed jumper, a backcourt strip — drew its elapsed time from the *same* shared truncated-normal clock (~18s at Center 17). This session gives **turnovers their own, shorter, court-dependent clock**: a backcourt turnover resolves before the 10-second mark (~5s band), a worked-out frontcourt turnover runs on the shot clock (~14.5s band), and neither eats the full possession a shot attempt does. This is the runtime piece that closes the league's pace gap — the league ran ~65.5 possessions/team because turnovers were spending a shooter's worth of clock; real basketball turns it over faster than it shoots.

**The basketball (Emmett's ruling).** Two bands, by court, bounded by the laws that govern each: a backcourt turnover *must* resolve before ~10s (else the 10-second-backcourt violation would have fired instead), a single frontcourt shot-clock segment *cannot* reach 30 without becoming a shot-clock violation. Offensive fouls travel with the turnover family — a charge is a turnover in the box score and is timed by court like any other. The three fixed-time violations (shot-clock 30 / ten-second 10 / five-second inbound 0) keep their invariant times; they are not drawn.

**Oracle-first, and the oracle overturned the prompt's framing.** A Python oracle (`tools/turnover_clock_oracle_s37.py`) reproduced `ClockDraw.Sample` exactly, validated its model against the *current* page (turnovers-draw-shared → predicts pace 65.5, the page reads 65.5), then predicted the change. The prompt assumed the tempo **Center** would shift *down* to drag pace from 65.5 to 69. The oracle showed that is not where the gap lives: the moment turnovers stop drawing ~18s and start drawing ~5s/~15s, pace rises to ~69.7 on its own, and the Center that lands exactly 69 is ~17.2 — essentially unchanged, if anything a hair *up*. Ruling (Emmett): **Center stays 17.0.** The dominant uncertainty was the backcourt/frontcourt split, invisible until the page prints it; moving Center to chase a point estimate ahead of that read would have been false precision. The bands are the dial.

**The mechanism.** A new `PossessionTimeProfile` marker (`BackcourtTurnover` / `FrontcourtTurnover`) rides on the `Terminal`, stamped by the emitting arm off the possession's court-state — the full A2 census is exactly three emitter families: Roll C's 12 drawn arms, Roll K's 3 turnover terminals, and the resolver's `ResolveOffensiveFoul`. The Governor's elapsed fork gained one branch, in strict precedence: invariant `ElapsedSeconds` first (the three violations, unchanged), then a profile-stamped `DrawTurnoverSeconds` band, then the shared `DrawPossessionSeconds` (everything else). Exactly one RNG-consuming draw per possession on every path, so a non-turnover possession's stream and draw are byte-for-byte what they were before (the neutrality anchor). `CoachAdjustedCenter` was extracted verbatim from `DrawPossessionSeconds` so the multi-period frontcourt band could reuse the identical center — no numeric change to the shared draw. The record carries `TimeProfile`, the pre-clamp `TurnoverRawElapsed`, and `ShotClockPeriods` so the page can split by court and report raw band means (the oracle's prediction target) beside the clamped applied mean.

**A2 was wrong, and the fail-loud guard caught it — the load-bearing correction of the session.** The build's stated load-bearing assumption was that a backcourt turnover can never span multiple shot-clock periods (you cannot rebound in the backcourt). The first delivery encoded that as a throwing guard. Emmett's harness run threw it across ~35% of the Phase 24 seeds. The premise was right about *basketball* but wrong about the *engine*: the `Frontcourt` flag does not mean "the ball is physically across half" — it latches only on Roll A's halfcourt entry, and **transition (fast-break / steal) and ball-advanced possessions skip that entry entirely**, carrying `Frontcourt = false` through their shots, rebounds, and turnovers. So a fast break that misses, grabs its own offensive rebound (period → 2), and then loses the ball arrives as a "backcourt" turnover on a two-period possession — physically at the rim, flagged backcourt. The fix replaced the throw with `EffectiveTurnoverProfile(stamped, periods)`: any turnover on a possession that has offensive-rebounded (`ShotClockPeriods > 1`) is timed as **frontcourt** regardless of the stale flag, and flows into the multi-period frontcourt draw already built (prior periods as a normal possession + a final band segment). The guard's premise was simply false; the reclassification is basketball-forced. This is exactly the failure the adversarial preamble names — an architecturally plausible absolute that a green subset check would not have caught; the loud throw did.

**Phase 57 — the target-free structural block (registered after Phase 56).** (1) **Profile stamping in isolation** — each of Roll C's 12 drawn arms driven in both courts stamps court-correct and carries no invariant time; the 3 violation arms stamp no profile and keep 30/0/10; Roll K's 3 terminals stamp frontcourt. (2) **The reclassification rule** — `EffectiveTurnoverProfile` promotes backcourt+multi-period to frontcourt, leaves backcourt+single and frontcourt+any alone (the throwing guard it replaced is gone). (3) **Season fixture** — the strong cross-emitter **no-leak** guard (any drawn, non-fixed-time turnover reaching the Governor without a profile is counted; zero is the only pass — this is what proves the resolver's offensive-foul emitter stamps, without isolating it); both courts populated; every backcourt raw draw in `[1,10)` and every single-period frontcourt raw draw in `[6,30)` (multi-period excluded — its total can legitimately exceed 30); A6 per-game conservation still exact with the new bands.

**Validation — reasoned + oracle-traced, then harness-confirmed on Emmett's machine (after the one fix).** The full suite ran **ALL CHECKS PASSED**: Phase 57 green, Phase 24/25 clean (no throws), the season reconciliation and A6 identities intact. Page movement, read not tuned: backcourt raw mean **5.08s** (oracle 5.08), frontcourt raw mean **17.93s** — higher than the oracle's single-period ~15.2 because ~20% of frontcourt turnovers (`multiPeriod n=736`) are post-offensive-rebound possessions carrying a long two-period total; 80% single-period at ~15 blended with 20% at ~28 is ~17.9, arithmetic that checks out. The consequence: turnovers eat slightly more clock than the naive oracle assumed, so pace lands a hair under 69.7 — still on target.

**One diagnostic caught at build time, ruled and fixed.** The observation run (a **100%-press** stress corpus) tripped its runaway-game tripwire once in 1000 games — seed 930 reached 203 possessions. Not a correctness failure: the tripwire (`> 200`) was calibrated to the old clock world where a turnover ate ~18s and 200 possessions was impossible. With ~5s backcourt turnovers under relentless press, a 101-possession-a-side game is a legal (9-sigma) tail; the mean there is 70.4/team, on target. Ruling (Emmett): widen the tripwire to `> 260` — still catches a true infinite loop (which prints thousands), no longer flags a legal max-press outlier. Harness-only, one line.

**Deferrals recorded this session (logged, not built):** **turnover-band calibration** — the band centers/spreads shipped as placeholders, tuned off the page's new split in the calibration pass; and the flagged open question that **single-period transition / ball-advanced turnovers currently draw the short backcourt band** — right for a bring-up strip, arguably too short for an already-across possession — to be decided once the split's size and mean are on the page, not this session.

**What shipped (engine):** `Core/RollResult.cs` — EDIT (`PossessionTimeProfile` enum + the `Terminal.TimeProfile` init-property). `Rolls/RollC.cs` — EDIT (the 12 drawn arms stamp court-correct; the 3 violations untouched). `Rolls/RollK.cs` — EDIT (the 3 turnover terminals stamp frontcourt). `Core/Resolver.cs` — EDIT (the `ResolveOffensiveFoul` emitter stamps court-aware). `Config/RollClockConfig.cs` — EDIT (the six band knobs + Load validation). `Core/Governor.cs` — EDIT (the profile-aware fork; `DrawTurnoverSeconds`; `CoachAdjustedCenter` extracted verbatim; `EffectiveTurnoverProfile`; the three new `PossessionRecord` fields threaded through the one ctor site). **(harness):** `Program.Checks.TurnoverClock.cs` — NEW (Phase 57). `Program.cs` — EDIT (registration). `Program.Season.Calibration.cs` — EDIT (the court split, filtered by the official classifier then grouped by profile; raw/applied means; the leak + range observations). `Program.Observation.cs` — EDIT (runaway tripwire 200 → 260). `config.json` — EDIT (the six band knobs). `tools/turnover_clock_oracle_s37.py` — NEW. Docs after the green run: this entry; `docs/design.md` clock section edited in place (the court-aware bands, the stamp-vs-effective distinction, the deferred seam marked built); `docs/status.md` (court-aware clock → Built; two S37 rulings → Closed; the band-calibration follow-on → Open).

**Next:** the **season calibration pass** at seed 20260703 is the front-runner — it now inherits pace ~69, the turnover-length-by-court split, and all three generation-time shot-diet effects, and it owns the band-value tuning plus the single-period transition-band question above. ## Session 36 — Roll G matchup displacement: the Route B residualized bend + the usage-gated asymmetric ladder (2026-07-04)

**Scope:** Engine build (the first engine *behavioral* change since the tendency-derivation sessions) plus the harness Phase 56 block, a read-only observation readout, and docs. This session adds the **third and last generation-time shot-diet effect** in Roll G: **matchup displacement**, driven by how much better or worse the whole defending lineup is than the featured shooter — the overall *level*, not the *shape*. Phase 9 already owned shape (uneven defense → tilt toward the soft zone) and Phase 17 owned volume (heavy usage → widen the diet); displacement is the level effect. It is the runtime half of closing the three-point-rate gap the Session 34/35 tendency retune left open — that pass set the neutral-matchup baseline; this pass is the matchup bend. The executable spec is a committed locked oracle (`tools/displacement_oracle.py`, LOCKED SPEC v1, 28 structural checks, 10-vector golden fixture); the C# mirrors it constant-for-constant and stage-for-stage, and **if the two ever disagree, the oracle wins**.

**The basketball (all rulings Emmett's, recorded in `docs/rollg-displacement-brief.md`).** A defending lineup clearly superior to a featured shooter forces his diet **outward** — away from the rim, toward low-efficiency bailout threes. An inferior lineup **invites** him inward, and he accepts only to the degree his own inside skills allow. Everything is relative to the player himself. Efficiency needs nothing new: the make curve at Roll H already prices a bad shot; displacement only moves *where* the shots come from. Usage is the volume knob — zero displacement at or below an equal share, smooth above it.

**Route B — the bend is now exact shape, level carved out.** Phase 9's "uniform gaps cancel" behavior used to be an *accident* of the convex gap function: a uniform level difference produced *nearly* equal multipliers that *nearly* cancelled. Session 36 made it **exact** by subtracting the diet-weighted skill level from every zone gap before the bend (`residual[z] = gap[z] − skillLevel`). A uniform defensive upgrade now moves the shape by *exactly* zero. The level that was carved out feeds displacement instead. This was ruled by measurement (Emmett, 2026-07-04): holding the split at "accidental residual" left a small designed-basketball effect resting on a numerical accident; Route B makes the two effects — shape (bend) and level (displacement) — cleanly separable.

**The derivation, stage by stage (mirrored from the oracle).** (1) **Level** = `skillLevel` (diet-weighted sum of per-zone gaps — an edge in the zones he actually shoots counts more) + `physicalLevel` (a *gentle* athleticism term: shooter composite vs the defending lineup's **mean** athleticism — all five, not the top three — through the same `GapFn` at a deliberately low steepness, 3.0 vs the make door's 11.5). The physical term is gentle by design; the make curve owns the harsh physical punishment. The physical term feeds the **level only** — residuals are computed against the skill level alone, so the bend's zone-shape read stays exactly the skill read it always was. (2) **Magnitude** = `DisplacementMaxMagnitude · tanh(level / DisplacementLevelReference) · min(1, DisplacementUsageScale · usagePressure)` — bounded, smooth, usage-gated (null and zero usage both mean magnitude zero). (3) **The asymmetric gated ladder** (Rim +2 / Short +1 / Mid 0 / Long −1 / Three −2, scaled by magnitude): when magnitude > 0 the two inward rungs are **gated by the shooter's own inside skills** — Rim by Finishing, Short by Close — so an advantaged non-finisher declines the rim invitation; when magnitude ≤ 0 the outward push is **unconditional**. Force needs no permission; invitation needs the skill to accept. (4) **Composition**: the bend delta and the displacement delta are both computed from the *same* normalized baseline, added, clamped at zero, renormalized **once**. The Phase 17 usage widening stays downstream, applied last, untouched.

**Five load-bearing assumptions, all attacked at draft time and re-confirmed against the fresh pull before any edit.** (1) **The oracle's engine constants equal the live engine's** — every value (skill/physical steepness and exponent, reference scale, location blend and shift, the zone-blend table) matched in both the defaults and `config.json`; golden parity with config-loaded constants is the tripwire, and a drifted constant fails it loudly. (2) **Roll G's pipeline order** is FastBreak → no-shooter stub → zero-defender (pure tendency + widening) → bend → widening; displacement lands inside the bend block, which the three bypass paths never reach, so those paths needed **zero new gates** — asserted by reading, not by adding code. (3) **Two different baseline reads coexist deliberately** — the bend + displacement consume the **coached** baseline (the diet the player will actually try to shoot), while the diet shift's intrinsic-capacity read consumes the **raw authored** tendencies (flexibility is intrinsic; a coach bends *where* he shoots, not *how adaptable* he is). With the default identity-ish coach the two are near-equal, so the anti-double-count rule matters only for a biased coach; the port kept them distinct. (4) **Route B + displacement leaves every existing harness check passing** — every Phase 9 (a)–(h) and Phase 17 (a)–(g) scenario was re-run numerically through both pipelines at draft time and the predictions held on the machine exactly (d2 diff 3.2pp, d3 diff 0.0000, P17(b) residual 0.0600, b 23.38%, e2 15.70%, e3 18.58%). (5) **The golden fixture was not yet committed** — the build ran the committed oracle once and committed its emission byte-for-byte; the parity check validates the fixture contract (zone order, full five-defender lineups, complete traces) before trusting a single number.

**One build-time call, flagged at the check-in gate and taken with Emmett's go-ahead.** The golden fixture's level-matched vector (5b) solves a defender's `PostDefense` to a fractional value **by construction** — that exactness is the point of the fixture. But `Player` attributes are `int`, so the parity check cannot build that defender as a real `Player`. Resolution: a small numbers-only `DisplacementDefender` record (the four defender reads as doubles) that both the live game and the parity check feed into the same aggregation math; live players convert into it losslessly via `FromPlayer`. This reshaped §3a into two tiny extractions inside `Matchup` (`DefenseRatingRaw`, `BlendTopThree`) so the top-3 zone blend and the five-man athleticism mean have one source and two feeders — behavior byte-identical, no basketball change. The locked oracle and fixture were untouched.

**One build error caught by Emmett's harness run, fixed and re-shipped.** The first delivery added the nine displacement-bucket observation counters to `RoutingOutcome` (the resolver's return) but missed that the harness reads them off a **second, parallel record** — `PossessionRecord`, populated at the Governor seam — which never received them. The fix threads the nine counters through all three layers of that copy (the record's field list, the copy-out from the outcome, and the one positional constructor call), positioned between `ThreePm` and `ShotResolutions` in both the record and the call so the positional args stay aligned. This is precisely the stale-reference bug class the CONVENTIONS §2 sweep exists to catch; the miss was a reminder that the counter path spans an extra record hop the first sweep didn't follow.

**Phase 56 — the golden parity harness block (registered after Phase 55).** Four sub-checks: (1) **stage-wise golden parity** — the fixture contract is validated loudly (zone order; every vector carries the full five-defender lineup — a single-defender fixture could not catch a wrong aggregation; the complete ten-field trace), then every vector runs through `DeriveDisplacement` with **config-loaded** constants, every stage compared at cross-language tolerance; (2) **no-displacement equivalence at equal level** — a shooter whose diet-weighted skill level is exactly 0 and whose athleticism equals the lineup mean reproduces the old pipeline `renorm(base · mult(rawGap))` within 1e-12, with usage deliberately > 0 to prove the equivalence is *level*-driven, not usage-driven; (3) **ablation** — `DisplacementMaxMagnitude = 0` equals the pure shape bend, and the note that 0 does *not* undo Route B; (4) **direction + gate spot-checks** — overmatched → Three up / Rim down, advantaged finisher → Rim up, advantaged non-finisher (Finishing below the gate) → Rim ladder exactly 0, zero usage → magnitude exactly 0.

**Validation — reasoned + Monte-Carlo-traced, then harness-confirmed on Emmett's machine.** Sandbox pre-check: a Python mirror transcribed from the *written C#* (not the oracle) reproduced all 10 golden vectors at every stage with zero mismatches, and pre-ran Phase 56 sub-checks (2)–(4) green before any harness existed. Braces balanced on every touched file; stale-reference sweep on `bentNorm`/`LocationMultiplier`/the retired raw-gap path came back clean; the sole `PossessionRecord` construction site confirmed. On Emmett's machine, after the one-file fix: the full suite ran **ALL CHECKS PASSED** — Phase 56 green (all four sub-checks, exact predicted numbers: 4a level −9.8 / Three 45.0%→51.7%, 4b level +27.9 / Rim 30.0%→37.6%, 4c rim ladder 0.000, 4d magnitude 0.000), Phases 9 and 17 unchanged, the 100k and season reconciliation identities intact, and the observation run clean (zero parks, no throws).

**The page movement (read, tuned nothing).** At the frozen sentinel corpus the displacement readout confirmed the mechanism qualitatively: the **overmatched** bin (level < −5) ran a *higher* 3PA-rate (28.3%) and *lower* 3P% (29.3%) than the **near-even** bin (25.8% / 36.3%) — the low-efficiency bailout-three signature the whole effect was built to produce. The **advantaged** bin (level > +5) came back **empty**, which is a property of the corpus, not the mechanism: the sentinel pits two evenly-matched populated rosters, so almost every featured shooter sits at-or-below his defenders and the level distribution never reaches "meaningfully advantaged." The advantaged direction is proven instead by Phase 56 (4b) and the stress-test **EliteVsWeak** bucket (Team A's rim share climbs to 39% while the weak side is pushed out to 29% threes). League 3PA-rate barely moved (0.237, near the pre-session baseline) — expected per the brief's honest note: Route B reshapes uneven matchups but does not manufacture threes league-wide, and a near-even corpus has little to reshape. Nothing was tuned to hit a number; the new constants are calibration placeholders, pinned only by golden parity at the approved state.

**Deferrals recorded this session (logged only, not built):** the **`Outside == 0` heave** (the math pass excluded it — stays parked); **personality/timidity on the usage dial, strategy layers, and teammate spacing / lineup-context** (a future Roll G lineup-context bend for teammate spacing as a selection effect); **any magnitude tuning** — the displacement constants are calibration placeholders in the page-only sense (no macro-target asserted anywhere), pinned by golden parity at the approved calibration state; later tuning follows the oracle-first flow (approve a new oracle calibration → regenerate the fixture → sync the C# defaults and config → parity stays green), never config-only. The empty **advantaged observation bin** is a corpus property to revisit when a varied-population season page exists, not a plumbing gap.

**What shipped (engine):** `Core/Displacement.cs` — NEW (`DisplacementDefender`, `DisplacementTrace`). `Core/Matchup.cs` — EDIT (the `DeriveDisplacement` derivation; the `DefenseRatingRaw` / `BlendTopThree` / `LocationMultiplierFromGap` extractions, existing signatures preserved and delegating). `Config/MatchupConfig.cs` — EDIT (the displacement block + Load validation). `Generators/RollGGenerator.cs` — EDIT (the bend block rewired to the derivation; `ApplyDietShift` untouched; class doc updated to the current pipeline). `Generators/IRollGGenerationProvider.cs` — EDIT (`RollGGeneration` gains the optional `DisplacementLevel`). `Rolls/RollG.cs` — EDIT (stamps `ShotDisplacementLevel` via one optional param). `Rolls/RollK.cs` — EDIT (clears it in `ResetOffense`). `Core/PossessionState.cs` — EDIT (the new nullable fact). `Core/Resolver.cs` — EDIT (passes the level through; the nine bucket counters at the Roll H chokepoint). `Core/RoutingOutcome.cs` + `Core/Governor.cs` — EDIT (the nine counters carried through to `PossessionRecord` — the build-error fix). **(harness):** `Program.Checks.Displacement.cs` — NEW (Phase 56). `Program.cs` — EDIT (registration). `Program.Observation.cs` — EDIT (the read-only displacement-context readout). `config.json` — EDIT (the displacement block mirrored). `Charm.Harness.csproj` — EDIT (the fixture copied beside the binary, tendency precedent). `tools/displacement_golden.json` — NEW (the oracle's emission, byte-for-byte).
