## Session 35 — Tendency derivation synced to oracle v2: the modern-era retune (2026-07-04)

**Scope:** Harness-only runtime change plus four documentation corrections — no engine behavioral code changed. This session synchronizes the C# shot-tendency derivation (the skill-derived generator that replaced the nine-row role table in Session 34) to the committed **oracle v2** (`tools/tendency_oracle.py`, header LOCKED SPEC ORACLE v2), and upgrades the golden-parity check from final-integers-only to a **stage-wise pipeline contract**. The problem Session 34 left open: the league's three-point rate read ~0.19–0.21 against a ~0.39 real target — the shot diet was three-starved. The v1 derivation was faithful to its oracle but the *oracle* modeled three FREQUENCY as strongly rating-gated (a below-average shooter barely fired), which suppressed volume across the whole perimeter population. Oracle v2 rebuilds the three signal and adds an explicit era stage; this session ports it constant-for-constant and stage-for-stage. Only `Program.Gen.cs`'s derivation section changed; both stamp call sites, the fixture copy item, and the fixture-contract shape were re-verified on the fresh pull and left untouched.

**The four v2 rulings, embraced (Emmett, recorded in the oracle header).** (1) **Rating drives efficiency and usage, NOT frequency, for perimeter players.** On the 0–99 scale 50 is league-average conversion, so a 25-rated guard is an *open-only* shooter, not a non-shooter — shooting is pervasive across college perimeter players (a guard who truly can't shoot has to be elite elsewhere or he has no scholarship, down to D3). So a perimeter player's three FREQUENCY is broad and only weakly rating-dependent; the rating's real punishment lands at the make curve (contested) and the usage layer (volume), not the diet. (2) **Nonzero rating = capable.** Any player with `Outside > 0` now carries a small universal three floor (~4%): a rating-3 big fires his occasional wide-open one at ~30%. The old "paint big takes exactly zero threes" rule is overturned. (3) **The era profile** — one explicit post-peakedness stage of five weight-space multipliers (Rim 1.00 / Short 0.66 / Mid 0.50 / Long 0.70 / Three 2.10) encoding the modern shot-selection *culture* (threes up, mid-range way down, floaters/long-twos trimmed, rim untouched), cleanly separated from individual *capability*. A 1995-mode league is these five numbers and nothing else. (4) **The paradox, embraced:** a poor shooter with no other tools (no rim game, no athletic edge) correctly skews three-HEAVY — it is all he is capable of; his level fit (D1 washout, serviceable D2) is the population/divvy's job, not the derivation's.

**The three signal is now a two-path blend, the floor is universal.** The old single gated path (`Outside × gate(Outside, 34, 56)`) is replaced by `p·compressed + (1−p)·gated`, where `p` is **perimeter-ness** (small body OR a real handle, 0..1). The perimeter path is COMPRESSED — `(28 + 0.55·Outside) × gate(Outside, 2, 18)` — broad frequency that only the near-zero rating fades out of; the interior path stays stretch-gated — `Outside × gate(Outside, 32, 50)` — so a big still earns arc volume only through a real stretch rating. The opportunity floor's three term became `0.040·(Outside>0 ? 1 : 0) + 0.020·perim`: everyone capable gets the universal floor, perimeter players a touch more. The `perimeter_ness` expression, previously inline in the floor, was **hoisted to one shared helper** (`TendPerimeterNess`) since the three signal now reads the same value — one definition, two readers, exactly as the oracle has it. Rim / Short / Mid / Long signals are unchanged.

**The era stage is the new sixth pipeline stage.** The pipeline was raw signals → peakedness pow → margin bleed → opportunity floor → integerize (five stages). v2 inserts, immediately after the `Math.Pow(signal, gamma)` peakedness transform and before the bleed, an element-wise multiply by the five-number era profile. Capability signals stay pure; the era is the one place shot-selection culture lives.

**Two oracle structural checks were overturned by rulings 1 and 2; the port inherits the new truth.** The oracle's own gate rewrote two checks when v2 was authored, and this session's port reproduces both. (a) *Rim runner's threes:* the v1 check asserted `Three == 0` for the lob/putback big; ruling 2 makes that false — the check now asserts `2 ≤ Three ≤ 6` (rare but real, the occasional wide-open one). The literal-zero truth now lives only on the **true** non-shooter (`Outside == 3` single digits), which still tilts hard to rim. (b) *The "weak-shooting spot-up" archetype was mislabeled:* `Outside 40` on this scale is a *below-average* shooter, not a non-shooter — a fringe guard with no rim game is correctly a corner spot-up guy (three-dominant on very few attempts, with usage owning the low volume). The check now asserts he tilts three, not away from it. The two new v2 probe archetypes — the open-only guard (`Outside 25`, skews three: the paradox) and the true non-shooter big (`Outside 3`, tilts rim) — are the archetypes that pin these two truths apart.

**Golden parity is now stage-wise, not just final integers.** The v1 check proved only that the five final integers matched — but two different implementations can round to the same five ints from different intermediate math, so a subtle port bug in one stage could hide behind a correct final diet. `tools/tendency_golden.json` now carries, per vector, a `trace` with all five per-stage fields (`rawSignals`, `gamma`, `postEraWeights`, `postBleedWeights`, `postFloorWeights`) alongside `expected`. The rewritten `RunTendencyGoldenParity` keeps the v1 fixture contract (zone order, the 13 inputs, valid diet shape) and **adds**: it rejects any vector lacking a full trace, then runs each C# stage against the oracle's trace — intermediate doubles compared at cross-language tolerance `|a−b| ≤ max(1e-9·max(|a|,|b|), 1e-12)` (Python `**` and `Math.Pow` may differ by ULPs), and the five final integers compared **exactly**. A mismatch names the vector, the stage, the index, and both values. The success line now reads `19 vectors, all stages within tolerance, all diets exact`.

**Five load-bearing assumptions, all re-confirmed against the fresh pull before any edit.** (1) **The 13 derivation inputs are unchanged in v2** — the new perimeter-ness reads Height and BallHandling, both already on the input list; a fresh oracle read showed no new input key (the fixture contract validator and both stamp sites depend on that list). (2) **Both stamp sites are already live and unchanged** — grep confirmed `DeriveAndStampTendencies` at Program.Gen.cs and Program.Divvy.cs and exactly the two `GenMapToPlayer(` pipeline call sites; this session does not touch stamping, and a green Phase 54 re-proves the pool path exactly as in Session 34. (3) **The C# stages decompose 1:1 with the trace fields** — the only structural insertion is the era multiplication between the pow and the bleed. (4) **The trace fixture internally reconciles** — every vector's `postFloorWeights`, re-run through the oracle's integerizer, equals its `expected` (19/19), *and* a full re-derive from raw ratings matched every trace field at tolerance; so the C# check may treat a trace mismatch as a port bug, never a fixture bug, once the contract validation passes. (5) **Cross-language float parity holds at tolerance, not equality** — intermediates within relative 1e-9, the five final integers exact.

**Outside review adjudication (ChatGPT, per CONVENTIONS §6c).** Three findings, all folded or filed. **Folded:** the trace fixture itself — the reviewer's point that final-integers-only parity can pass while an intermediate stage is wrong is exactly right, and it is why the fixture now carries per-stage traces and the check compares them. **Folded:** the `docs/tendencies.md` clarifying paragraph — the reviewer flagged that a reader of the tendencies catalogue could think the whole "how often" side was now skill-derived; the added paragraph makes explicit that only the five-zone shot-*location* diet became derived, while the paired behavioral action leans remain a separate future layer, so the orthogonality principle stands. **Deferred (logged, not built):** the **open-only-guard context readout** — a realized-3PA/3P%-under-neutral-vs-strong-defense-vs-late-clock diagnostic the reviewer wanted, which needs Roll G context plumbing that does not exist yet; parked for the Roll G session.

**The heave-deferral correction.** Session 34's journal and the design/floor comments described a deferred Roll G "emergency heave" as covering *every* true non-shooter's ~0.2% career buzzer three, with the generation floor keeping a genuine non-shooter's three at exactly zero. Ruling 2 changes this: the universal capable floor now **absorbs almost all of it** — every player with any outside rating reads a nonzero three tendency. Only the literal `Outside == 0` player still reads a zero three, and that residual (a single-digit-percent-of-a-percent buzzer heave) is all that remains for Roll G at pie time, if ever. The floor comment and the design note were corrected to say so.

**Validation — reasoned + Monte-Carlo-traced, then harness-confirmed on Emmett's machine.** Sandbox pre-check: a Python mirror transcribed from the *written C#* (not the oracle) reproduced all 19 golden vectors at every stage and every final diet, within the same tolerance the check uses. Stale-reference sweep confirmed the two deleted constants (`TendThreeCredLo/Hi`, `TendFloorThreePerim`) appear nowhere; braces balanced; everything outside the derivation section byte-identical to the pulled source. On Emmett's machine: the full suite ran `ALL CHECKS PASSED` with **Phase 54 PASS** (the pool-path regression re-proof — stamping untouched). The `gen` run completed end to end, which is itself the parity proof: `RunTendencyGoldenParity` runs first in `RunGen` and throws uncaught on any mismatch, so a failure would abort before the header ever printed — the completed run is reachable only if every stage matched within tolerance and every diet matched exactly. The generated rosters show the retune live: three share ~33–36%, mid down to ~9.5%, long ~5%, where the v1 gen showed three ~21–26%.

**The season page movement (the whole point of the retune).** At seed 20260703 on `stock-d1.world.json`, the calibration page's **3PA rate rose from ~0.19 to ~0.32**, moving decisively toward the 0.39 target; **long share held at ~5%** and **mid and short both fell** (mid to ~10.5%), exactly the intended redistribution. The five per-zone FG% lines stayed OK — **3P% ~33% (target 34), combined FG% ~45.6% (target 44), rim ~61%** — the make curves were untouched, and 3P% barely drifted even as the SHOOTER MIX shifted (more attempts now come from ordinary shooters, which is the retune working, not a curve regression). The residual from ~0.32 to the 0.39 target belongs to Roll G's matchup displacement, as planned — this pass moved the generation-side neutral baseline; the runtime bend is the follow-on.

**Deferrals recorded this session (logged only, not built):** **Roll G matchup displacement** and any lineup/spacing bend (overmatched → low-efficiency bailout threes; undermatched → pulled to the rim) — this pass is the neutral-matchup baseline only, and the ~0.32→0.39 residual rides here. The **open-only-guard context readout** (realized 3PA/3P% under neutral vs. strong-defense vs. late-clock) — needs Roll G context plumbing; named by the outside review. The **Roll G heave residual** — now only the literal `Outside == 0` player (the universal floor absorbed the rest). The oracle's population-mean diet remains a **directional diagnostic only**, never a gate.

## Session 34 — Shot tendencies derive from the player's own skills (the role table retired) (2026-07-04)

**Scope:** Harness-only runtime change plus four documentation corrections — no engine behavioral code changed. The problem the redesign targets: the procedural generator authored each player's five shot tendencies (Rim / Short / Mid / Long / Three) from a **nine-row role table**, one fixed vector per role, identical for every player who drew that role. Two defects fell out of that: the vectors overweighted the long two for nearly every role (the league shot ~21% threes vs a ~39% real target, with an unrealistic long-two tail), and every player in a role shot the **same** diet no matter what skills he actually drew. This session replaces the table with a **deterministic derivation from the player's own final ratings**, ported constant-for-constant from a committed locked oracle. Population variety now comes entirely from the varied skills the generator already draws; identical final ratings yield an identical diet.

**Determinism ruling, locked at the check-in gate.** `DeriveTendencies` is a **pure function of the final rating map** — no player-style seed, no manufactured tendency noise. This reversed the design brief's original §4.2 ("same ratings must NOT mean same tendencies," which had proposed a per-player style draw). The reversal reasoning: the Klay-vs-Curry distinction the style draw wanted is already delivered by the skills themselves — two shooters with different creation/mid/outside numbers already derive different diets — and if two players' ratings are *truly* identical there is no basketball reason they should want different shots; inventing one would only reintroduce the pathology (a player acquiring a shot his skills don't support). The other half of that distinction — a skilled shooter who *takes* few shots — is **shot volume**, which is usage/hierarchy's job, a separate existing layer, not this function's. The build synchronized the brief's §4.2 (marked superseded, old reasoning preserved here in the journal) and both stale cross-references to it.

**The oracle is the spec.** `tools/tendency_oracle.py` (committed, header LOCKED SPEC 2026-07-04) alongside its emitted parity fixture `tools/tendency_golden.json` (17 named rating maps → exact expected diets) is authoritative. The C# port mirrors it stage-for-stage, constant-for-constant: four shaping stages (raw per-zone signals → peakedness gamma → margin bleed → opportunity floor) then integerization to five ints summing to 100, each ≤ 99, with fully deterministic tie-breaks (largest-remainder rounding and 99-cap redistribution both resolve in fixed zone order Rim → Short → Mid → Long → Three). If the C# and the oracle ever disagree, the oracle wins; future tuning happens in the oracle first. The stretch-post long-two gate keeps its clean input partition — **no shooting in the frontcourt-plausibility factor, all shooting in the catch-and-shoot credibility factor** — so a big earns his pop from being a big who can shoot, never from a role label.

**Five load-bearing assumptions, all re-confirmed against the fresh pull before any edit.** (1) The derivation must run **after all rating mutation** — the generator keeps sculpting ratings after the initial draw (lean tilt, position floors, leg-health lift, and the pool path's third-leg redraw all raise ratings that feed the derivation), so deriving earlier would stamp a diet from a half-finished player; none of those mutators touch tendency keys. (2) There are **two** generation call sites, not one — the roster path (Program.Gen.cs) and the divvy pool path (Program.Divvy.cs) — verified by grep on `GenMapToPlayer(`; both stamp. (3) The role-table copy in `GenRatings` was the **only** procedural tendency-authoring site — a repo-wide grep for `.Tendencies` found exactly one reader; the explicit-authoring sites (JSON rosters, stress fixtures, harness defaults) write named tendency fields directly and stay untouched. (4) Every one of the 13 derivation inputs exists in the rating map at both stamp points (a missing key throws loudly). (5) The rounded diet always passes `Player.Validate` (each 0–99, sum > 0), guaranteed by the integerizer and proven by the oracle's 4000-player sweep; `Player.Validate` already runs at both sites, so a bad diet fails loud.

**One build-time call, flagged at the gate and taken with Emmett's go-ahead.** The golden fixture has to be found at runtime. Rather than resolve it relative to the working directory (which would silently depend on where the command is launched from), it is **copied beside the binary** the same way the world csvs already are — the Phase 53 convention — which meant one copy-instruction line in the harness project file. That project-file touch was outside the prompt's stated scope wall; Emmett approved it at the check-in gate as the safer option (can't break based on launch directory).

**The change.** The `int[] Tendencies` field is removed from the `GenRoleDef` record and from all nine role entries (roles keep position + skill emphasis); the copy block inside `GenRatings` is gone (it no longer writes tendency keys). A pure `DeriveTendencies` helper (the oracle port) and a thin `DeriveAndStampTendencies` wrapper were added; the wrapper is called at **both** pipeline tails, after the last mutator and before the player is built. A `RunTendencyGoldenParity` check loads the fixture once at the start of the `gen` command, validates the fixture **contract** first (zone order == Rim/Short/Mid/Long/Three, every vector carries all 13 inputs, every expected diet is length five, in [0,99], summing to 100 — so a stale or malformed fixture is rejected loudly rather than silently trusted), then requires every C# diet to equal the oracle diet element-for-element, throwing on any mismatch with the fixture name and both diets printed.

**Validation — reasoned + Monte-Carlo-traced, then harness-confirmed on Emmett's machine.** Sandbox pre-checks: a Python mirror transcribed from the *written C#* (not the oracle) reproduced all 17 golden diets exactly, and the two tie-trap vectors were probed for rounding-flip risk — their smallest remainder gaps (0.041 and 0.024) sit far from any flip, retiring the one risk flagged at check-in (Python/C# decimal parity on tie-heavy vectors). On Emmett's machine: the `gen` run printed **golden tendency parity: 17 vectors, all exact** as its first line, then generated valid rosters showing the intended within-role variety (one AthleticBig taking ~1.3 threes/game at a credible clip while another takes essentially zero — impossible under the old identical-within-role table). The team long-two share fell to ~5% from the table era's ~10%, the miscalibration the redesign targeted. The full suite ran `ALL CHECKS PASSED`, with **Phase 54 PASS** the specific proof of the pool path — the `gen` command exercises only the roster path, so Phase 54 (which builds the real national pool through the changed pipeline and validates every drafted player) is what proves the divvy stamp.

**Deferrals recorded this session (logged only, not built):** the **Roll G emergency-heave floor** — a tiny ~0.2% floor on every shot zone when Roll G builds the pie, so a true non-shooter can still heave at a buzzer; it lives below integer-tendency resolution and is its own separate add-in (the opportunity floor here keeps a genuine non-shooter's three at exactly zero on purpose). **Matchup displacement** (overmatched → low-efficiency bailout threes; undermatched → pulled to the rim) — Roll G's job; this pass is the neutral-matchup baseline only. The oracle's population-mean diet is a **directional diagnostic only**, never a gate — its sampler is intentionally approximate and does not reproduce the real roster pipeline; the generated population's mean diet is printed the same way.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Gen.cs` — EDIT (role table retired; the derivation helpers, the pure `DeriveTendencies`, the `DeriveAndStampTendencies` wrapper, the golden-parity check + its invocation; roster-path stamp). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Divvy.cs` — EDIT (pool-path stamp, one line). `src/Charm.Harness/Charm.Harness.csproj` — EDIT (the golden fixture copied beside the binary — the approved build-time call). `src/Charm.Engine/Core/Player.cs` — EDIT (comment-only: RimTendency and ThreeTendency docstrings rewritten so a design principle stated in source no longer contradicts the generator — generated tendencies derive from the final skill profile; JSON/stress fixtures may still author). `docs/shot-tendency-derivation-brief.md` — EDIT (§4.2 rewritten to the determinism ruling, marked superseded; two stale cross-references corrected). **No engine behavioral code changed.**

**Next:** the season calibration pass the earlier sessions set up — the shot diet was the named three-starved gap (3PA rate 0.21 vs 0.39 target), and this derivation is the generation-side half of closing it; the runtime half (Roll G's matchup bend and the heave floor) is the natural follow-on. The next-session prompt is its own audited pass.

## Session 33 — The ghost endings: OTHER named per-label, the Roll K turnover leak fixed, the whitelist guard (2026-07-03)

**Scope:** Harness-only — no engine source change, no config change, no dial tuning. The problem, measured by the Session 31/32 instrument: ~4% of all possessions (31,922 at seed 20260703) ended in the OTHER bucket, a silent catch-all the card could not see into. The draft-time audit had already proven the bucket hid a real defect: **Roll K's post-offensive-rebound turnovers end with labels the turnover classifier did not know, so every post-ORB turnover ever played had been counted as OTHER instead of a turnover** — 4,269 of them at this seed (2,587 dead-ball + 1,682 live-ball). This session itemized the bucket, returned the leaked turnovers home, and installed a whitelist guard so no future label can ever hide there again. Run as a measure-first two-phase session: Phase A (the breakdown, delivered alone) → STOP for rulings on the counts → Phase B (the fix). **The correction is aggregate-only** — the Roll K records carry no per-player turnover metadata, so team turnover totals rise but no individual credit changes, the same treatment team violations already receive.

**Four load-bearing assumptions, all confirmed against the fresh pull before any edit.** (1) Both Roll K labels are LIVE terminals that flip possession by the engine's own contract (`RollK.cs` ~101–112; `DeadBallTurnover` → dead-ball inbound to the defense, `LiveBallTurnover` → transition steal to the defense), and both were absent from the classifier's 15 labels — the grep across the whole engine found exactly one construction site each, no third. (2) The steal-side answer, checked explicitly per the adversarial preamble: the resolver's metadata dispatch handles three named label groups (team violations, interior, ball-handler) and the two Roll K labels match **none** of them, so they fall through with all three credit fields empty — no committer, no live-ball flag, **and no stealer credited to the thief.** There is therefore no asymmetry to heal: the play was invisible on both sides, and the fix corrects team totals only, symmetric as hoped. (One small divergence from the prompt recorded: the "stays null" comment it cited sits on the team-violation branch; the Roll K labels are skipped by omission, not by an explicit branch — same effect.) (3) The four jump-ball labels are dynamic with a two-value suffix domain — `JumpBall{Tip,Arrow}:{Home|Away}`, exactly four legal labels (`Resolver.cs` ~817–828), and the awarded team is set by the arrow/tip, so nothing may assume a jump-ball ending flips possession (a held ball can retain offense). (4) The full label universe is enumerable from source: the grep of every `Terminal(` construction site matched the prompt's list exactly — nothing hides outside the four jump-ball labels, the offensive loose-ball foul, the offense-OOB ending, the two Roll K labels, and `parked:*` (expected zero). The Phase A breakdown is the empirical twin of that grep, and the two agreed: the itemized block summed to exactly 31,922, no parks, no stranger labels.

**Phase A — the breakdown (delivered alone, classifies nothing).** `SeasonLeagueStats` gained a per-label tally fed only from records landing in the OTHER else-branch (label → count, elapsed sum), plus a jump-ball award split parsed from the record's `Offense` and the label suffix — offense retained vs defense awarded, tip vs arrow, each with its elapsed sum. The printer gained an itemized block beneath the existing split. This existed so the two mid-session rulings would be made with the counts on the page. **The measurement's payload:** OTHER at seed 20260703 broke down as OutOfBoundsOffOffense 9,609 (30.1%) / JumpBallArrow:Home 7,263 / JumpBallArrow:Away 7,162 / LooseBallFoulOnOffense 3,619 / DeadBallTurnover 2,587 (mean **29.9s**) / LiveBallTurnover 1,682 (mean **30.1s**) — the two Roll K labels running conspicuously long because they happen after a shot and an offensive rebound, late in the possession. The jump-ball split came back **entirely arrow, zero tip** (7,088 offense retained / 7,337 defense awarded): opening-tip contests award the ball to *start* a possession, so they never appear as a possession-ending record. Every held ball that ends a possession mid-game is an arrow read — the instrument caught the real behavior.

**Three rulings taken at the Phase A STOP.** **R1 — held balls the arrow awards to the defense do NOT join the turnover line.** Standard scorekeeping charges no turnover when a held ball is lost on the arrow, and the calibration target is built from published box scores, so counting the 7,337 defense-awarded held balls would push the sim's turnover line further from the number it is measured against (would have driven turnovers to ~14.0, TO% to ~21.5). Bookkeeping-only regardless: held-ball records retain no tied-up player's slot, so no individual credit is created either way. **R2 — OTHER stays one bucket** with the itemized line beneath it; promotion to named length buckets would add rows telling nothing the itemized line does not already show, and would lengthen the conservation identity. Reversible the moment a future dial needs one of these as a first-class length input. **R3 was a confirmation, not a change:** every in-play tie-up already awards the ball to the possession-arrow owner and flips the arrow (routine alternating possession, correct college basketball); only the opening/OT tip is a real wingspan contest with the loser owed the arrow. Emmett confirmed the behavior; no engine change — any change to the tip would touch `JumpBall.cs`, walled out of this session.

**Phase B — the fix, per the rulings.** The two Roll K labels joined `IsTurnoverPossession` (now **17 labels**), locked and unconditional. R1 added nothing (held-ball losses stay off the turnover line). R2 kept OTHER whole, so the §3.8 conservation identity's term list was **unchanged** — the two labels simply migrate from the OtherN term to the TurnoverN term, and the identity sum is invariant to which bucket they sit in. The §3.8 block gained the **whitelist guard** as check (g): every label residing in OTHER must be one of the named residuals (jump-ball with suffix exactly Home or Away, offensive loose-ball foul, offense-OOB); any other label — **including any parked terminal** — is a hard failure naming the label. `parked:*` is explicitly NOT an accepted residual: every page to date reads zero parks, so a park is an engine dead-end to investigate, not a residual to tolerate.

**The scope-reshaper caught at build time — a second reconciliation the prompt did not name.** The prompt's §0.5 named the observation mode as the *one* place the classifier change would ripple, "the only known exception." Grepping the classifier's callers on the fresh pull found that assertion was incomplete: **`AttributionSanityCheck` (Phase 24) carries the identical per-player-turnover identity** — sum of per-player TO credits == total turnovers minus the unattributed labels — runs 200 populated games that produce offensive rebounds, sets `sanityOk = false` on failure, and **is in the suite.** Without a matching fix there, counting the Roll K turnovers would have broken that identity by exactly the leaked count, and "suite all green" would have carried a hard red, not the cosmetic observation-only line the prompt anticipated. This is precisely the Session 32 gate lesson — a check whose term list structurally expects the old turnover set must move in lockstep. Both reconciliations (observation + Phase 24) got the same exemption: the two Roll K labels added to the already-subtracted unattributed set, the same shape as the existing team-violation exemption. A third caller — `Phase33TurnoverCommitterCheck` — was checked and left alone: it inspects only committer-bearing turnovers (which Roll K is not), so it cannot break; its stale "mirrors the harness helper" comment was corrected to say the two Roll K labels are deliberately omitted as slot-less. Bench and Gen (diagnostic modes, never in the suite) were left untouched with a deferral logged. **This was a build-time call** (extending ruling B's exemption to a second, unnamed site rather than stopping to re-litigate) — flagged to Emmett in the delivery; the alternative was shipping a knowingly-red suite.

**Validation.** Suite: `ALL CHECKS PASSED`, with the new whitelist line green (`OTHER whitelist — ... no label hides here`), the drift guard still green (confirming the Roll K records carry no metadata), and both reconciliations reconciling cleanly (Phase 24's TO line now reads `team violations N + Roll K post-ORB M correctly unattributed`). The Monte-Carlo pre-check mirrored the accumulator arithmetic against the Phase A numbers and matched the harness to the record: conservation delta 0, whitelist accepts exactly the four residuals with zero offenders, projected page movement dead-on. Season page at 20260703: turnover **n=136,918** (+4,269), OTHER **n=27,653** itemizing to exactly the four named residuals (9,609 + 7,263 + 7,162 + 3,619), turnovers/team **13.3 HIGH**, TO% **20.4 HIGH** — the corrected reading, pre-fix and post-fix recorded side by side per §1. Turnover-length ticked 17.6 → 17.9s (the long Roll K turnovers pulling the mean up); everything else on the page byte-identical to the pre-fix run. Honest verdict: reasoned + Monte-Carlo-traced, then harness-confirmed on Emmett's machine.

**Deferrals recorded this session:** the **turnover-clock dial** (now with a cleaner, leak-free turnover-length reading); the **shot-diet and whistle dials** (unchanged, still the points-gap's owners); the **steals/dead-ball composition question** (sharpened by the corrected count and by the confirmed steal-side symmetry); **player-level attribution for held balls and Roll K turnovers** (aggregate-only this session — held-ball records retain no slot, Roll K records carry no committer); the **observation mode's own coarse bucketing** (it already sweeps the two Roll K labels into its Turnover bucket by fallthrough, so its terminal-mix Other stayed 0.0000 — untouched by scope wall, no change needed); **Bench/Gen turnover residual labels** (the printed "team-violations" figure there now silently includes Roll K — harmless, diagnostic-only, parked); **multi-seed measurement**; the **RollHConfig anchor comment** (carried from Session 32). Calibration itself remains deferred until the diet/whistle dials close the points gap.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Harness.Shared.cs` — EDIT (the two Roll K labels into `IsTurnoverPossession`, now 17). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Season.Calibration.cs` — EDIT (Phase A: per-label OTHER tally + jump-ball award split accumulators and the itemized printer block). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.Season.cs` — EDIT (§3.8 check (g), the OTHER whitelist guard). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Observation.cs` — EDIT (Roll K exemption in the per-player-TO reconciliation). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.GameLifecycle.cs` — EDIT (the same exemption in Phase 24's reconciliation — the unnamed scope-reshaper — plus the corrected mirror comment in Phase 33). **No engine source file changed, no config changed.**

## Session 32 — The make dial, pass 1: per-zone midpoints recentered to the living population (2026-07-03)

**Scope:** Config-and-instrument only — the first tuning session against the Session 31 measuring stick, run as two harness runs with an oracle between, plus one Emmett-approved mid-session deviation (two stale harness checks made curve-relative). **No engine source file changed.** The problem, measured: the season shot FG% 55.8 vs 44.0 and 3P% 50.1 vs 34.0 — because the Session 50 curves anchored **rating 50 = real D1 average** and the divvied population's effective shooting sits far above 50, cashing in exactly as designed. The dial: slide each zone's logistic **midpoint** so an average shooter *in our league* lands on the real per-zone anchors (Three 34 / Long 36 / Mid 39 / Short 43 / Rim 61). Emmett's standing rulings held throughout: **recenter, never compress** (floors, ceilings, K untouched — a great shooter stays exactly as far ahead of average as before); a still-high combined FG% would not be chased (it landed OK anyway); one dial family, everything else reported only.

**Two rulings locked at the check-in gate, both load-bearing.** (1) **The 20 per-zone logistic parameters move into config.json.** The prompt assumed they already lived there; the gate found all 20 existed only as C# auto-property defaults in `RollHConfig`. Emmett's call: canonicalize — all 20 keys added to the RollH section, fifteen carrying the exact Session 50 defaults, five carrying the new midpoints. Config is now the single live home of the curve, and the oracle reads it directly (no second copy anywhere). (2) **The midpoint commit range widened from the drafted [0, 100] to [0, 120].** Read from source at the gate: authored attributes live in 0–99 (`Player.Validate`), but the curve eats the matchup-shifted **effective** rating, uncapped by design — and the observed 50% three-point shooting itself implies the league's average effective Three rating is ~94, so a midpoint above 100 is the dial doing its job, not diagnostic nonsense. Load-bearing because **Long (102.68) and Three (109.97) both landed above 100** — under the rule as drafted, this session would have ended in a STOP-and-report instead of a fix.

**Phase A — the instrument rider (harness-only, delivered first).** `SeasonLeagueStats` gained eight per-zone longs (Three rides the existing 3PA/3PM pair), fed in the existing per-record loop; the readout gained a per-zone FG% block after the main table — sim vs the Session 50 anchors, ±1.0 bands, LOW/OK/HIGH, page-only like every row — plus a zone-FGA-mix line printing the conservation sum in the open. The five anchor targets live in **one static table beside the printer, the sole committed home of those constants**; the oracle receives them as command-line inputs copied from the page, never a second hard-coded copy. Phase 55 §3.8 gained its sixth check: **league-scale zone conservation** — Rim+Short+Mid+Long+Three FGA == FGA and the FGM twin (the per-possession identity is asserted per-seed in Program.Observation's zone-bin checks; this proves the ACCUMULATOR preserved it across a full fixture season) — no make-rate value asserted, ever, by design. Measured at seed 20260703: **rim 67.7 / short 51.7 / mid 51.7 / long 49.6 / three 50.1 — every zone HIGH**, sum conserved exactly (557,781 == 557,781).

**Phase B — the oracle (`tools/make_midpoint_oracle.py`, committed).** A declared **first-order proposal, not a population-rating recovery**: the post-logistic adjustment stack (openness, spacing/gravity, usage tax, passing, screening, help/off-ball suppression, hustle, IQ) and live matchup bending of block/foul are unmodeled, with the bounded run-2 iteration as the convergence mechanism. It reads curve and carve parameters from config.json, validates exactly five zones, mirrors `MakeProbability` constant-for-constant, and inverts through the exact box-score identity (**MissFouled is not an FGA; MadeAndFouled is FGA and FGM**: observed = [make·(1−block−foul) + foul·maf] / [1 − foul·(1−maf)]) by bisection on the exact curve — no linearization. Two stop rules: solvability (a clean make at/outside the open (floor, ceiling) interval has no inversion) and the [0, 120] commit range. Rim is declared a **mixed-sample heuristic** (pools ordinary attempts and putbacks; the record carries no putback tag — the resolver's count reaches the walk outcome as `PutbackAttempts` but the Governor never copies it to `PossessionRecord`, so the prompt's conclusion held). First derivation: shifts **Rim +24.8, Short +33.6, Mid +52.6, Long +43.1, Three +49.4**; forward-checked exact in the sandbox (the new curve at the observed-implied rating reproduces each target through the carve to the digit). One source fact recorded in passing: the Session 50 Three fit carries a small residual — a rating-50 shooter reads ~35.7% observed against the 34.0 anchor, and Three is the one zone whose target inverts to rating ~44.8 where the other four invert to ~50.0 on the nose. The oracle's exact math absorbs it; noted, not chased.

**Run 2 → one iteration → run 3: every zone OK.** Run 2 landed four of five in band — **rim 61.2 dead-on despite the putback worry** — with mid LOW at 37.7 vs a 38.0–40.0 band. Per the locked protocol (one derive-apply iteration, then stop regardless), the oracle reran on run-2 numbers: mid −4.66 → **90.3196**; the four in-band zones' sub-1.3-point proposals were deliberately **not** applied (an in-band zone stays put — nudging it re-rolls its dice for no gain). Run 3: **rim 61.1 / short 42.8 / mid 38.9 / long 35.6 / three 33.6 — all five OK.** The session's success criterion, met with the iteration budget to spare.

**The one deviation — two Phase 6 harness checks had gone stale, and were made curve-relative (Emmett-approved mid-session).** The first post-change suite run failed on Phase 6 (d) and (f) — not engine misbehavior, but the checks' assumptions about **where authored ratings sit on the curve**: (d) asserted the 90→99 make gain is smaller than 30→50 (diminishing returns at the top), which is false once the midpoint sits above the authored range — **the entire 0–99 scale now lives on the rising side of the curve, so a 90→99 jump buys more than 30→50**, a real design consequence of recenter-not-compress that now belongs to the deferred curve-steepness conversation; (f) demanded a strong defender cut a rating-50 shooter's three by a fixed ≥3 points, but that shooter now sits in the flat lower tail where the true drop is ~2.2. Both rewritten to ask the loaded curve itself: (d) asserts flattening **above the loaded midpoint** (a logistic property, true at any midpoint; the authored-range sweep keeps its monotonicity and ceiling assertions), and (f) computes the **expected drop from the loaded curve** and demands the sampled batch match it within 0.01 — exact in that fixture because every bending attribute is even across arms (baseline carve; drop = analytic × (1−block−foul)) and the batch reuses one RNG stream across arms (noise ~0.001). This is the second recalibration of (f)'s margin (0.05→0.03 at Session 50); the curve-relative form **retires the pattern** — the suite now stays green across every future turn of this dial, which the §0.2 gate demanded by design but two checks quietly violated. Gate honesty note: the pre-build grep hunted hard-coded make **rates** and found none; these were hard-coded **slope/margin** expectations, a class the next dial prompt should name explicitly.

**The card after (read and reported, never chased).** Combined **FG% 44.8 OK** — the predicted may-stay-HIGH on the rim-heavy mix did not materialize. Points fell through the band to **LOW 62.7**: the league now shoots realistically but is three-starved (3PA rate 0.21 vs 0.39) and whistle-light (FT rate 0.26 vs 0.34) — the remaining points gap belongs to the diet and whistle dials, cleanly separated from accuracy for the first time. Credited rebounds climbed 23.0 → 28.6 (more misses, more boards) but stay LOW; assists fell 19.9 → 15.8 (still HIGH); pace slid to LOW 65.5; OT 3.1% still LOW; steals LOW unchanged; **ORB% 29.2 OK throughout — that machinery was never the problem.** The standings churned completely on the same seed — Maine 25-5 atop the table where La Salle's 25-5 dissolved to 21-9 — same schedule, same rosters, every shot re-decided by the new curves: determinism working exactly as promised.

**Deferrals recorded this session:** **curve steepness** (its own design conversation before any K moves — now carrying the sharpened observation that diminishing returns at the top no longer exist inside the authored 0–99 range); **the shot-diet dial** (3PA rate 0.21 vs 0.39); **the whistle** (FTA LOW — and the standing condition rides here: if the Roll H block/foul baselines ever move, the rim/short midpoints re-derive); **the putback record tag** (not needed — rim converged without the split; stays parked as a named option); **the RollHConfig anchor comment** ("rating 50 = real D1 average" is now stale-in-place — the one-line correction rides the next session that legitimately touches engine files; a comment edit alone does not justify breaking this session's wall); **the OTHER-bucket breakdown** (carried from Session 31); **multi-seed measurement** (pass 1 recentered against 20260703 alone; a later pass may blend seeds if per-zone drift proves material).

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Season.Calibration.cs` — EDIT (per-zone accumulator longs, the static anchor-target table, the per-zone readout block + mix line). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.Season.cs` — EDIT (§3.8 league-scale zone conservation). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.Shooting.cs` — EDIT (Phase 6 (d)/(f) made curve-relative). `src/Charm.Harness/config.json` — EDIT (all 20 per-zone logistic parameters canonicalized into the RollH section; five midpoints recentered: Three 60.6 → **109.9675**, Long 59.5793 → **102.6819**, Mid 42.3369 → **90.3196** in two steps (94.9805 at run 2, −4.66 at the iteration), Short 42.3369 → **75.9276**, Rim 43.9840 → **68.7559**). `tools/make_midpoint_oracle.py` — NEW (the committed derivation, its caveats printed with every run). **No engine source file changed, comments included.**
