## Session 31 — The calibration instrument: league readout vs the D1 decade blend (2026-07-03)

**Scope:** Harness-only, no engine changes, no config changes, no tuning — the measuring stick, not the dials. The season loop stops discarding its per-game numbers: the attribution box the game body already computes (and the loop threw away with a `_`) now feeds a league-wide accumulator, and the season page gains one section after SANITY PULSE — **sim vs. a blend of the last decade of D1 men's averages (2015-16..2024-25), line by line, LOW/OK/HIGH per row** — plus a seconds-per-possession split by how possessions end. Emmett's rulings, locked 2026-07-03 before drafting: the reference is the decade blend; **targets carry tolerance bands, not bullseyes, and live on the page only** — never a suite assertion, because rates move when dials are tuned later and hard-asserting them would make every future calibration session break the suite by design; turnover possessions should eventually draw less clock *on average* with the full range staying legal (a shifted draw center, never a truncated window) — **this session measures, the dial is deferred**; no tuning of any kind.

**All five §0 assumptions held at the check-in gate, verified against the pulled source.** The per-possession record carries `Elapsed` (the capped per-possession clock charge) and `EndLabel`, with NoShot and HoldShootLast identified via the record's `EndOfHalfIntent` field — never via EndLabel, because HoldShootLast still runs the resolver and can end Made/DREB/turnover; both are excluded from the length buckets but included in pace. Turnover classification has one canonical home — `IsTurnoverPossession`, the committed 15-label classifier — and the instrument calls it, never re-listing the labels; turnover *metadata* is read only by the drift guard. Total personal fouls are **not** retained across a game (`ResetForNewHalf` fires at the half; no cumulative counter exists), so the PF row is dropped from v1 rather than reconstructed — a non-shooting defensive foul below the bonus leaves no countable trace, and an estimate must not wear a measurement's clothes. Two notes flagged and accepted at the gate: the observation run's own drift guard re-lists the labels inline (the new check calls the helper instead — the observation file stays untouched, outside scope), and the accumulator landed in a new `Program.Season.Calibration.cs` rather than crowding the 565-line season file whose header is the schedule oracle spec.

**The instrument.** `SeasonLeagueStats` is fed once per game inside `RunSeasonCore` from the `(game, result, attributed)` triple — the only game-loop change is keeping what was discarded. From records: FGA/FGM, 3PA/3PM, FTA/FTM, record Points (a cross-check), possession count, turnover count via the helper, per-bucket (count, elapsed sum), and a **per-game elapsed guard** (`|sum of record Elapsed − TotalSeconds|` — per-game, not a season aggregate offsetting errors could satisfy; both sides sum the identical applied doubles, so exact equality is expected and the 1e-6 tolerance is defensive). From the box, all 20 indices: OReb/DReb/Ast/Stl/Blk — every league line is side-symmetric, so a green §3.8 must never be read as re-proving the §1b credit mapping; Phase 55's replay owns that. Denominators are exact and stated in the code: **every per-team-per-game volume divides by 2·G** (the league totals pool both teams), percentages are straight ratios, pace is actual possession records per team OT-included, TO% is turnover possessions over total records. The buckets: MADE / FT-TRIP / MISS-DREB / MISS-OOB / TURNOVER (with a fixed-time-violation sub-line: the three invariant-clock labels at 30.0/0.0/10.0s) / OTHER (parked:*, LooseBallFoulOnOffense, future labels) / EXCLUDED, conserving to the total. The reference card is **provisional by design** — center points compiled from published national per-season averages, not yet pinned to one saved source extract; the bands (±1.0 point on percentages, ±5% relative on volumes) are 5–10× wider than any methodology-of-averaging difference, so a verdict cannot flip on provenance; when a tuning session needs a bullseye on a line, it pins that line's source first. The card's stated caveat: public rebound totals include *team* rebounds; the sim total is all credited individual boards (the closest engine analog of the uncredited board is the MissOutOfBoundsLost ending) — the gap is made visible, not papered over.

**Phase 55 §3.8 — machinery only, five checks, zero basketball values asserted, zero additional games** (it reads the accumulator the §3.5 fixture run now carries on `SeasonRunOutcome`): (a) **triple point reconciliation** — recorded game scores == record Points == accumulator points, all three printed (fixture: 44,731 three ways); (b) the **drift guard** — every record carrying turnover metadata satisfies the classifier, so a future TO label turns red instead of leaking into OTHER; (c) the **bucket conservation identity** (fixture: 16479+3101+9788+464+7617+1656+691 == 39,796 exactly); (d) the **per-game elapsed guard** == 0 mismatched games (max delta printed: exactly zero); (e) FGM ≥ 3PM, FTA ≥ FTM, every total non-negative.

**Validation — ALL CHECKS PASSED on the machine (252 OK, 0 FAIL), and the first calibration readout of Project Charm is on the page.** Pre-checks in the sandbox: a 200k-record Monte Carlo mirroring the classification, conservation identity, elapsed guard, and verdict bands, all green; one real compile risk caught pre-delivery (concatenated interpolated strings lose `FormattableString`, breaking the invariant-culture wrapper — restructured). The stock page at seed 20260703, read and reported, not chased: **the headline is that shots go in far too often** — FG% 55.8 vs 44.0, 3P% 50.1 vs 34.0 — and most of the card is downstream of that one fact: FGA LOW and total rebounds very LOW because makes end possessions and misses create boards, assists HIGH (19.9 vs 13.5) partly because there are more makes to assist on, points HIGH (75.3) on efficiency alone despite low volume. **The telling OK: ORB% at 29.0 vs 28.5** — when a miss does happen, the fight for the board splits realistically; the rebound machinery looks right, it is starved of misses. Independent of the make problem, two shape findings: **the shot diet is three-starved** (3PA rate 0.21 vs 0.39 — a diet issue, separate from accuracy) and **the turnover composition leans dead-ball** (steals LOW 4.4 vs 6.2 while total turnovers run slightly HIGH). Pace OK (66.6 vs 69.0), FT% OK (70.2), TO% OK (19.8). The length split: turnover possessions 17.3s vs ~18.2s for shooting endings — nearly identical, which is exactly the gap the deferred turnover-clock dial exists to widen; fixed-time violations 15.3s. The known lines confirmed: points HIGH, OT LOW (2.9% vs 4–8%). **One flag recorded, not chased: the OTHER bucket is ~4% of all possessions (28,746 stock; 4.2% fixture — consistent), against a near-zero expectation** — parked stubs and offensive loose-ball fouls; a future session should print its per-label breakdown, since 4% is large enough to matter for the rebound and FT lines.

**Deferrals recorded this session:** **turnover clock weighting** (a shorter draw *center* through the existing ClockDraw, same floor/cap — home: a pace calibration session, informed by this split); **reference-card source pinning** (per line, when a tuning session needs a bullseye); **the total-PF cumulative counter** (a small additive engine-side counter, when a fouls/whistle pass needs the PF line); **the OTHER-bucket breakdown** (named above); and **calibration tuning itself — dial by dial, one per session, against this page.**

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Season.Calibration.cs` — NEW (the accumulator, the provisional reference card, the printer). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Season.cs` — EDIT (keep `attributed`, feed the accumulator, carry it on `SeasonRunOutcome`, print the readout after SANITY PULSE). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.Season.cs` — EDIT (§3.8, plus one header sentence). **No engine change, no config change, no tuning.**

**Next:** Emmett's call between the arc map's Pass 3 (the prestige dynamics) and the first calibration tuning sessions this instrument now enables — the card's own reading suggests the make-rates are the highest-leverage first dial, and the OTHER-bucket breakdown is a cheap instrument follow-up either way. The next-session prompt is its own audited pass.

## Session 30.1 — The opening five seats a wing: the floor is now 1B/2G/1W, and the no-wing residual is retired (2026-07-03)

**Scope:** A micro-session of one seating-rule change, made against new evidence. The Session 29.1 floor (>=1 big, >=2 guards) accepted the no-wing five as a legal small-ball residual — visible as one warning line on a smoke-sim page. The first stock season changed the size of that fact: **44 of 347 schools opened without a wing, and under the fence's same-position pairing their three benched wings played zero possessions across an entire 30-game season.** Emmett saw the season page, asked whether the cause was wing supply (it is not — every roster carries exactly three wings by pool construction; the gap was purely the seating rule), and ruled: **the floor extends to at least one wing.** The quota is now >=1B / >=2G / >=1W with one free slot, and the residual is retired — every position now seats at least one starter, so every benched player has a same-position door.

**The change is three lines, and it was proven exhaustively, not sampled.** `BuildOpeningFive` gains a third counter (`needW = 1`) in the same greedy walk — take the earliest player, skip one only when taking him would strand an unmet quota. The mandatory pre-check ran the new walk over **all 4,200 distinct orderings of a 4G/3W/3B roster** (an exhaustive proof of the entire input space, since the walk reads only positions in order): every ordering seats a legal five, the walk never strands, and the opening five still equals the raw first five whenever the raw five already satisfies the quotas. About 10% of orderings change their five versus the old walk — consistent with the 44/347 (12.7%) observed on the Session 30 page. Downstream, three assertion sites gained the wing: Phase 54 §9d (the floor check on every roster in both worlds, and the raw-satisfies condition), Phase 55's opening-five check on the prestige-0 schools, and the walk's contract comment. **The absent-position warnings (smoke sim and season prep) stay, repurposed as never-fire sentinels** per the 29.1 once-per-side contract — a NOTE line printing anywhere is now a seating bug, and the season page's pass signal flipped from "44 expected lines" to "zero lines."

**What deliberately did not change:** the schedule and its fingerprint (the schedule never reads rosters — the page printed the identical 29fd9e25… hash), the divvy itself (the walk runs after rosters are drafted and is rank-blind), the `gen` mode (its assembly never used `BuildOpeningFive`), and the engine.

**Validation on the machine — ALL CHECKS PASSED, zero NOTE lines, and the standings re-read.** Phase 54's floor line went green across both worlds under the new quota. The stock season at the same seed: **the proof table's middle plateau resolved** — Session 30 read 12.9 / 14.5 / 14.5 flat across the middle bands; with every school's wings playing it reads 12.8 / 14.4 / **14.8** / 16.5 / 17.5, cleanly ordered bottom to top — recorded as an observation (one seed, real games), not a proven causal claim. Duke moved 15-15 → 16-14 with its wings on the floor; La Salle (prestige 48) took the table at 25-5 behind three leaked top-decile players, the escapes table naming all three; Iowa State fell to the bottom at 5-25. OT 152/5205 (2.9%), average total score 150.5 — both stable. The elite-variance and compressed-spread calibration observations from Session 30 stand unchanged.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Divvy.cs` — EDIT (the wing counter in `BuildOpeningFive`; the contract comment records the 30.1 ruling and retires the residual; the smoke-sim warning re-commented as a sentinel). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.Divvy.cs` — EDIT (§9d floor + raw-satisfies gain the wing). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.Season.cs` — EDIT (the prestige-0 opening-five check gains the wing). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Season.cs` — EDIT (comment only: the prep warning is a sentinel). **No engine change, no schedule change, no config change.**

**Next:** unchanged from Session 30 — **Pass 3 of the arc, the prestige dynamics** (the four forces + clamps, oracle-first), with calibration's precondition met and its data points accumulating. The next-session prompt is its own audited pass.

## Session 30 — World Structure Pass 2: the minimal season loop — 5,205 real games, and prestige-as-access shows up in the standings (2026-07-03)

**Scope:** Pass 2 of the world-structure arc: the **minimal season loop** — a new `season <world.json> <seed>` mode that regenerates every school's divvied roster (world + seed, nothing persisted — the S29 contract exercised for the first time), builds a **deterministic 30-game schedule** (16 conference + 14 non-conference per team, exactly 15 home / 15 away, neutral floors — the road seam stays 0), plays **all 5,205 stock games through the real engine**, and prints the standings page: all 347 schools ranked by W-L, the prestige-band proof table, the top-ten overachievers with their leaked top-decile talent named, and the OT sanity pulse. **Harness-only** — nothing under `src/Charm.Engine/` changed — and the `gen` mode and divvy smoke sim stay **byte-for-byte** behind the session's one structural move: the single-game body was extracted out of `RunGenMatchup` into a shared helper so the season and the lab run the *same* game code from one construction site. Emmett's four rulings, locked 2026-07-02 before drafting: 30 games as 16+14; neutral floors this pass; the page shows the **full** 347-row table plus the proof table and the overachievers; and OT needed no work — the Governor's untimed-until-untied loop was already real, so a season can simply assert that no tie survives.

**The check-in gate ran in full; all eight load-bearing assumptions held, and the audit surfaced one wrinkle worth designing around.** Verified against pulled source before the go: the OT loop cannot exit tied; scores live at `GameState.HomeScore/AwayScore` and the committed gen path reads them; `RunGenMatchup` loads its ~20 configs per call (the extraction's justification); sides are stamped per matchup (A → PlayerIds 1–10, B → 11–20); `RoadMakePenalty` ships 0.0; the stock world is 347 schools / 32 conferences with sizes 8–16 and the fixture 4×5, with the extra-meeting parity condition (r·s even) verified for every occurring size — and provably **always** even at 16 games, so the preflight's parity check is contract protection for a future games-count change, never a live trap; the divvy is deterministic from (world, seed); and exactly two prestige-0 schools exist. The wrinkle: the committed gen seed scheme (resolver `base+i`, governor `base+i+1`) lets game *i*'s governor seed equal game *i+1*'s resolver seed. Harmless in the lab; the season deliberately uses a **stride-2 scheme** (resolver `base+2i`, governor `base+2i+1`) so its resolver and governor seed sets are disjoint by construction — asserted in Phase 55, with `gen` untouched behind the wall.

**The schedule builder was oracle-proven before a line of C# — 960 seeded builds green — and the oracle is committed this time.** The contract (the oracle docstring is the spec; the C# header restates it): the schedule gets its **own SplitMix64 stream** (`WorldRng(seasonSeed ^ 0x5EA5C4ED)`, the sample-sheet XOR pattern) consumed in a fixed order — one Fisher-Yates ring shuffle, then one draw per actual conflict repair; **conference slates and orientation consume no randomness at all**. Conference slates are pure structure: conferences by id, members by id, `base = 16/(s−1)` meetings per pair plus an r-regular **canonical circulant** of extra meetings (r even → offsets 1..r/2; r odd — s even by parity — → offsets plus the diameter matching), emitted i<j with multi-meetings consecutive. Non-conference is a **14-regular simple graph with no conference-mates**: shuffle the schools into a ring, take the k=1..7 circulant (14-regular by construction), then repair each conference-mate conflict by a **double-edge swap** (seeded scan start, first legal rewiring of R1 `(a,c)+(b,d)` then R2 `(a,d)+(b,c)`; swaps preserve 14-regularity, so only simplicity and the mate ban ever need checking). One addition earned by the acceptance run itself: the fixture is razor-tight (15 eligible opponents, 14 needed — every school must play all-but-one of its eligibles), and single-swap repair dead-ends on ~1 in 20 fixture seeds — so a failed attempt **restarts with a fresh shuffle from the same continuing stream, up to 20 attempts**, then fails loudly naming the stuck pairing. Measured: fixture retries histogram {1: 474, 2: 25, 3: 1} over 500 seeds; **stock completed on attempt 1 in all 260 of 260 builds**. Every build proved every invariant: 16+14=30 per team, floor/ceil conference meetings, no repeat non-conference pairs, no mates, no self-games. The Session 29 lesson (an uncommitted oracle cost 29.1 a rebuild) is applied: **`tools/schedule_oracle.py` ships in the repo**.

**Orientation is a small piece of graph theory doing honest work: exactly 15 home / 15 away, always, with no randomness.** Every team's multigraph degree is 30 — even — so every component carries an Eulerian circuit; a deterministic Hierholzer walk (components by lowest id, adjacency in game-index order) orients each game in its consumption direction, from = home, and a closed circuit forces out = in = 15 at every vertex. The road seam is 0 today, but no school banks a lopsided home ledger against the day it is not. The whole schedule then serializes to a **SHA-256 fingerprint** (`gameIndex|kind|homeId|awayId` per line, schedule order, never re-sorted), printed on the page and asserted by Phase 55 against the oracle export at the fixed seed 20260703 — the stock fingerprint matched to the digit on the machine.

**The extraction, and what it accidentally proved about prestige.** `RunGenMatchup`'s loop body moved verbatim into `RunSingleGenGame(configs, sideA, sideB, teamASide, teamBSide, resolverSeed, governorSeed)` with configs pre-loaded once per caller into a `GenEngineConfigs` record (same Load calls, same order). One expression transliterated of necessity — `teamAIsHome ? aDepth : bDepth` became `teamASide == TeamSide.Home ? ...`, identical semantics since the flag and the side are definitionally equivalent at both call sites — and attribution kept its committed seed (the resolver seed). `gen` computes the same seeds and side alternation and delegates, so the byte-for-byte wall holds by construction. The accidental finding: the loop body **never reads a `GenProgram`** — the smoke sim only builds them because the old signature demanded a `GenConfig`. So the season path carries **no GenProgram at all**, and the prompt's §3.4 clamp check (prestige 0 → 1 at the generation seam) had no plumbing to attach to. Reported as the session's one divergence and replaced by the **stronger structural claim, asserted in Phase 55: prestige's only door into a season game is the roster the divvy drafted** — there is no side door to clamp. The season runner itself: per-school `GenPlayerRow` lists built once (the smoke sim's exact Rows shape, opening five per the 29.1 seating floor, the absent-position warning printed once per affected school — 44 no-wing schools on the stock page, the accepted residual visible at population scale for the first time); sides stamped per game (home 1–10, away 11–20); **HomeSchool → the engine's Home side, full stop** — the §1b mapping a flipped implementation of which would pass every conservation and determinism check, which is exactly why Phase 55 carries an independent replay.

**Phase 55 — twenty-one checks, all green on the machine, and honest about what a green run proves.** Stock schedule legality in full plus the oracle fingerprint and the seed-set disjointness; build determinism; the preflight rejecting a rigged one-school conference **by name** (the rigged world first proven valid under the Pass 1 validator, so the red is provably the preflight's) while explicitly **not** rejecting a two-school conference (s=2 is legal: sixteen meetings of one opponent); the adapted §3.4 (rows for all 347, world unmutated, both prestige-0 schools still read 0 and seat a legal five); a full fixture season conserving exactly (every team 30 results, wins == losses == 300, zero ties, a strict winner every game); the **attribution replay** — game 0 rebuilt independently and rerun on the season's seeds, its scores matching the recorded result, proving home scores land on home schools end to end; standings asserted to be exactly the fold of the recorded results (no second bookkeeping path); and a second full fixture season identical to the first, score for score. **Proven:** schedule legality and oracle fidelity, determinism, conservation, the credit mapping. **Not proven:** outcome realism, calibration direction, or that the proof table's shape is basketball truth — page-level findings, never suite assertions. Cost note: Phase 55 plays ~600 fixture engine games, a visible bump in suite time, accepted.

**Validation on the machine — ALL CHECKS PASSED, and the first season of Project Charm is on the page.** Stock season at seed 20260703: fingerprint matched, 5,205 games played, Arizona 24-6 at the top of a full 347-row table, Tennessee-Martin 6-24 at the bottom. **The proof table climbs: band average wins 12.9 / 14.5 / 14.5 / 16.5 / 17.6 from bottom band to top.** Prestige-as-access is now visible at season scale — and three observations are **recorded for basketball judgment, not acted on**: (1) the two middle bands sit dead even at 14.5, and the whole top-to-bottom spread is ~5 wins over a 30-game season — consistent in direction with Session 27's fence-era margin compression, a calibration item now measurable against a living population; (2) elite-prestige variance is wide — Duke (98) went 15-15 while Kansas (97) went 22-8 and Texas (94) 23-7 — and the no-wing-on-the-floor residual shows **mixed** evidence at the extremes (Duke 15-15, Missouri 9-21, Air Force 8-22 lacked a wing; so did West Virginia at 22-8 and Louisville at 20-10), so no clean signal is claimed either way; (3) the sanity pulse reads plausible — 167 of 5,205 games to overtime (3.2%, a touch under real college rates), average total score 150.5. The escapes table works as designed: George Washington +9.5 over band with a leaked top-decile wing named, and three of the ten overachievers carried **no** top-decile player at all — overperformance without a star, which is the matchup engine talking rather than the pool.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Season.cs` — NEW (preflight, the oracle-mirrored schedule builder with the bounded retry, Hierholzer orientation, the fingerprint, the season runner, the standings page, the `season` CLI). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.Season.cs` — NEW (Phase 55). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Gen.cs` — EDIT (the `GenEngineConfigs` record + loader and `RunSingleGenGame`; `RunGenMatchup` delegates). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.cs` — EDIT (the `season` dispatch returning before the suite; Phase 55 registered). `tools/schedule_oracle.py` — NEW (the committed oracle). **No engine change, no config change, no csproj change.**

**Next:** per the arc map, **Pass 3 — the prestige dynamics** (the four forces + clamps, oracle-first), now buildable against a season loop that actually produces results for the forces to read. Separately, the standing precondition for **calibration** — a real, varied, living population — is now met for the first time; when calibration begins is Emmett's call, and this session's three recorded observations (the band plateau, the compressed spread, the OT rate) are its first data points. The next-session prompt is its own audited pass.

## Session 29.1 — Fair scouting and a playable floor: FT out of the rank, big athleticism graded on the big scale, the opening five gets 1B/2G (2026-07-02)

**Scope:** A micro-session of three surgical changes inside the Session 29 divvy layer, nothing under `src/Charm.Engine/`, driven by three basketball rulings Emmett made after reading the Session 29 stock pages: **(1) shooting must not buy prestige access** — the scout rank read the whole skill-leg mean, FreeThrow included, so good FT shooters drifted up the prestige ladder systematically; the rank's skill input now excludes FreeThrow (the FT draw itself and the sheet's FT column are untouched). **(2) Scouting is position-relative** — the rank already judged size per position (the affine map) and skill per position (holes exclude irrelevant skills), but athleticism was read raw, so every board docked bigs the built-in mobility downshift and elite posts sat a full noise-band low; a big's athleticism mean is now graded back onto the position's own scale by re-adding `GenBigAthDownshift`. **(3) The opening five gets a playable floor** — the earliest five acquired that includes at least 1 big and at least 2 guards; everything else stays first-come, and acquisition order remains the immutable depth order.

**The add-back is the exact inverse — proven post-enforcement, with a standing condition.** Piece 2 is only correct if "mean + 8" exactly undoes the generation-side "−8", so the full trace was run against pulled source at draft time and re-verified at the gate: the downshift is applied at all three ATH draw sites (plus branch, ordinary branch, the third-leg redraw's ATH arm); the position floors never touch an athleticism rating (the guard/wing driving-access test reads ATH but writes a shooting rating; a big's floors are rebounding and rim presence); bigs have no ATH holes, so the mean is over all seven ratings; the worst possible post-shift draw is 26 (scarce band 34 minus 8), so the zero-clamp never binds and the pool's leg-health floor of 20 never lifts a big's ATH leg; the team-variety lean tilt is never called on the pool path; `GenMapToPlayer` copies without clamps. **Standing condition, carried forward: if the scarce band's floor or the pool leg-health floor ever moves, this proof is re-run before the +8 is trusted again.**

**The oracle was rebuilt and proven faithful before the change went in.** The Session 29 oracle lived in that session's sandbox and was not committed, so this session rebuilt it constant-for-constant from the committed C# (the RNG-consumption contract in the source header is the spec) and — before touching the rank — verified it reproduces the committed Phase 54 constants: the noise triples to 1e-15, both apportionments, the rank formula fixtures to 1e-9, and, at the fixed stock seed, the exact group means (251/212/178/162/160) and the exact leak count (48). The full-pipeline reproduction of those two seed-pinned numbers is strong evidence of a bit-faithful mirror end to end.

**The acceptance hit the prompt's stop condition — and what broke turned out to be revealed truth, not regression.** With the fair rank in, the 260-seed acceptance (200 fixture, 60 stock) came back clean on every hard invariant — zero stalls, every roster legal and covered, protected-supply slack never negative, the leak alive in 197/200 and 60/60 — but two of the carried assertions failed, and per the prompt's own instruction the session stopped and reported instead of re-tuning. **(a) "Scarce two-leg outranks one-leg on average" broke — and it was already false per-position in the committed engine:** a one-leg guard has averaged above a scarce two-leg guard all along (165.7 vs 163.7); the pooled means only ordered because unfairly-cheap bigs dragged the one-leg average down. **(b) The borderline/useful tiers stopped overlapping in true rank (0/60 seeds; 20/20 under the old rank):** the old overlap was manufactured by each tier mixing fairly-graded perimeter players with ~25-point-discounted bigs, inflating the spread; with positions co-located the tiers separate cleanly — while the board noise every school sees (sigma ~10.7) still exceeds the tier gap (~7.5), so on the boards schools actually draft from the tiers still blur. Emmett ruled on both: **two strong legs plus one bad leg ≈ one strong leg plus two passable ones is fine** (future coach layers will bend individual boards toward size or other preferences), and **tiers cleanly separated in true ability with the mixing coming entirely from scouting error is fine** (same reasoning). The assertions were rewritten to certify the ruled world: three > borderline > useful > scarce strict on means, one-leg below useful, scarce vs one-leg deliberately unordered; the two overlaps that are robust across seeds (useful/scarce 55/60, scarce/one-leg 60/60) asserted in true rank, and the borderline/useful gap asserted UNDER the board-noise sigma. A third, smaller correction of the same class Session 29 made mid-run: demanding prestige-depth monotonicity within every single 20-school seed is a statistical over-assertion (the committed engine fails it half the time); the honest fixture criterion is the mean across seeds, which is cleanly monotone.

**Magnitude, honestly:** the prompt predicted bigs would rise 20–25 rank points; the actual mean rise is **+13.5** (about 1.3 noise sigmas), with the worst-graded athletic-poor bigs rising +25 to +35 and guards/wings moving only on the small FT exclusion (mean +0.2). The access story lands regardless, now as numbers on the page at the fixed seed: **top-prestige-decile mean drafted-big rank 182.3 vs bottom decile 154.0**, and **35 of the 57 blue-chip bigs (three-leg + borderline) on top-quartile-prestige rosters** (38 under the old rank — the count barely moved; what moved is WHERE in the rotation they land and that boards no longer shove every big to the late acquisitions). On the stock page Duke now opens two bigs, and the Session 29 "bigs go late everywhere" observation is resolved.

**The opening-five walk, and its logic visible on the page.** `BuildOpeningFive` is a greedy walk of the acquisition order using the same feasibility shape as the draft's last-slot rule: take the earliest player, skipping one only when taking him would leave too few remaining slots to cover the unmet quota (≥1 B, ≥2 G). Rank-blind by signature — its inputs are the acquisition order and positions, never rank or ratings. Every roster is exactly 4G/3W/3B, so the quota is always satisfiable and the walk cannot strand. When the raw first five already satisfies the quotas, the opening five IS the raw first five (133 of 347 stock rosters at the fixed seed). The fixed-seed page shows the walk working: Duke's fifth starter is its *seventh* acquisition — a guard — because the walk skipped a third big and a wing to seat the second guard; Binghamton skips its fifth acquisition (a guard) to seat the big at six; North Dakota's raw five was already legal and rides untouched. **The accepted residual, ruled and recorded as a known limitation:** a no-wing five is still possible (e.g. 4G/1B small-ball), and benched wings then cannot check in under the fatigue fence's same-position pairing — the smoke sim now prints exactly one warning line per affected side listing its absent positions, so the residual is visible on the page, never silent.

**Phase 54 grew a ninth section and rewrote two assertions; every pre-existing line listed as byte-for-byte stayed byte-for-byte.** New: **FT-blindness** (a generated player's rank at FT=25 vs FT=95, bit-identical `==`); **three full-pipeline per-position rank fixtures** (fixed hand-specified rating dicts for a B, a G, and a W, asserted against oracle constants to 1e-9 — these go through `DivvyScoutRank` itself, closing the trap where the §6 formula fixtures feed leg means directly and would stay green even if the wiring were never done); **post access** (top-prestige-decile mean drafted-BIG rank strictly above bottom decile); and **the seating floor** (≥1 B / ≥2 G on every roster in both worlds, deterministic, equals the raw first five wherever raw already satisfies). Rewritten per the rulings: the group ordering/overlap block (above) and the opening-five contract line. One stale reference caught by the pre-delivery grep: the leak check's detail string still cited the old oracle constant (48); the fair-rank oracle number at the fixed seed is 54, and the harness printed exactly 54.

**Validation — suite green on the machine, page confirmed.** All checks passed on the bare suite; the stock divvy page at the fixed seed matched the oracle to the digit (group means 259.9/218.7/182.7/163.8/164.0; leaks 54), every starred five carried a big and two guards, and bigs appeared in the early acquisitions on elite sheets. The Duke–North Dakota smoke sim ran clean with every reconciliation `[OK]` and no absent-position warning (both fives carried a wing). Honest verdict as delivered: reasoned + oracle re-proven across 260 seeds under the ruled criteria, then harness-confirmed on Emmett's machine.

**Two new deferrals, named this session:** **versatility / multi-position players** (a second seatable position, cross-position fence pairing, coverage counting either quota, coach valuation — home: player-generation pass 2 plus the lineup/coaching layer) and **the FT-hitch archetype** (the rare broken-stroke skilled player shooting in the 40s — texture, judged after seasons produce FT volume). Both of Emmett's rulings on the revealed truths also pre-name coach-layer work: per-coach board preferences (size-lovers, etc.) are where "which of two even prospects do YOU rank higher" eventually lives.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Divvy.cs` — EDIT (`DivvyScoutRank` fair grading; `BuildOpeningFive` floor walk with the new positions parameter; both callers updated; the smoke sim's one-line-per-side absent-position warning; the rank comment block refreshed). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.Divvy.cs` — EDIT (the ordering/overlap block rewritten per the rulings; the opening-five contract line rewritten; section 9 added; the stale leak constant fixed). **No engine change, no Gen change, no config change.** Docs after the green run.

**Next:** unchanged from Session 29 — **Pass 2 of the arc, the minimal season loop on divvied rosters** (placeholder scheduling, real engine games at population scale, standings and the prestige-vs-wins proof). Calibration stays deferred until that loop produces a living population. The next-session prompt is its own audited pass.

## Session 29 — Roster Genesis Pass 1.5: the national pool and the prestige-weighted divvy — prestige becomes access (2026-07-02)

**Scope:** A new pass **inserted into the world-structure arc** ahead of the season loop (governing record: `docs/roster-genesis-brief.md`, settled in design conversation immediately after Session 28 shipped): every school in a world file gets a ten-man roster drawn from **one national talent pool** (10 × school count) by **prestige-weighted selection** — not from per-team generation off a prestige number. The pool's shape is the one authored distribution (the leg-count mix, the **third-leg gradient** inside the two-leg population, exact positional quotas); prestige stops generating quality and becomes what it actually is: **access to talent**. Harness-only — nothing under `src/Charm.Engine/` changed, every pre-existing suite block ran unchanged — and the Session 26 machinery (GenRatings, floors, leg-health enforcement, GenMapToPlayer, Player.Validate) is reused verbatim; the `gen` lab mode and its prestige curve survive untouched as an instrument. **Ordering is the point:** this had to exist before the Pass 3 dynamics are tuned, or the forces would have been calibrated against per-team-generated rosters and the pool swapped in later — the moving-target mistake this project's standing principle exists to prevent.

**The check-in gate ran in full; three rulings were Emmett's, locked before any code.** All seven of the prompt's load-bearing assumptions were verified against pulled source (prestige touches quality only via GenLegCountFor inside GenRoster, so the pool path bypassing GenRoster leaves the old curve intact; SKILL is never a third leg because every position's leg priority puts it in the top two; the ordinary band and per-position size bands as claimed; the big athleticism downshift applied after the draw in both branches; the stock world carries exactly two prestige-0 schools, kept strictly positive in the odds by the +10 base; WorldRng exists; the Divvy symbol space was clean). The rulings: **(1) the pool path's leg-health floor drops to 20** — the scarce gradient band ships as drawn; a leg can be bad, never broken — while the `gen` mode keeps its original 40 via a default parameter, the only Gen edit of the session. **(2) The opening five is the first five players acquired, no shape rule** — the seating requirements read from the current runner and honored as found are "five players with positions," nothing more; the game molding a team toward a well-rounded five *is* the design. **(3) The middle class was thickened at the gate:** the prompt's 24% two-leg became **32%** (one-leg 67.2%, three-leg 0.8% unchanged) — roughly 3.2 multi-leg players per roster on average at n=347 instead of 2.4 — with the gradient fractions riding unchanged (15% borderline / 35% useful / 50% scarce).

**The model, as built.** The pool: positions fixed by pool id (4n guards, 3n wings, 3n bigs — global coverage feasible by construction, still validated loudly before pick one); leg tiers from **hierarchical largest-remainder apportionment** (top-level mix over the pool, gradient tiers over the *realized* two-leg count, canonical-order ties — at n=347: 28/1110/2332, gradient 167/388/555; at n=20: 2/64/134 and 10/22/32, both oracle constants Phase 54 asserts); roles with quota heads (the first ⌈1.2n⌉ guards forced into lead-handler roles, the first ⌈1.2n⌉ wings forced ThreeAndDWing — coverage supply guaranteed with 20% headroom). Two-leg players get the pass's namesake: the **third-leg gradient** — the ordinary stamp on the missing leg is redrawn from the tier's band (borderline 56–70 / useful 46–55 / scarce 34–45 on the generic scale), mapped through the position's size scaling where the third leg is SIZE (with the free throw recomputed, since Height changed) and downshifted after the draw for a big's ATH. The **scout rank** — the quarantined exception to the no-scalar wall — is `L1 + 0.9·L2 + 0.4·L3 + 0.045·max(0, L3−30)²` over the three leg means (holes excluded, SIZE normalized by a single per-position affine map anchored ordinary-lo→44, plus-hi→88), sorted descending: monotone in every feeding rating, **convex in the third leg** (per-point deltas 1.255 → 2.245 → 3.37 across the bands — every ounce of the third leg worth more the more you have), ordered on average with real overlap (group means 251 > 212 > 178 > 162 > 160, adjacent groups overlapping). It lives on the pool row only — never on a Player, never printed as an overall, never sorting anything outside the draft board. The **divvy**: each pick won by weight `(currentPrestige + 10)^2` — the exponent is **the constitutional dial** (too steep collapses the pool back into an authored curve; the payoff is a blue blood getting more *cracks* while occasionally losing one), placeholder until burn-in like every number in this pass. Each school sees the board through **stable noise**: a per-(school, player) perturbation (sd 8% of the pool's rank range, triangular like the world seeder's jitter — no transcendentals, so the oracle mirrors it bit-for-bit) drawn from a fresh SplitMix64 seeded by mixing (divvySeed, schoolId, poolPlayerId) — a coherent *alternate scouting board*, order-free by construction, never a per-pick reroll. **Coverage is a hard constraint with two layers:** the per-school last-slot rule (an unmet coverage role keeps a slot of its position free — a school never burns its final guard slot on a non-lead while it lacks a lead) and the **global protected-supply rule** (taking a protected-role player you don't need is illegal whenever remaining supply equals remaining unmet obligations — the greedy grab that would strand another school is blocked by legality, not penalized by a score). A school with no legal candidate is skipped by the winner draw; ties on the board break to the lowest pool id.

**Oracle-first, and the oracle was the hard gate: 260 seeded drafts green before a line of C#.** The Python oracle mirrors the whole thing constant-for-constant — SplitMix64, the apportionment, the rating draws, the redraw, the rank, the noise derivation, the odds, the full draft with both legality layers — under a **fixed RNG-consumption contract** that is the reproducibility spec (sequential stream: Phase A tier shuffle, Phase B one role draw per player in id order, Phase C ratings per player in id order, Phase D one winner draw per pick; the noise on its own per-pair streams). Acceptance across 200 fixture seeds (n=20) and 60 stock seeds (n=347): **zero stalls, zero stranded rosters**, every roster full/legal/covered, protected-supply slack never negative, expected multi-leg per roster **monotone in prestige with overlap** at both scales, and the leak alive in 198/200 and 60/60 seeds (the small-n misses are honest randomness — the fixture is proven explicitly, never assumed to be a miniature stock world). An adversarial rigged-board test proved the protection: a high-prestige school coveting both lead guards at zero headroom is blocked from the second by legality, and both schools finish covered. One acceptance criterion was corrected mid-run — demanding a leak in literally 200/200 fixture seeds was a statistical over-assertion at n=20, relaxed to a stable-rate threshold with the fixed-seed leak pinned for Phase 54 instead.

**Phase 54 — eight check groups, all green on the machine.** Determinism (same seed twice → identical draft at both scales; different seed differs); the noise's exported triples asserted to 1e-15 plus read-order independence; every roster legal at both n (ten each, drafted once, 4/3/3, lead + wing defender covered, Player.Validate green); the pool's generated shape equal to the apportionment constants; a **rigged pool rejected loudly** naming the positional shortfall and the role quota before pick one (never a stranded team at pick 3,400); the rank fixtures to 1e-9 with convexity, the 20-player monotonicity spot check, and stock-pool group ordering with overlap; access sanity on the fixed seed (top-prestige-decile mean drafted rank above bottom-decile, at least one leak — chosen to be robust even if the C# stream ever diverged from the oracle's, since at stock scale essentially every seed leaks); and the protected-supply slack asserted non-negative across both worlds plus five extra fixture seeds, with the opening five pinned deterministic and rank-blind. **The stock world for the suite comes from `ConvertWorld` on the csvs already beside the binary** — the Phase 53 path — which subtracted a planned csproj edit from the session entirely.

**Validation on the machine — the suite green with every pre-existing block unchanged, and the page reads right.** The stock divvy (seed 20260702): pool generated exactly to target on every line; picks by prestige band cleanly ordered in access (80–99 mean pick 694, 0–19 mean 2918); **48 top-decile players below median prestige** — the Gonzaga mechanism alive without anyone authoring it; and the Session 26 depth-gap headline now *emerging* from access — Duke (98) carrying eight multi-leg players deep into the rotation, North Dakota (0) one-leg on all ten, Boston University (43) in between with exactly the "a couple of real players and a supporting cast" middle-class texture the thickened mix was chosen for. Variance and overlap, the recorded Pass 3 assumption, observed early: band means 1.56 / 2.33 / 3.32 / 4.58 / 5.81 multi-leg per roster with spreads wide enough that every adjacent band overlaps (a 0–19 school reached 5 while a 60–79 school drew 0).

**Two emergent observations, recorded for basketball judgment, not acted on.** **(1) Bigs go late everywhere:** the athleticism downshift tilts the rank slightly perimeter, so boards lean guard/wing and every sample sheet shows bigs at the bottom acquisitions — arguably scouting-realistic, Emmett's call later whether it's a feature or needs a thumb on the scale. **(2) Some elite opening fives have no big** (Duke's is 3G/2W): first-five-acquired plus perimeter-tilted boards means a team can open without an interior body, and since the fatigue fence subs strictly within position, benched bigs never check into a smoke sim for such a team. Honored as found this session; **deferred item:** opening-five shape / lineup logic belongs to a future lineup-or-coaching layer, not to the divvy.

**Engineering calls, flagged not slipped.** (1) **`SplitMixRandom`** — a `System.Random` subclass backed by `WorldRng` (every overload consumes exactly one double as `min + (int)(u·(max−min))`) so `GenRatings` is reused byte-for-byte while the pool stays reproducible on any runtime; the adapter is the named seam of assumption 1. (2) The **single affine size↔generic map per position** (slope 44/24 both directions) — used forward to place a SIZE third leg's band and inverse to feed the rank; the plus-band tops and ordinary-band bottoms align exactly across positions, and the mild mid-band distortion is acceptable in a rank that is *designed* to be only roughly right. (3) The rank formula's exact weights are engineering (Claude's lane per the brief), shown at the gate and pinned by oracle constants rather than slipped. (4) The third leg is derived **from the plus set directly**, never by a second `GenLegPriority` call — the drafted version of that line would have consumed an extra wing draw and silently diverged from the oracle's consumption contract; caught in the pre-delivery re-read. (5) What a green Phase 54 does **not** prove, stated plainly: bit-level equality between the Python pool and the C# pool is not asserted (formula-level constants and every invariant are), and none of the magnitudes are basketball truth — the mix, the gradient fractions, the odds exponent, and the noise sigma all ship placeholder, tuned at burn-in against pool-built populations.

**What shipped:** `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Divvy.cs` — NEW (the whole divvy layer: constants, the adapter, apportionment, the pool with the gradient redraw, the rank, the noise, the preflight validator, the draft with both legality layers, the opening five, the four-part readout, the smoke sim, the `divvy` CLI). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Checks.Divvy.cs` — NEW (Phase 54). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.cs` — EDIT (the `divvy` dispatch returning before the suite; the Phase 54 registration). `src/Charm.Harness/Program.Gen.cs` — EDIT (GenEnforceLegHealth's optional floor parameter, default preserving every existing call site). **No engine change; no csproj change.** Rosters are deliberately **not persisted** — deterministic from world + seed, regenerated by the season pass.

**Next:** **Pass 2 of the arc — the minimal season loop, now running on divvied rosters** (placeholder scheduling, real engine games at population scale, standings and the prestige-vs-wins proof), per the amended arc map. Calibration stays deferred until that loop produces a living population. The next-session prompt is its own audited pass.

## Session 28 — World Structure Pass 1: the static skeleton — the world file, the pyramid seeder, and the proof on the page (2026-07-02)

**Scope:** The first pass of the **world-structure arc** (governing record: `docs/world-structure-brief.md`): the **era-file schema**, the **stock D1 world** converted from the two reference csvs (347 real schools, 32 conferences), the **count-agnostic pyramid seeder**, the **world-integrity validator**, and the **distribution readout** — the pyramid on the page. A **BUILD, and harness-only:** no rosters generated, no games run, nothing under `src/Charm.Engine/` touched, so the engine is byte-for-byte what it was after Session 27 and every pre-existing suite block ran unchanged. The session had an unusual shape, run correctly end to end: the build prompt was drafted per CONVENTIONS §6 (reflection gate, full source audit, adversarial preamble), went out to ChatGPT, and came back with **four genuine catches — all accepted, none pushed back** (a per-school division marker the schema had claimed but not serialized; an explicit contract that the seeder reseeds *historical* prestige too; the literally-impossible "suite byte-for-byte unchanged" wording sharpened to "all pre-existing blocks unchanged"; and quote-aware csv parsing required by name). Emmett then chose to build in the same session; the check-in gate still ran in full — all required reads completed, findings reported, explicit go received before the first file existed.

**The check-in had already defused the data traps before any code.** Three things in the reference csvs would have bitten a naive build. **(1) `teams.csv`'s `Division` column is not the NCAA division** — all 347 schools are D1; that column marks East/West splits *inside* conferences (verified against the split conferences in `conf.csv`). It is dropped; every school is stamped `division: "D1"` (the per-school marker the brief requires from day one). **(2) `conf.csv` carries a 1–5 conference rating that maps cleanly onto the four authored tiers** — 5 → `power`, 4 → `highMid`, 3 → `lowMid`, 1–2 → `low` — and the authored data proves the placeholder floors (40 / 20 / 8 / 0): per-tier prestige minimums in the csv are exactly 45 / 21 / 8 / 0, so the stock file clears every floor with the tightest case sitting right on the line (lowMid min 8 on a floor of 8). "Independent" (14 schools) rides as an ordinary low-tier conference row, no special casing. **(3) The world's prestige scale is 0–99 but the roster generator's floor is 1** (two csv schools sit at 0) — recorded as a boundary rule, not a code change: any future pass that feeds a school's prestige to generation treats 0 as 1 at that seam; nothing in Pass 1 exercises it. Emmett's calls, locked at check-in: the stock file keeps the game's authored prestige **loaded as written** (the seeder is tooling, never a load-time mutation — the readout *reports* an authored file's deviation from the pyramid, it never corrects it); **historical prestige = current prestige everywhere** this pass; seeder conference-awareness is rough, not fancy.

**The schema — the arc's first persistent schema, designed as one.** A single JSON era file with `schemaVersion: 1` from day one (the save-format discipline starts here, per the standing note). `metadata` carries `kind` (`authored`/`generated`), `eraLabel`, `division`, and `worldSeed` — present **iff** generated, the reproducibility contract. `tiers` is exactly the four canonical objects; the **floor** is the load-bearing number this pass, while `equilibrium` and `pullbackIntensity` are carried as schema now (placeholders, consumed by the Pass 3 dynamics) so Pass 3 needs no schema migration. `conferences` are id / name / shortName / tierId; `schools` are id (internal, opaque — the dynamics never read a name) / name / abbr / city / state / color / lat / long / conferenceId / **per-school division** / currentPrestige / historicalPrestige, both prestige values 0–99. The reader is the **bench-reader standard**: a strict tree-walk that refuses unknown keys, duplicate keys, wrong types, and out-of-range values at every level, naming the exact school/conference/field — reusing the bench's own helpers. The writer is **deterministic on purpose**: canonical tier order, conferences and schools by id, fixed property order, `\n` newlines, invariant numeric formatting — same inputs, byte-identical file.

**The seeder — oracle-first, floors honored by construction, reproducible on any runtime.** Before a line of C#, a **Python oracle** (24 checks, all green) proved the full algorithm: **largest-remainder apportionment** over the brief's band proportions (exact at n=7, 20, 347, 1000, 1600), the **feasibility formula**, and the assignment. The C# mirrors it **bit-for-bit**, starting with the PRNG: an explicit **SplitMix64** (`WorldRng`), not `System.Random`, so a shared world file reproduces identically on any future .NET runtime — with a **fixed consumption order** as the contract (7 tie-break doubles, two jitter doubles per school in ascending id order, one double per band slot top-down). Assignment: each school gets a **station** = its tier's equilibrium + triangular jitter (±30) — roughly tier-ordered with real overlap — then band values are sorted ascending and each goes to the unassigned school with the **lowest station whose conference floor permits it**. Floors are therefore honored **by the construction of the assignment, never by a post-hoc clamp** that would silently distort the band counts; a value no school can take throws loudly (it means the validator missed an infeasibility). The seeder generates a **new** file from an existing file's structure — incoming prestige ignored entirely, seeded `historicalPrestige` set equal to seeded current, `kind: "generated"`, the seed stamped.

**The validator — runs on every load, and the special check is the one that matters.** Ordinary schema checks (unique ids, real conference/tier references, exactly the four tiers, bounds, floor ≤ equilibrium, seed iff generated, division match) plus **member-below-floor** (an authored file with a school under its conference's floor fails, naming school, value, conference, floor) plus the brief's rule-6 check: **the target pyramid and the floors must be simultaneously satisfiable** — cumulative, per distinct floor descending: schools whose floor forces them to prestige F+ must not exceed the pyramid slots in bands reaching F+. An infeasible file fails naming the binding conflict (which floor, how many forced, how many slots) — never a silent floor weakening or a distorted pyramid.

**Phase 53 — the committed proof, in the suite.** Seven check groups, all green on the machine: the converter produces a valid 347-school / 32-conference world from the committed csvs (every school D1, historical == current); the **20-school fixture** loads green (nothing assumes 347); an in-memory **infeasible** world (300 power floors at n=347) is rejected with the named conflict; a member **below floor** is rejected naming the school; the seeder is **deterministic** (same seed → identical assignment, different seed → different assignment) and the seeded world itself validates; **pyramid exactness** at both n=347 and n=20 (band counts equal the apportionment; the canonical n=347 apportionment equals the oracle constant `3/21/31/49/80/73/90`; floors honored; values 0–99; historical == current); and tier means strictly ordered `power > highMid > lowMid > low` at both sizes (means only — overlap is the design, so per-school ordering is deliberately not asserted).

**Validation — green on the machine, and the reports matched the oracle to the decimal.** The full suite ran green with every pre-existing block unchanged (no engine change; Phase 53 is the only added output). Then the two commands: **`world convert`** produced the stock file and a report matching the pre-computed prediction on every row — including the on-message headline: the stock data's deviation from the target pyramid lands **exactly where Emmett thinned it** when deriving the target from this same reference (20–39 band **+9.3** points fat, the <20 base **−10.4** thin; every other band within ±0.7). The report shows it; nothing corrects it — reshaping is later passes' work. **`world seed`** (seed 20260702) hit the target **dead on**: counts 3/21/31/49/80/73/90, tier means 78.9 / 60.4 / 38.8 / 19.5, and the overlap visibly alive on the page (lowMid's max 61 above power's min 54; a real interleave, not neat blocks). Both generated world files are committed alongside the code.

**Three engineering calls, flagged not slipped.** (1) The converter validates its row count against the csv's **own count line** rather than hard-coding 347 — the 347 assert lives in Phase 53 instead, so the tooling itself stays count-agnostic per the standing rule. (2) The explicit **WorldRng** instead of `System.Random` (above) — reproducibility must not depend on a runtime's version-specific algorithm. (3) The **csproj** now copies the two csvs and the fixture beside the binary (the `config.json` convention), so the suite reads them from `AppContext.BaseDirectory` regardless of working directory. **One honest pre-delivery fix:** the report's deviation column initially used an invalid composite format string — caught by the sandbox re-read before delivery, not by a compiler Claude does not have.
